The Spaces tab that carries this door exists only behind house-first, which is OFF on a first TestFlight launch.
confirmed.fix: Give YourHouseRail a 'See all spaces' tail on the flags-off root (or ship round 1 with house-first on). Same one row also un-buries All Items (.crossRoom), which sits behind Your Spaces.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-read DailyRoomView.swift:247-370: the flags-off root mounts HouseRecordCard, TodayNextMoveCard, RoomHeroCard (onOpen -> .roomProject(roomId:)) and YourHouseRail (onCard/onAddRoom only). No block, and no rail tail, routes to .yourSpaces. Confirmed there is no gallery door. Two corrections to the evidence, neither of which changes the verdict: (a) the grep missed a third site, DailyRoomView.swift:538 `coordinator.navigate(to: move.kind == .reviewActiveRoom ? .yourSpaces : ...)` — but that is the guard-failure branch of performRoomMove (:536-545), reached only when the TodayNextMove targetID fails to parse as a UUID, so it is not a door a tester can find; (b) CompanionActionRows.swift:157 does register a .yourSpaces row, so the Companion sheet is a real (if buried) door, as the finding itself allows. Fix sketch is sound and cheap.
confirmed.judgeNote: Facts confirmed, framing over-stated — the door is buried, not absent. CompanionActionRows.swift:142-158 emits a 'Your spaces / N rooms' row (and 'Add your first space' at roomCount 0), CompanionOverlay.swift:669 dispatches its route, and DailyRoomView.swift:538 reaches .yourSpaces via the reviewActiveRoom next-move. The grep in the evidence missed these because the companion routes through an action item, not a literal navigate(to:) call. So a flags-off tester CAN add and reach spaces — via the orb, which is that root's whole navigation model, exactly as Studio and Pieces are. The fix sketch is still right and cheap (a 'See all spaces' tail on YourHouseRail, which also un-buries All Items), hence T1 not cut. The T0 item this really surfaces is a program decision, not code: whether round 1 ships with house-first ON, since flags-off-on-first-launch means every tester's first session is orb-only. Worth putting to Kody explicitly — it changes what half this audit's Spaces findings are even reachable in build 1.

confirmed.title: 'Browse pieces' has no Today door on either root
confirmed.evidence: blocks() emits header, record, nextMove, designerSeat, roomHero|houseRail|startWithARoom, newThisWeek, savedSummary, story, signInLine — no marketplace door. NewThisWeekRail taps go to .pieceDetail, never to the catalogue, and the rail needs >=3 genuinely new rows to draw at all (newThisWeekFloor = 3). Every .emergence(pieceId: nil) door lives on StyleResultView, RoomProjectView, CrossRoomView, a CollectionsView empty state, or the Companion.
confirmed.fix: Add a 'Browse pieces' tail to NewThisWeekRail, or restore a marketplace-links row to HomeComposition.
confirmed.codeNote: Real on the FLAG-OFF root only; two evidence errors. (1) "either root" is wrong — house-first mounts PiecesTabRoot (TabRoot.swift:63-68) and the Pieces tab is on screen while Today is showing. (2) The claim that every `.emergence(pieceId: nil)` door lives on StyleResult/RoomProject/CrossRoom/Collections/Companion is incomplete: DailyRoomView.swift:538, OnboardingFlowHost.swift:112, QuietConversationFlowHost.swift:306, CompanionContextProvider.swift:297/301, AppCoordinator.swift:587/618/638. (3) Today DOES carry a conditional catalogue door the finding missed: TodayNextMove(kind:.exploreActiveRoom) — "Find the first piece for <room>" / "Browse Patina's edit and begin shaping the room." (TodayExperience.swift:169-179) → performRoomMove (DailyRoomView.swift:535-546) → .roomEmergence → RecommendationsView(roomId:). Corrected finding: HomeComposition.blocks (TodayExperience.swift:273-297) emits no PERSISTENT catalogue door, and the one door it can emit requires an active room WITH a taste portrait AND zero items — a first-round tester gets .scanFirstRoom instead (roomMove guard, :149-156), so the catalogue is unreachable from Today after the post-quiz landing until they have scanned and portraited a room. NewThisWeekRail→.pieceDetail and newThisWeekFloor=3 are confirmed as written.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed against HomeComposition.blocks (TodayExperience.swift:273-297) — no marketplace door in the list, and with flags off there is no Pieces tab either. First session survives because StyleResultView carries a door; the SECOND launch is where it bites: the tester lands on Today with no route to the shop but the Companion orb, and newThisWeekFloor=3 means the rail that might have substituted often will not draw against a 15-row catalogue. Core loop broken from home, S effort. Fix in the same pass as A1-04 — one flag-off Today that has doors to both commerce surfaces.

confirmed.title: A guest can save pieces but has no door to Saved except the Companion orb
confirmed.evidence: Today's savedSummary block is gated `if input.isSignedIn, input.savedPieceCount > 0`. SavedDoorRow on Browse draws only `if isTabRoot`, which is true only for the house-first Pieces tab (TabRoot.swift:64). The code still asserts the old world at CompanionActionRows.swift:262: 'the Companion's Saved row is the only route to the Saved screen anywhere in the app.'
confirmed.fix: Drop isSignedIn from the savedSummary gate, or draw SavedDoorRow unconditionally on Browse.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified verbatim. Gate `if input.isSignedIn, input.savedPieceCount > 0` at TodayExperience.swift:292-293; SavedDoorRow drawn `if isTabRoot` at RecommendationsView.swift:115-121; isTabRoot defaults false and is set only by TabRoot.swift:42-47, i.e. only under house-first. CompanionActionRows.swift:258-263 carries the quoted assertion verbatim. Full census of doors to `.table`: DailyRoomView.swift:352 (savedSummary, signed-in), RecommendationsView.swift:117 (tab root), CompanionActionRows.swift:91 and :270, CompanionAreaBuilders.swift:130/136, AppCoordinator.swift:591 (Companion .showTable intent). For a guest on the flag-off root — the exact first-round TestFlight state — every one of those except the Companion is gated off. The guest CAN save: RecommendationsViewModel.saveProduct is not auth-gated and shots/A/17-guest-save.png shows the heart filling.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: TodayExperience.swift:293 gates savedSummary on isSignedIn, SavedDoorRow draws only `if isTabRoot` (RecommendationsView.swift:115) which needs house-first — OFF on a TestFlight first launch. And guest saves DO persist (RecommendationsViewModel.swift:180-189 inserts a TableItemModel with no auth guard). So the guest taps hearts, and the pieces go somewhere they cannot find. 'The app lost the things I saved' is the worst impression in this area and it lands in minute three. Highest-priority of the two door findings — fix this before A1-03 if only one fits.

confirmed.title: DesignerConsultationView shows a hard-coded placeholder 'Matched Designer' card
confirmed.evidence: A gradient circle plus the literal strings 'Matched Designer' / 'Based on your style profile' / "We'll pair you with a designer who understands your aesthetic". Nothing resolves a real designer. This screen is the landing target of the 'Get design help' / 'Work with a designer' empty-state CTA on eight Studio surfaces (Invoices, Projects, Decisions, Documents, Threads, Proposals, Budget, Notifications).
confirmed.fix: Replace the card with the flow's own value proposition, or delete it and let the screen be the hero + 'Start a request'.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed verbatim. DesignerConsultationView.swift:53-75 (`designerCard`): Circle().fill(PatinaGradients.earth) at 60×60, 'Matched Designer' in h5, MonoLabel 'Based on your style profile', caption "We'll pair you with a designer who understands your aesthetic". Nothing in the file resolves a designer — the view has no view model and no service; its only live wire is `coordinator.presentDesignServices`. The harm is sharper than 'placeholder copy': the card uses avatar grammar (circle + name line + qualifier), so 'Matched Designer' reads as the NAME SLOT of a real person the tester has been assigned, filled with a fake. The eight-surface reach claim checks out — all eight route to `.designerConsultation`: InvoiceListView.swift:122, ProjectListView.swift:225, DecisionListView.swift:149, DocumentListView.swift:99, ThreadListView.swift:248, ProposalListView.swift:117, BudgetView.swift:94, NotificationFeedView.swift:160. It is also the no-request body of DesignRequestStatusView.swift:62, so a round-1 tester reaches it on either predicate branch. Fix as written (delete the card, keep hero + 'Start a request') is right and is S.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed verbatim at DesignerConsultationView.swift:56-74 — a PatinaGradients.earth circle where a face would be, 'Matched Designer' in h5, 'Based on your style profile'. To a homeowner this reads as a person they have been matched with; to a designer's eye it reads as a Figma placeholder shipped by accident. Worse in context: this same view is the fallback body of DesignRequestStatusView when `requests` is empty (see C4-19), so a tester who already filed sees a fake 'Matched Designer' too. The hero copy above it already carries the value proposition; deleting the card loses nothing. T0, S.

confirmed.title: Nine LiDAR-only scan screens are unreachable on a Simulator and on non-LiDAR iPhones
confirmed.evidence: bootstrap() reads RoomCaptureService.isSupported; false -> step .fallback, which goes .fallback -> .conversation -> .reveal -> .floorPlan. ScanThresholdView, ScanWalkView, PauseMenuView, ScanReviewView, HeroPickerSheet, PhotoReorderSheet, CaptionEditorSheet, ScanSavedConfirmationView and SoftLandingView are never entered on such a device.
confirmed.fix: No code fix — a program note. (a) A non-LiDAR tester's whole 'add a room' experience is one typed form, which the visual/copy lanes should judge on its own. (b) No Simulator walk in this audit can cover those nine screens; they must be marked code-read only.
confirmed.codeNote: Factually correct and I traced every transition, but it is a coverage note, not a defect — its own fix says 'No code fix'. Verified: bootstrap() is at :149-159 (finding cites :145-153, ~4 lines off) and sets `step = .fallback` when RoomCaptureService.isSupported is false; the full set of `step = .` assignments is lines 123, 156, 158, 211, 224, 241, 246, 261, 270, 282, 288, 345, and the non-LiDAR chain is fallback(158) -> conversation(211) -> reveal(270) -> floorPlan(282/288). .savedConfirmation is set only at :123 (inside the LiDAR review full-screen cover) and .softLanding only at :224 (from savedConfirmation), so ScanSavedConfirmationView and SoftLandingView are unreachable too — all nine screens confirmed code-read-only. Adjusted because severity major + testerVisible true belong on the defect version of this fact, which is C7-10; keep A1-15 in the coverage record, not the fix backlog.
confirmed.judgeNote: Downgraded from major/testerVisible because this is not a defect — it is a coverage caveat plus a program note, and the finder says so ('No code fix'). Its device-gating half restates C7-10/C9-06. Its unique and genuinely valuable contribution is the audit-hygiene ruling: ScanThresholdView, ScanWalkView, PauseMenuView, ScanReviewView, HeroPickerSheet, PhotoReorderSheet, CaptionEditorSheet, ScanSavedConfirmationView and SoftLandingView are code-read only in this audit and no Simulator walk can cover them. That caveat should be carried into the fix program verbatim and paired with the device scan pass C7-04 demands — nine unexercised screens on the headline feature is the largest blind spot in the rooms-scan area.

confirmed.title: Route .roomSavedItems has no screen door — Companion-only
confirmed.evidence: Whole-tree grep for `.roomSavedItems(roomId:` outside the two dispatchers, CompanionContext and RouteTabTable finds exactly one construction site, inside the Companion's room-area rows. No control on RoomProjectView, YourSpacesView or CollectionsView reaches it. The screen is now real (TableItemModel.roomId IS written since the baseline).
confirmed.fix: Add a row to RoomProjectView's items header: 'N saved in this room ->'.
confirmed.codeNote: Whole-tree grep for `roomSavedItems` returns 21 hits; exactly one CONSTRUCTS the route — CompanionAreaBuilders.swift:164, inside the `.roomProject` area rows ("Saved in this room / Your picks here"). Everything else is a dispatcher case, a name table, or analytics (ContentView.swift:234/272, HouseFirstRoot.swift:175/213, Coordinator.swift:59/137/197, AppCoordinator.swift:334/498, RouteTabTable.swift:40, CompanionContext/Provider/ViewModel, ContextMemoryStore.swift:210, CompanionAPIClient.swift:324). No control on RoomProjectView, YourSpacesView or CollectionsView reaches it. Destination is CollectionsView(roomId:) on both roots as cited.
confirmed.judgeNote: Re-framed from tester-visible to invisible: nothing on RoomProjectView, YourSpacesView or CollectionsView tells the tester a room-scoped Saved screen exists, so they experience an absence, not a dead end — no broken affordance, no error, no route that stops. It is an unreached feature rather than a rough edge. Real value once rooms carry enough saves to be worth filtering, which will not be true in the first week.

confirmed.title: .emergence(pieceId:) non-nil arm is dead code, duplicated in both roots
confirmed.evidence: Grep for `.emergence(` across the app finds only `pieceId: nil` constructions plus the two dispatchers and ContextMemoryStore.swift:215. The `if let pieceId` branch mounts a second ProductDetailView that nothing can reach; .pieceDetail is the live route to a piece.
confirmed.fix: Collapse .emergence to a payload-free case, or delete the branch in both dispatchers.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified on d7287c3f8. Every `.emergence(` construction in Patina/ passes `pieceId: nil` — AppCoordinator 587/618/638, DailyRoomView 538, RouteTabTable 93, QuietConversationFlowHost 306, OnboardingFlowHost 112, RoomProjectView 262, CrossRoomView 206, StyleResultView 51, CollectionsView 161/382, CompanionContextProvider 297/301, CompanionActionRows 120, CompanionAreaBuilders 101/121/206. Non-nil appears only in PatinaTests (RouteTabTableTests 51/147, WidgetLinkRoutingTests 55). DeepLinkHandler and both widget targets (PatinaWidget, PatinaWidgetShared) never build the case at all, so no deep link can reach the non-nil arm either. Add one site to the collapse the finding misses: ContextMemoryStore.swift:215's `guard let pieceID else { return nil }` is dead for the same reason.
confirmed.judgeNote: Fact stands; severity should be polish, not minor. The audit's minor means "a tester notices on a second look" — no tester will ever reach an unreachable arm, and .pieceDetail already serves the live path, so there is no behavioural surface at all. Its only real cost is the double-apply tax (it is one of the branches A1-10 makes you edit twice), which is why it should be collapsed during A1-10's extraction rather than as its own ticket. T2, ride-along.

confirmed.title: A whole navigation-intent layer has no call sites (handleIntent / IntentDetector / startRoomScanFlow)
confirmed.evidence: handleIntent is called only by handleIntentWithResponse, which nothing calls. IntentDetector is referenced only from that dead pair. startRoomScanFlow and resetToThreshold have no callers.
confirmed.fix: Delete it, or wire the Companion chat rail it was written for. Worth doing early: it makes route-door greps lie — .yourSpaces and .table look like they have coordinator doors (see A1-02, A1-04) when they do not.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. handleIntent's only caller is handleIntentWithResponse (AppCoordinator:664), which no app code calls; IntentDetector is referenced only at :667 plus its own file; startRoomScanFlow (:679) has no caller; resetToThreshold (:691) is called only from inside handleIntent (:603). One correction to the fix, not the finding: PatinaTests/CompanionBarSlotTests.swift:154,158 DOES call handleIntent, and :147-148 asserts the coordinator source text still contains `func handleIntent(` and `func handleIntentWithResponse(` — so a straight delete reddens that suite. The route-door warning is right and worth carrying: `.yourSpaces` (:599) and `.table` (:595) get their only coordinator `navigate(to:)` from this dead switch.
confirmed.judgeNote: Zero tester impact, and I would normally park dead code at T2 — but this one earns T1 for a reason the finder already names correctly: it makes route-door greps lie, so A1-02 and A1-04 read as having coordinator doors they do not have. The fix program will be doing nav work in week 1; leaving a decoy intent layer in place means diagnosis on those two findings restarts from a false premise. Delete it FIRST in the nav lane, before any nav fix is written. S effort, no risk — nothing calls it.

confirmed.title: The full navigation-destination dispatcher is duplicated verbatim across the two roots
confirmed.evidence: HouseFirstRoot.swift:163-168 says so itself: 'A verbatim second copy of ContentView's dispatcher... This copy dies with the flag-off root, one release from now.' Both are ~180 lines and exhaustive over AppRoute.
confirmed.fix: For the fix program: every navigation-shaped change must be applied twice until the flag-off root is retired, and only the flag-off copy is what a round-1 tester sees. Consider extracting the dispatcher now.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. HouseFirstRoot.swift:162-168 carries the self-describing comment verbatim ('A verbatim second copy of ContentView's dispatcher… This copy dies with the flag-off root, one release from now'). ContentView.swift is 433 lines with the dispatcher at 228-425; HouseFirstRoot.swift is 356 lines with its copy at 172-355; both are exhaustive with no `default:` at the top level. Not a defect so much as a program rule, and the rule is correct: with every flag OFF on a first TestFlight launch, ContentView's copy is the only one a round-1 tester ever renders.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not tester-visible directly, but it carries the sharpest indirect tester risk in this batch, and the program rule matters more than the extraction. THE RULE (adopt at T0, costs nothing): with flags off, ContentView's copy is the only dispatcher a round-1 tester reaches — a nav fix written and verified in HouseFirstRoot ships literally nothing to build 1. Every nav-shaped fix needs both copies touched and the flags-OFF root screenshotted as the acceptance evidence. THE EXTRACTION (T1): pay the M once before the nav lane starts rather than double-applying every fix through the first week; doing it mid-lane is where the half-applied fix gets born. W3 duplicated deliberately and that reasoning has expired now that both roots are being edited.

confirmed.title: Notifications lands on a different tab depending on how it was opened
confirmed.evidence: RouteTabTable assigns .notifications to the Studio tab, which is what an APNs tap or a restore uses. But an in-app navigate() pushes onto the tab already on screen, and the Today bell (DailyRoomView.swift:257) calls navigate(to: .notifications) — so the same screen lands on Today from the bell and on Studio from a push, with two different Back destinations.
confirmed.fix: Either route the bell through openExternal, or accept and document it. Only bites once house-first is on.
confirmed.codeNote: Behaviour is real but it is the DESIGNED behaviour, spelled out in three separate comment blocks — RouteTabTable.swift:9-13 ('deliberately NOT consulted for an in-app push: tapping a row pushes onto the tab you are already on, so Back returns you where you were'), AppCoordinator.navigate:319-323, TabNavigationModel.push:54-57. Both entries give a coherent Back (bell→Today, push→Studio root); neither dead-ends. Not a defect, and a tester would have to compare an APNs entry against a bell entry in the same session to notice. Downgrade to polish / testerVisible false / cut.
confirmed.judgeNote: Flipping testerVisible to false for round 1, as the finder half-anticipated ('only bites once house-first is on'). With flags off, the home bell is the sole entry point and C2-05 means there is no APNs-tap path at all, so the two Back destinations cannot both exist. The underlying inconsistency is real and worth resolving before house-first goes on for anyone — a screen whose Back button goes somewhere different depending on how you arrived is the sort of thing that erodes confidence without a tester ever being able to name it. Batch with C2-11 into the house-first enablement work, and route the bell through openExternal rather than documenting the divergence.

confirmed.title: navigate(to: .designerConsultation) is silently rewritten to a different destination
confirmed.evidence: The route is intercepted at the top of navigate(to:) and rewritten to .designRequests(focusLeadId:) whenever DesignHelpDestination.current is not .newRequest. Eight Studio empty states are labelled 'Get design help' / 'Work with a designer' and open the request-status screen instead for a client who already filed one.
confirmed.fix: Correct behaviour (SP-07), wrong label — have the empty states read the same DesignHelpDestination and print 'See your design request' when that is where they go.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism real, blast radius REFUTED, and the proposed fix has already shipped. The rewrite exists as described (AppCoordinator.swift:294-304, and again in openExternal at :366-377) and is deliberate SP-07. But the evidence — 'Eight Studio empty states are labelled "Get design help" … and open the request-status screen instead for a client who already filed one' — is wrong for all eight. Every one of them already reads the request state and already prints the conditional label: `DesignRequestStatusService.shared.promotedRequest != nil ? "Track your request" : "Get design help"` at InvoiceListView.swift:115, ProjectListView.swift:218, DecisionListView.swift:142, DocumentListView.swift:92, ThreadListView.swift:241, ProposalListView.swift:110, BudgetView.swift:87, NotificationFeedView.swift:139 — and in that branch their own action (e.g. InvoiceListView.swift:119-124) routes straight to `.designRequests`, never touching the rewrite. That IS the fix as written, shipped under SP-08. RESIDUAL (narrow, real): the label predicate is `promotedRequest` while the route predicate is `DesignHelpDestination.current` (built from EngagementTier + `openRequest`, DesignHelpDestination.swift:36-55), and DesignRequestStatusService documents these as deliberately different (:438-448). A client who dismisses the home card this session makes promotedRequest nil while openRequest stands, so the label flips back to 'Get design help' while the tap still lands on the existing request. Reachable only after filing AND dismissing — not a round-1 tester path. Severity minor → polish, testerVisible → false; cut unless the label/route predicates are unified anyway.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed at AppCoordinator.swift:293-304 (and the same guard at presentDesignServices, :408-417). The behaviour is right and deliberate (SP-07 exists precisely to stop duplicate leads); only the label is wrong. Low reach in round 1 — it fires only for a tester who already has an open request, so most first-week testers never see it, and those who do land somewhere useful rather than nowhere. T2: the empty states should read the same DesignHelpDestination and print 'See your design request', but that is a week-two refinement, not a build-1 gate. Bundle it with the C4-19 fix, which touches the same resolver.

confirmed.title: Two orphan views still compile with no mount (AddedToRoomToast, DesignRequestResumeBanner)
confirmed.evidence: Whole-tree grep across the app target (excluding each view's own #Preview) finds no call site, and neither PatinaTests nor PatinaUITests references them. DesignRequestResumeBanner even carries accessibilityIdentifier("DailyRoomView.DesignRequestResumeBanner") for a screen that does not mount it.
confirmed.fix: Delete both, or mount AddedToRoomToast on the add-to-room success path — the 'added to {room}' confirmation currently has no UI.
confirmed.codeNote: Orphan claim confirmed: AddedToRoomToast and DesignRequestResumeBanner have no call site in Patina/, PatinaTests/ or PatinaUITests/ outside their own #Preview, and DesignRequestResumeBanner.swift:65 does carry accessibilityIdentifier("DailyRoomView.DesignRequestResumeBanner") for a screen that never mounts it. The FIX SKETCH is wrong and should not be carried: the live 'Add to room' path already renders its outcome — RecommendationsView.swift:96-108 shows `addToRoomMessage` including the honest not-yet-synced failure. What is actually dead beside the toast is DailyRoomViewModel's entire picker path: `presentingAddFor` (:71, written :508/:512) and `toastMessage` (:72, written :523, cleared :530) have no view reader, so `addToRoom` cannot be reached from any screen. Delete the toast and that state; do not mount it.
confirmed.judgeNote: The dead views are confirmed, but the fix sketch's impact claim over-states: the add-to-room success path is not silent today. ProductDetailViewModel.addToRoom sets isSaved = true and fires HapticManager.shared.notification(.success) (lines 78-81), so a tester gets a state flip plus a success haptic. What is genuinely missing is naming the room the piece went to and offering a path to it — a polish opportunity, not an absent confirmation, and a product call rather than a defect. Handle it as: delete both orphans at T2; if anyone wants the toast, raise it as a fresh product item so it is not smuggled in as a bug fix. Worth keeping from this entry: DesignRequestResumeBanner ships accessibilityIdentifier("DailyRoomView.DesignRequestResumeBanner") for a screen that never mounts it — a UI test asserting on that id would pass or fail for the wrong reason.

confirmed.title: AppCoordinator.hasExistingRooms() is a self-described placeholder
confirmed.evidence: `/// Check if user has existing rooms (placeholder - would query SwiftData)` returning `settings.roomCount > 0`. No caller today, but it is the kind of stub a later reader will trust.
confirmed.fix: Delete it, or point it at RoomStore.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified verbatim at AppCoordinator.swift:282-286, comment and body as quoted. Grep across Patina/, PatinaTests/ and PatinaUITests/ returns the declaration line only. Swift emits no unused-symbol warning for a private func, so it ships silently until someone deletes it — the finding's 'a later reader will trust it' concern is the whole value here.
confirmed.judgeNote: no V2 verdict

confirmed.title: Load-bearing comment is now false: 'the Companion's Saved row is the only route to Saved'
confirmed.evidence: The SP-12 comment states the Companion row is the only route to the Saved screen anywhere in the app. SavedSummaryRow (Today, DailyRoomView.swift:348) and SavedDoorRow (Pieces tab, RecommendationsView.swift:116) both exist now — though both are gated (see A1-04), which is probably why the comment survived.
confirmed.fix: Update the comment when A1-04 is fixed.
confirmed.codeNote: The SP-12 comment at CompanionActionRows.swift:258-262 does claim the Companion row 'is the only route to the Saved screen anywhere in the app', and two other routes now exist: DailyRoomView.swift:348 mounts SavedSummaryRow (RoomHeroCard.swift:224) and RecommendationsView.swift:116 mounts SavedDoorRow (SavedDoorRow.swift:24). A load-bearing comment that would talk a future editor out of the right change.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correct and not tester-visible — a stale load-bearing comment. Not its own task: it is a rider on the A1-04 gating fix, and the finding itself says so ('Update the comment when A1-04 is fixed'). Track it as an acceptance-criterion line on A1-04 rather than a backlog row, otherwise it will outlive the fix it describes. T2.

confirmed.title: CFBundleVersion 1 is BELOW the build already on App Store Connect — next upload is rejected
confirmed.where: apps/mobile/Patina/Patina.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 1 in all 8 target configs, e.g. :489, :519, :698, :750) + ASC app 6762007888
confirmed.evidence: `asc testflight pre-release list --app 6762007888` → preReleaseVersions [{"version":"1.0","platform":"IOS"}]. `asc builds list --app 6762007888 --paginate` → exactly one build, version "2", uploaded 2026-05-12, processingState VALID, expired true (2026-08-10), minOsVersion 17.6. The project as it stands produces 1.0 (1) — lower than the 1.0 (2) already on the train.
confirmed.fix: Bump CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION to 3 in BOTH the Patina and PatinaWidget configs (they must stay identical or the widget trips ITMS-90473), then adopt a monotonic scheme — a single Config/Version.xcconfig holding MARKETING_VERSION + CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION, bumped by the archive script. Keep MARKETING_VERSION 1.0.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-verified live: `asc builds list --app 6762007888 --paginate` returns exactly one build, version "2", uploaded 2026-05-12, processingState VALID, expired true (2026-08-10), minOsVersion 17.6, usesNonExemptEncryption false, under preReleaseVersion 1.0/IOS. pbxproj has CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 1 in all 8 configs and MARKETING_VERSION = 1.0 everywhere, so the next archive is 1.0 (1) — below 1.0 (2). Expiry does not free the number. Line-number correction for the fix program: CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION lives at pbxproj:489 (widget Release), :521 (widget Debug), :677 (Patina Debug), :725 (Patina Release), plus :769/:791/:812/:832 on the test targets — the cited :519/:698/:750 are a few lines off. App and widget currently agree (1.0/1), so the ITMS-90473 pairing note in the fix is a constraint to preserve, not a present defect.
confirmed.judgeNote: Trivially true and trivially fatal: 1.0 (1) < the 1.0 (2) already on the train, so the upload bounces before anyone sees it. Bundle the fix with the other pbxproj T0 edits (A2-03, A2-13) so the project is touched once. The monotonic-scheme half (Version.xcconfig) is the part that stops this recurring at build 2 — keep it, do not defer it.

confirmed.title: No PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy while the app uses required-reason APIs — ITMS-91053 at processing
confirmed.evidence: `find apps/mobile/Patina -name '*.xcprivacy'` → nothing. The built .app carries only vendored manifests (PostHog_PostHog.bundle, PLCrashReporter_CrashReporter.bundle, swift-crypto_Crypto.bundle). Required-reason APIs in first-party code: UserDefaults ×117 (incl. UserDefaults(suiteName:) at FeatureFlags.swift:210, LastSeenStore.swift:53, RecordOwner.swift:42) → CA92.1; ScanDiskBudget.swift:211-212 `.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey` → DiskSpace; FileManager.attributesOfItem at TarArchive.swift:57 and ScanBundleWriter.swift:150,187,382 → FileTimestamp. supabase-swift 2.40.0's checkout ships NO PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, so its statically-linked usage rolls into the app's missing manifest.
confirmed.fix: Add Patina/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy: NSPrivacyTracking=false, empty NSPrivacyTrackingDomains, NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes (email / user ID / photos / product interaction, Linked, non-Tracking), NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes = UserDefaults CA92.1, DiskSpace E174.1, FileTimestamp C617.1. The widget needs its own (it reads the App Group defaults).
confirmed.codeNote: Every factual claim reproduced exactly: `find apps/mobile -name '*.xcprivacy'` returns only Capture's and vendored dependency manifests, nothing under apps/mobile/Patina; 117 UserDefaults hits in Patina/; UserDefaults(suiteName:) at FeatureFlags.swift:210, LastSeenStore.swift:53, RecordOwner.swift:42; ScanDiskBudget.swift:211-212 .volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey; attributesOfItem at TarArchive.swift:57 and ScanBundleWriter.swift:150,187,382; and the supabase-swift 2.40.0 checkout genuinely ships no .xcprivacy. ADJUSTED ON SEVERITY ONLY: 'ITMS-91053 at processing' is not established. Apple's required-reason rule surfaces as an upload-time notice and blocks App Store acceptance; it is not shown to fail build processing or Beta App Review, and no upload has ever been attempted here (A2-07/G-01). Must-fix before submission and worth doing before round one, but it is not proven to stop a TestFlight build reaching testers.
confirmed.judgeNote: Tier unchanged, confidence in the mechanism lowered. Apple's hard rejections here have centred on third-party SDK signatures; first-party required-reason usage has more often arrived as a post-processing ITMS-91053 email than a wall — so blocker→major. It stays T0 anyway: the fix is one file, it is mandatory before any App Store submission, and the downside of being wrong is a lost upload cycle at exactly the moment Kody has testers waiting. Sequencing note for the plan: do not block the FIRST upload attempt on getting the manifest perfect — write it, upload, and let processing tell you.

confirmed.title: iPad idiom + portrait-only + no UIRequiresFullScreen — iPad multitasking validation error on upload
confirmed.where: project.pbxproj TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2" (both targets, all configs) + INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations = UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait
confirmed.evidence: Merged as-built Info.plist from the Debug product: UIDeviceFamily [1,2], UISupportedInterfaceOrientations [UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait]. `grep -rn UIRequiresFullScreen apps/mobile/Patina` → no hits anywhere. This is the classic ITMS-90474 shape; the iOS 26 SDK's always-resizable iPad model makes the all-orientations requirement stricter, not looser.
confirmed.fix: Set TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1 on Patina and PatinaWidget. Honest for a round-1 iPhone 17 Pro audience and removes the whole class of iPad validation and iPad-layout debt.
confirmed.codeNote: Config facts confirmed (built plist: UIDeviceFamily [1,2], UISupportedInterfaceOrientations [UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait]; grep for UIRequiresFullScreen across apps/mobile/Patina returns nothing, and it is absent from the as-built plist too). ADJUSTED: the blocker framing — 'iPad multitasking validation error on upload', ITMS-90474 — is unsupported. No archive, export or validate has ever completed for this app (A2-07, G-01), the finding's own reasoning that 'the iOS 26 SDK's always-resizable iPad model makes the requirement stricter' is stated as inference rather than evidence, and the app that IS on ASC was uploaded under an older project state. Same root cause and same one-line fix as C9-01 — fold it in there and let the A2-07 dry run say whether validation actually complains. Severity blocker → major on the C9-01 (undesigned iPad layout) ground, not the upload ground.
confirmed.judgeNote: Right call, wrong load-bearing argument, and testerVisible flipped false→true. The ITMS-90474 premise is shakier than 0.75 suggests — under the iOS 26 SDK iPad windows are always resizable and UIRequiresFullScreen no longer has its old effect, so the validation error may not fire at all. The T0 case does not need it: C9-01 proves TestFlight will offer this build to the tester's iPad, where it installs as a native iPad app over zero size-class code and fixed-count grids. A design client is exactly the person who owns an iPad. Family=1 is an S-effort honest scoping of round one and deletes the whole class.

confirmed.title: Beta App Review details are empty — the external tester group can never be served a build
confirmed.evidence: `asc testflight review view --app 6762007888` returns one betaAppReviewDetails record with literally "attributes": {} — no contactFirstName/LastName/Email/Phone, no demoAccountName/Password, demoAccountRequired unset, no notes. The external group "MiddleWest Client" (created 2026-09-01T19:50Z) exists, and the app gates everything behind sign-in.
confirmed.fix: Fill contact details; set demoAccountRequired=true with a working production account (try tester@patina.cloud / 000000 first); notes should explain that the OTP arrives by email and name the guest-browse path so a reviewer can get in without one.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-verified live: `asc testflight review view --app 6762007888` returns one betaAppReviewDetails record, id 6762007888, with literally "attributes": {} — no contact name/email/phone, no demo account, no notes. Also verified the external group exists and is empty of prerequisites: `asc testflight groups list` → 'Internal Patina' (internal, hasAccessToAllBuilds true, created 2026-09-01T19:50:28Z) and 'MiddleWest Client' (external, created 2026-09-01T19:50:46Z). External distribution needs Beta App Review, and the app gates everything behind sign-in, so this genuinely blocks the external group.
confirmed.judgeNote: The invite dead-ends before the app exists. The external group 'MiddleWest Client' was created today, so external distribution IS the round-one plan, and external distribution requires Beta App Review, which requires these fields. The demo-account line matters most: everything is behind sign-in, so a reviewer with no working account fails the app for a reason that has nothing to do with the app. Try tester@patina.cloud / 000000 in the simulator once before writing it into the notes — an untested demo credential in review notes is worse than none.

confirmed.title: No TestFlight test information (beta description, feedback email) — external submission blocked and testers get a blank card
confirmed.evidence: `asc testflight app-localizations list --app 6762007888` → {"data":[], "meta":{"paging":{"total":0}}}. No beta app description, no feedbackEmail, no marketing/privacy URL on the TestFlight side.
confirmed.fix: Create the en-US betaAppLocalization (description, feedbackEmail, marketingUrl https://patina.cloud/app, privacyPolicyUrl https://patina.cloud/privacy), then per-build whatsNew via `asc builds test-notes create`.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-verified live: `asc testflight app-localizations list --app 6762007888` → {"data":[],"meta":{"paging":{"total":0}}}. No beta description, no feedbackEmail, no marketing/privacy URL on the TestFlight side. Pairs with A2-04 as the same submission-prerequisite step.
confirmed.judgeNote: Under-rated as pure config — this is the tester's actual first screen. The TestFlight card is read BEFORE the app launches, so 'the first five minutes' start here, in copy Kody has not written. A blank description plus no feedback email is the first impression of a product whose whole pitch is care. Treat it as a copy task (patina-brand-voice), not a form to fill, and pair the per-build whatsNew with it — those two strings are the only narration a tester gets between invite and launch.

confirmed.title: No ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption and no encryption declaration — every upload parks in Missing Compliance
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption apps/mobile/Patina` → nothing. `asc encryption declarations list --app 6762007888` → {"data":[]}. The May 2026 build carries usesNonExemptEncryption:false, i.e. it was answered by hand in the ASC UI.
confirmed.fix: Add <key>ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption</key><false/> to Patina/Info.plist. The app uses only HTTPS/TLS plus Apple/swift-crypto for standard purposes, which is exempt.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified three ways: grep for ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption across apps/mobile/Patina returns nothing; the key is absent from the as-built Info.plist (plutil -p on the Debug product); and `asc encryption declarations list --app 6762007888` → {"data":[]}. The May 2026 build carries usesNonExemptEncryption:false, i.e. answered by hand in the UI, exactly as the finding says. Severity major is right — it is answerable in the ASC UI per upload, so it delays rather than stops.
confirmed.judgeNote: Over-stated as major: this is not a wall. The May 2026 build shipped with usesNonExemptEncryption:false answered by hand in the ASC UI, which is the proof that a human can clear it in ten seconds per upload. Downgraded to minor — a recurring manual gate, not a blocker. Kept at T0 purely because it is one Info.plist line riding with A2-02, and because a build parked in Missing Compliance on a Friday costs the round a weekend.

confirmed.title: The Release/archive path has never been run for this app — the riskiest step is unproven and on the critical path
confirmed.evidence: ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives does not exist. `find ~ -name '*.xcarchive'` finds only apps/mobile/Capture/.build/archives/PatinaField-2026083*.xcarchive (the Field app). Across ~40 Patina-* DerivedData trees there is NO Build/Products/Release* directory — every build has been Debug-iphonesimulator (one Debug-iphoneos under Mobile-*). Corroborated in-repo: PushTokenService.swift:191 states "this project's Release signing has never performed a true distribution archive".
confirmed.fix: Before anything else in the fix program, run one throwaway `xcodebuild archive -destination generic/platform=iOS` + `-exportArchive -exportOptionsPlist` (method app-store-connect, automatic signing) purely as a dry run, and inspect the exported IPA's embedded.mobileprovision entitlements. That single run converts A2-03, A2-08, A2-19, A2-23 and A2-24 from predicted to observed.
confirmed.codeNote: The underlying fact holds and I re-verified it: ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives does not exist, apps/mobile/Patina/.build does not exist, and every Patina-* DerivedData tree under ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData has only Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator. PushTokenService.swift:190-192 says so in its own comment. ADJUSTED because it is now partly superseded: lane G DID run `xcodebuild archive` (research/G-archive.log:7201 '** ARCHIVE FAILED **', exit 65) — the prescribed dry run was performed and is blocked at compile by G-01, not by signing. Reframe as a sequenced step ('no successful distribution archive or export has ever been produced; re-run the archive + -exportArchive + codesign -d --entitlements inspection immediately after G-01 lands'), which is what converts A2-03, A2-19, A2-23 and C9-20 from predicted to observed. It is not an independent blocker; G-01 is.
confirmed.judgeNote: Premise superseded, prescription intact. The G lane DID run the archive (research/G-archive.log) — it failed at compile (G-01), not at signing. So 'never attempted' is now 'attempted, died before the interesting part': the export, the re-sign, and the embedded entitlements remain genuinely unobserved. Downgraded blocker→major because it is an unknown rather than a wall, but it stays T0 — it is literally how build 1 gets made, and it discharges A2-19, A2-23, C9-20 and A4-13 in one run.

confirmed.title: GitCommit.swift is gitignored but compiled, and its directory is not a sandbox-declared output — clean-checkout/CI archive fails
confirmed.evidence: `git ls-files apps/mobile/Patina/Patina/Generated/` → empty; .gitignore:57 ignores it. The phase declares outputPaths = ("$(SRCROOT)/Patina/Generated/GitCommit.swift") but its first action is `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"` — the directory is not a declared output — while the project sets ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES in both Debug and Release. On a fresh clone the file is absent when the PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup is resolved, so `GitCommit.sha` (AppConfiguration.swift:77) is not in scope. In Release the script also computes SHA="" and must rewrite the file, so the write is not skippable.
confirmed.fix: Either commit a GitCommit.swift with sha = "" (remove .gitignore:57) and let the Debug-only phase overwrite it, or emit into $(DERIVED_FILE_DIR) and add it as a real generated source. Also add $(SRCROOT)/Patina/Generated to outputPaths so the mkdir is sandbox-legal.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism confirmed in every particular: .gitignore:57 ignores Patina/Generated/GitCommit.swift, `git ls-files apps/mobile/Patina/Patina/Generated/` is empty, the 'Stamp Git SHA' phase (pbxproj:410-429, alwaysOutOfDate = 1) declares only the FILE in outputPaths while its first action is `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"`, ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES sits at pbxproj:585 (Debug) and :649 (Release), and AppConfiguration.swift:77 compiles `GitCommit.sha`. ADJUSTED on severity, blocker → major: there is no CI archive to break (grep of .github/workflows for 'xcodebuild' or 'Patina.xcodeproj' returns nothing), and Kody's checkout has the file — which is exactly why lane G's Release build reached Swift type errors (G-release.log) instead of failing in the script phase. It bites the first fresh clone or the first CI archive, not the round-one upload, and it is not tester-visible.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not a build-1 blocker: G-01's Release build resolved GitCommit.sha fine and died only on preview fixtures, which proves the file is present where Kody actually archives. blocker→minor. But do not cut it — this repo dispatches agents into worktrees by convention (patina-parallel-work), and a fresh worktree has no Generated/GitCommit.swift, so the fix program itself will hit this the first time it tries to archive from an isolated checkout. T1, and pair it with A2-09 as one 'a fresh worktree must build' row.

confirmed.title: Secrets.swift is gitignored and its example twin is excluded from the target — a clean checkout does not compile
confirmed.evidence: Secrets.swift holds the only non-empty supabaseAnonKey (208 chars, JWT-shaped) and postHogAPIKey (47 chars, phc_-shaped) — measured by length, never printed. Secrets.example.swift is explicitly excluded from the Patina target via membershipExceptions, so a checkout without Secrets.swift has no `Secrets` symbol at all. openAIKey and claudeAPIKey are nil in the real file, so any Companion path needing them is dead in every build.
confirmed.fix: Keep the key out of git but make the symbol always exist: include a fallback Secrets declaration in the target, or generate Secrets.swift from an xcconfig/env at the start of the archive script. Record the archive prerequisites in apps/mobile/Patina/CLAUDE.md.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified: .gitignore:53 ignores Patina/App/Configuration/Secrets.swift, and pbxproj:87-94 excludes App/Configuration/Secrets.example.swift from the Patina target via membershipExceptions, so a checkout without Secrets.swift has no `Secrets` symbol at all. Secrets.swift is present locally (mode 600, untracked) — I did not open its values. The nil-key claim checks out by pattern match only: 'openAIKey: String? = nil' and 'claudeAPIKey: String? = nil' each appear once in the real file, so any Companion path requiring them is inert in every build. Same clean-checkout class as A2-08 but a genuinely different mechanism — keep both.
confirmed.judgeNote: Halved. The clean-checkout half is real and shares A2-08's root — Secrets.example.swift is excluded from the target via membershipExceptions, so a fresh clone has no `Secrets` symbol at all. The Companion half is over-stated: grep across the app finds openAIKey and claudeAPIKey referenced NOWHERE outside their own declarations in Secrets.swift:24,27 and the example twin — nothing reads them, so no Companion path is dead; they are two dead fields. major→minor. Fold into the A2-08 row; the dead fields are a one-line cleanup, not a finding.

confirmed.title: Global accent colour is undefined — system controls tint iOS blue inside a warm Patina palette
confirmed.evidence: The colorset is {"colors":[{"idiom":"universal"}]} — an entry with no `color` value. `xcrun assetutil --info` on the shipped Assets.car lists 37 entries and every one of them is AppIcon* — there is no AccentColor asset in the binary at all. Only 25 `.tint(` call sites exist across 435 Swift files. App ground is PatinaColors.Background.primary = off-white (light) / warm-graphite (dark).
confirmed.fix: Give AccentColor a real light/dark value from PatinaColors, or delete the colorset and set `.tint(...)` once on the root WindowGroup. Untinted system affordances — alert default buttons, text-field caret and selection, Link, swipe actions, Toggle, date pickers, sheet grabbers, refresh spinners — currently render system blue, the single most legible 'template app' tell.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified on main d7287c3f8: Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset/Contents.json is {"colors":[{"idiom":"universal"}]} — no `color` key — while pbxproj:672,720 set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME = AccentColor. Concrete leaks exist: ScanUploadProgressView.swift:87 `return .accentColor` and :185 `Capsule().fill(Color.accentColor)`; FirstLaunchTour.swift:868 `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`. ~32 `.tint(` sites (finding said 25), none at the root WindowGroup. Canonical for the accent defect; C3-02 is the same root cause.
confirmed.judgeNote: CANONICAL. Verified: AccentColor.colorset Contents.json has an idiom entry with no color value. Highest impact-to-effort ratio in the whole audit — one colorset fixes the caret, selection, alert default buttons, Link, swipe actions, Toggle, date pickers, sheet grabbers and refresh spinners simultaneously. iOS blue inside a warm clay palette is the single most legible 'built from a template' signal, and the tester meets it in the email field in minute one.

confirmed.title: Two competing permission-string sets; build settings silently win and the surviving copy is marketing prose
confirmed.where: project.pbxproj INFOPLIST_KEY_NS*UsageDescription (:695-699 Debug, :747-751 Release) vs Patina/Info.plist:5-14
confirmed.evidence: The merged as-built plist settles precedence: camera = "Patina uses your camera to walk through your space together and visualize furniture in your room." (build setting), microphone = "Have a voice conversation with Patina about your space and style." (build setting), speech = "Speak naturally with Patina instead of typing." (build setting). The Info.plist wordings for those three — including the one that mentions QR-code sign-in — never reach a device. NSFaceIDUsageDescription and NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription survive from the file; NSMotionUsageDescription and NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription come only from build settings, so BOTH photo keys ship.
confirmed.fix: Pick one source (the build settings, since they win), delete the duplicated keys from Info.plist, drop NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription unless the app really reads the library, and rewrite each string as 'Patina uses X to Y.' The mic/speech strings are imperatives to the user, not statements of use — the exact shape reviewers bounce under 5.1.1, and a tester learns nothing about whether audio leaves the phone.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified against the merged built Info.plist (DerivedData Patina.app), not just the sources. Build settings win exactly as claimed: camera='Patina uses your camera to walk through your space together and visualize furniture in your room.', microphone='Have a voice conversation with Patina about your space and style.', speech='Speak naturally with Patina instead of typing.'. NSFaceIDUsageDescription + NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription survive from Patina/Info.plist; NSMotionUsageDescription + NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription come only from build settings, so both photo keys do ship. The Info.plist camera string that mentions QR sign-in never reaches a device. pbxproj lines are :683-687 (Debug) / :731-735 (Release), one off the cited :695-699/:747-751.
confirmed.judgeNote: The permission modal is the app's first sentence about itself, and the surviving strings are imperatives to the user ('Have a voice conversation with Patina…', 'Speak naturally with Patina instead of typing.') rather than statements of use — the exact 5.1.1(i) shape reviewers bounce. Escalates to blocker if the first round goes out as EXTERNAL TestFlight (Beta App Review applies); internal-only testers skip review, so it stays major. Shipping both photo-library keys also inflates the privacy nutrition label for data the app may never read. T0 regardless — one source of truth, three rewrites.

confirmed.title: Deployment target 26.5 with no 26.5-only code — excludes any tester not yet on that point release
confirmed.where: project.pbxproj IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.5 (project + both targets); built plist MinimumOSVersion 26.5
confirmed.evidence: The only version gates in 435 Swift files are four `#available(iOS 26.0, *)` checks: ProductDetailBlocks.swift:213, CompanionOverlay.swift:1141, ARPlacementView.swift:237 and :248. There is no @available(iOS 26.5) anywhere. The previously uploaded build shipped at minOsVersion 17.6.
confirmed.fix: Set 26.0 (matching the only gates in the code) and let a build prove it. A homeowner on 26.0–26.4 currently opens the invite and reads 'requires iOS 26.5 or later' — the invitation dead-ends before launch. If something genuinely needs 26.5, wrap it in #available rather than raising the floor.
confirmed.codeNote: Canonical entry for the deployment-target cluster. IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.5 at pbxproj:494,:526,:600,:658,:693,:741,:772,:794; as-built Info.plist MinimumOSVersion 26.5. Reproduced the availability census across Patina + PatinaWidget + PatinaWidgetShared: the only 26-era guards are #available(iOS 26.0, *) at ProductDetailBlocks.swift:213, CompanionOverlay.swift:1141, ARPlacementView.swift:237 and :248, plus legacy 14.0/14.5/18.0 guards; there is no @available(iOS 26.5) anywhere. The previously uploaded ASC build really did ship at minOsVersion 17.6 (verified live). Nothing in the app justifies the 0.5 above 26.0, and a 26.0-26.4 invitee is excluded before launch.

C9-02's census proves nothing above 26.0 is used, so this is a one-line setting protecting nothing. Not raised to blocker only because it bites a subset of invitees — but it is the cheapest insurance in the program and belongs in the same pbxproj pass as A2-01/A2-03.

confirmed.title: Launch screen has no declared background — the cold-launch flash does not match the app in either appearance
confirmed.where: project.pbxproj INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation = YES with no UIColorName; built plist UILaunchScreen = { UILaunchScreen = {} }
confirmed.evidence: The generated launch config is empty — no UIColorName, no UIImageName. The app's own first frame is Patina/Features/Splash/Views/SplashView.swift:20 painting PatinaColors.Background.primary, which PatinaDesignKit/Sources/PatinaDesignKit/Tokens/PatinaColors.swift:92-96 defines as off-white (light) / warm-graphite (dark). Reasoned from the plist, not screenshotted.
confirmed.fix: Add a LaunchBackground colorset (light off-white / dark warm-graphite) and set INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_UIColorName = LaunchBackground; optionally add the strata mark as UIImageName so launch and splash are one continuous image. Verify by screenshotting the first 300 ms in both appearances.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed and now SIM-VERIFIED, upgrading the lane's own 'reasoned from the plist, not screenshotted' caveat. shots/P/timing-1.png (t+1.26 s of a fresh cold launch) is a blank WHITE screen with no status bar; shots/P/ledger.md row 5 records white at 1.26 s → cream PATINA splash at 2.32 s → interactive Welcome at 3.38 s. So the undesigned flash holds for ~1 s, not a frame. Light: white → #FAF7F2; dark: white → #211E1B, which is the jarring case. Fix as written (LaunchBackground colorset + UIColorName).
confirmed.judgeNote: Downgrading major to minor: an empty UILaunchScreen yields the system background, so the light-mode flash is white against off-white (barely perceptible) and only the dark-mode flash (black against warm-graphite) actually reads. Still T0 — it is one colorset and it fires on every single launch, including the tester's very first frame. Screenshot the first 300ms in dark to confirm before and after.

confirmed.title: The analytics kill-switch is dead code — Debug builds report into the production PostHog project
confirmed.evidence: `AppConfiguration.analyticsEnabled` (AppEnvironment.current != .debug) has NO callers — grep across Patina/ and PatinaWidget* returns only the declaration. PatinaApp.init calls PostHogService.shared.initialize() guarded solely by `!Self.isUITesting`, and PostHogService.initialize() bails only on an empty key, which is never empty (Secrets.postHogAPIKey, host https://us.i.posthog.com). So the brief's premise ('PostHog only in Release') is false.
confirmed.fix: Either delete analyticsEnabled or actually gate on it. Preferred: keep PostHog initialised in Debug but pointed at a separate dev project key, so flag behaviour stays testable without polluting the exact funnels the first tester round is meant to measure — and without evaluating flags against dev identities.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism CONFIRMED exactly. `grep -rn analyticsEnabled` across apps/mobile/Patina returns ONE hit — AppConfiguration.swift:50, its own declaration; zero callers. PatinaApp.swift:73-76 gates `PostHogService.shared.initialize()` only on `!Self.isUITesting`. PostHogService.initialize() (:49-53) bails only on an empty key; Secrets.swift:30 holds a live `phc_…` key, host us.i.posthog.com. So Debug builds do report into the production project and the brief's 'PostHog only in Release' premise is false. ADJUSTED on severity only: testerVisible=false and the harm is analytics hygiene (dev events polluting the funnels Kody targets flags from), not something a tester judges — major overstates it against the brief's ladder. Minor.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: `analyticsEnabled` has exactly one occurrence in the tree — its own declaration — and initialize() gates only on a non-empty key. T0 by adjacency, not by independent urgency: it is the same file and the same commit as A2-16, S effort. It matters because every Simulator walk (this audit's included) has been writing app_open/login/dwell into the production project under locally-seeded ids, corrupting the exact funnels round 1 exists to produce. Prefer the separate dev-project key over a hard off switch so flag behaviour stays testable.

confirmed.title: No crash or error reporting in the TestFlight build
confirmed.evidence: The config sets only captureScreenViews=false, captureApplicationLifecycleEvents=true, sendFeatureFlagEvent=false, debug=isDebug. posthog-ios 3.48.0 exposes errorTrackingConfig (PostHogConfig.swift:175, wired at :238 behind errorTrackingConfig.autoCapture, @_spi(Experimental), additionally gated by the project's remote errorTracking config) and sessionReplay (:168, default false) — neither is touched. PLCrashReporter 1.12.2 ships inside the bundle as a posthog dependency but nothing arms it.
confirmed.fix: Enable PostHog error tracking (@_spi(Experimental) import PostHog; config.errorTrackingConfig.autoCapture = true) and turn errorTracking on for the project; consider sessionReplay with masking for the internal group only. Confirm dSYM upload so traces symbolicate. Today a crashing first session leaves only Apple's Organizer log — delayed and dependent on the tester's diagnostics setting.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. `grep -rn 'errorTracking|sessionReplay'` across the whole app returns ZERO hits — PostHogService.swift:58-66 sets only captureScreenViews/captureApplicationLifecycleEvents/sendFeatureFlagEvent/debug. `grep -rni 'sentry|bugsnag|crashlytics|NSSetUncaughtExceptionHandler'` also returns zero: there is no crash or error reporting of any kind. PLCrashReporter does ship in the bundle — the built .app contains PLCrashReporter_CrashReporter.bundle — and nothing arms it. Note this finding also REFUTES R-19's premise that 'PostHog error tracking is wired into this build'.
confirmed.judgeNote: Re-confirmed by grep — no errorTracking or sessionReplay reference exists anywhere in the target. Build 1 IS the crash-discovery round; shipping it with no reporting means a tester's crash reaches you only through Apple's Organizer, delayed and only for testers who opted into sharing diagnostics. Not tester-visible, but it is the instrument that decides whether round 1 teaches you anything. Confirm dSYM upload at the same time or the traces are useless.

confirmed.title: AppTrackingTransparency is linked but never requested; the opt-out branch is unreachable
confirmed.evidence: `otool -L Patina.debug.dylib` shows /System/Library/Frameworks/AppTrackingTransparency.framework linked. Nothing calls requestTrackingAuthorization and there is no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription in the merged plist, so trackingAuthorizationStatus is permanently .notDetermined — neither .denied nor .restricted — and PostHogSDK.shared.optOut() never runs. No AdSupport/IDFA anywhere.
confirmed.fix: Delete the import and the block. Declare NSPrivacyTracking=false in the new privacy manifest (A2-02) and answer the ASC nutrition label as not-tracking. Linking ATT with no purpose string invites a review question about tracking the app does not do.

PostHogService.swift:11 imports ATT and :70-76 reads trackingAuthorizationStatus, so status is permanently .notDetermined and optOut() is unreachable. plutil on the built merged Info.plist confirms no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key.

confirmed.title: aps-environment is 'development' in the shipped entitlements — push may register sandbox tokens in TestFlight
confirmed.evidence: Entitlement literal is <key>aps-environment</key><string>development</string>. PushTokenService.detectEnvironment (Patina/Services/API/PushTokenService.swift:205-222) parses the embedded .mobileprovision per token and maps development → sandbox, absent profile → production, unparseable → #if DEBUG. Its own header comment at :191 records that a true distribution archive has never been produced.
confirmed.fix: Part of the A2-07 dry run: unzip the exported IPA and run `codesign -d --entitlements` on the .app to confirm aps-environment: production. Then send one real push to a TestFlight install before the round opens — if the entitlement is not flipped at export, every device registers a sandbox token and production sends fail with BadDeviceToken, silently.
confirmed.codeNote: Mis-framed: Patina/Patina.entitlements is the SOURCE entitlement, not 'the shipped entitlements'. pbxproj has CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic with PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER empty (project.pbxproj:674-701, 722-749), so Xcode rewrites aps-environment against the distribution profile at export; 'development' is Apple's own template default. The app is belt-and-braces anyway — PushTokenService.detectEnvironment (Services/API/PushTokenService.swift:207-222) re-derives per token from the embedded .mobileprovision, and apns-send picks the host per token (apns-send/core.ts:47-57). This lane's own A3 agent already concluded the same (research/A3-prod.md:200-203: 'does not by itself break TestFlight push'). Not an app finding — fold the codesign -d --entitlements check into the A2-07 archive dry-run checklist.
confirmed.judgeNote: Adjusting the framing, not the fact: probability is low (Xcode's app-store export normally rewrites aps-environment to production under automatic signing) but the cost of being wrong is unbounded and unrecoverable — every device in the round registers a sandbox token, production sends fail BadDeviceToken silently, and no server-side fix reaches them without a second build. That asymmetry, not the severity, is what puts it in T0. It costs one command inside the archive dry run A2-07 already requires (codesign -d --entitlements on the exported .app). Note the sequencing though: with C2-05 unfixed nothing is being sent anyway, so this is a gate on the build, not a gate on the tester experience — do not let it grow into a project.

confirmed.title: Supabase SDK diagnostics are Debug-only, so the most likely TestFlight failure is invisible in Release
confirmed.evidence: `#if DEBUG let logger: (any SupabaseLogger)? = SupabaseDiagnosticsLogger() #else let logger: (any SupabaseLogger)? = nil #endif`. The file's own comment (:15-21) records that a failing keychain read once stripped Authorization off every PostgREST request and stayed invisible without this logger.
confirmed.fix: Keep the logger in Release but route it through PatinaLog at .error only (no session or request bodies), or capture failures as PostHog non-fatals once A2-16 lands. Keychain/entitlement state on a fresh device install is exactly this failure class, and a tester's 'nothing loads' is otherwise undiagnosable.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED verbatim. SupabaseClient.swift:48-52 is exactly `#if DEBUG let logger: (any SupabaseLogger)? = SupabaseDiagnosticsLogger() #else let logger: (any SupabaseLogger)? = nil #endif`, and the file header at :15-21 records the keychain/Authorization failure this logger once caught. Release therefore has no SDK diagnostics at all — and with A2-16 confirmed (no error reporting anywhere), a tester's 'nothing loads' really is undiagnosable.
confirmed.judgeNote: Small on its own, load-bearing in combination: with C7-08 it is the difference between 'the tester says nothing loads' being diagnosable or a dead end, and the file's own comment records this exact failure happening before. Keep it Release-safe — .error level only, no session or request bodies — and land it after A2-16 gives the failures somewhere to go.

confirmed.title: Every product surface is empty on production: get_recommendations returns zero rows for every tester
confirmed.evidence: products = 15 rows, of which layer='catalog' AND status='published' = 1: name 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp', description 'seed:stripe-smoke-2026-07-08', images [], vendor_id NULL, brand NULL, price_retail 2000. get_aesthete_matches Stage 0 filters exactly `p.layer='catalog' AND p.status='published'`, and forces v_layer:='catalog' when auth.uid() IS NULL (get_recommendations never passes p_layer, so signed-in callers default to catalog too). That single candidate then yields ZERO rows: (a) the shared neutral profile ae460000-0000-4000-8000-00000000e057 has style_vector NULL (verified) so v_query is NULL and the ANN insert is skipped; (b) the spectrum-only fallback requires b.pspec IS NOT NULL and `select (select ps.spectrums from _aesthete_product_spectrum(p.id) ps)` for that product returns null (verified) so _ae_cand is empty. (c) Even if a row survived, the RPC's RETURNS TABLE has no `brand` column and maker_name is COALESCE(v.name,'Unknown Maker') = the literal 'Unknown Maker', which Product.resolvedMakerName rejects, so withholdingUnresolvedMakers drops it. Anon PostgREST count over products: `content-range: 0-0/1`.
confirmed.fix: Seed a real catalogue: >=30 layer='catalog' status='published' products with brand or vendor, images, price, category and a product_dna/spectrum row so _aesthete_product_spectrum returns non-null. Give the neutral client_style_profiles row a style_vector, or add a last-resort candidate path in get_aesthete_matches when both ANN and spectrum paths are empty. Rename/retire 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp'.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED, prod-verified read-only. products: 15 rows total, layer='catalog' = 1, catalog+published = 1, catalog+published with images = 0 — the single row is 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp', lighting, price_retail 2000. `_aesthete_product_spectrum('a7fa2107-…')` returns NULL for that product (verified), so the spectrum-only fallback candidate set is empty. get_recommendations RETURNS TABLE is the 14-column shape with maker_name only and NO brand; pg_get_functiondef confirms `COALESCE(v.name, 'Unknown Maker')`, and ProductModel.swift:222-233 `resolvedMakerName` rejects the literal 'Unknown Maker'/'Unknown', so ProductAPIClient.swift:85-94 withholds the row. Zero pieces reach a tester. ONE evidence correction, not affecting the verdict: the neutral profile ae460000-0000-4000-8000-00000000e057 does not currently EXIST on prod (count 0) rather than 'having a NULL style_vector' — get_recommendations get-or-creates it (functiondef §3) and the INSERT omits style_vector, so it will be NULL when first created.
confirmed.judgeNote: The loudest thing in the audit. A browsing app whose first five minutes show nothing, and whose single visible product is named 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp' at $20 with no image, cannot ship to a homeowner — the tester's conclusion is 'this is a demo', and nothing else in the round gets evaluated. Sequence AFTER A3-03 so the widened get_recommendations projection is live, attach real vendors so resolvedMakerName stops withholding rows, and re-probe as anon before calling it done. Independently corroborated from the walk side (P-36).

confirmed.title: delete-account edge function 404s on Strata — App Store 5.1.1(v) account deletion can never succeed
confirmed.evidence: Live probe returns {"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Requested function was not found"}. list_edge_functions has no delete-account entry. supabase/functions/delete-account/ exists in the repo — it was never deployed. AccountDeletionService's own header calls it 'release-gating for any app that lets a person create an account'; every failure resolves to the single sentence "We couldn't close your account just now. Try again, or write to hello@patina.cloud."
confirmed.fix: `supabase functions deploy delete-account`, then probe with a real user JWT. Beta review can reject on this alone.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED four ways. Live `curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} -X POST https://bkvcixdmuyejfzcijpdg.supabase.co/functions/v1/delete-account` → 404. list_edge_functions on Strata returns 84 slugs, none named delete-account. The repo HAS supabase/functions/delete-account/{index.ts,handler.ts,handler.test.ts} and supabase/config.toml:572 declares `[functions.delete-account]` — it was written, wired and never deployed. AccountDeletionService.swift:5-6 calls it release-gating under 5.1.1(v); :36-37 resolves every failure to one sentence.
confirmed.judgeNote: Beta App Review can reject on 5.1.1(v) alone, and the tester-facing shape is a dead end: tap Delete account, get one apologetic sentence, forever. One deploy command plus a JWT probe. Ship it as one ticket with A-101 — 'account deletion is real and honest' — because fixing either half alone leaves the app either dishonest or broken.

confirmed.title: Migrations 00533–00540 were never applied to Strata — the whole iOS Daily Return server contract is missing

Repo has 00533_piece_detail_contract, 00534_client_attention_notifications, 00535_saved_items_price_snapshot, 00536_client_side_server_gaps, 00537_house_on_today, 00538_client_account_anonymize, 00539_saved_item_note_and_presence, 00540_direct_orders_attribution. Verified absent on prod: products.photo_verified_at, products.shipping_flat_cents, notify_client_attention(), purge_client_account(), client_account_purges, mark_client_account_purge_complete(), settle_direct_order_attribution(), get_direct_order_terms(), view client_designer_roster, table profile_presence. The get_recommendations on prod is the pre-00533 narrow projection (no brand/dimensions/lead_time/description).

Object-by-object probe returns 0 for ALL of: profile_presence, notify_client_attention(), purge_client_account(), get_direct_order_terms(), settle_direct_order_attribution(), products.photo_verified_at, rooms.budget_cents, profiles.last_seen_at, view client_designer_roster. pg_get_function_result on get_recommendations confirms the pre-00533 14-column projection with no brand/dimensions/lead_time/description.
confirmed.judgeNote: The single highest-leverage action in the whole audit: it closes A4-05, A3-11 and (per the lane) A3-10 through A3-14, and it is the precondition for A3-01's catalogue seed being visible at all. A homeowner opening build 1 gets a bell that says 'Nothing yet' while the Studio shows work, piece pages missing brand/dimensions/lead time, and inert room budgets — all one missing apply.
