confirmed.title: All 24 production profiles — emails, Stripe customer ids, phone, address — are readable by the anon key compiled into the app
confirmed.where: pg_policies: public.profiles; probe GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=* with Secrets.supabaseAnonKey
confirmed.evidence: Policy "Profiles are viewable by everyone" — roles {public}, cmd SELECT, qual: true. Live anon GET returns full rows including email ('kody.kochaver+client@gmail.com'), stripe_customer_id ('cus_Uqad0UqaHJ6kQX'), phone, city/state/zip, availability_status. `Prefer: count=exact` → content-range 0-23/24. The anon key ships inside every TestFlight binary, so anyone with the .ipa can dump the user table.
confirmed.fix: Replace the policy with `USING (auth.uid() = id)` plus an explicit narrow policy (or a SECURITY DEFINER view) for the columns other users legitimately need — display_name/avatar_url only. Audit which portal reads depend on the open policy first.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. pg_policy on public.profiles: policy 'Profiles are viewable by everyone', polcmd 'r', polroles = {} (i.e. PUBLIC), qual = `true`. anon holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants (has_table_privilege all true). profiles has 24 rows and carries email, stripe_customer_id, phone, city, state, availability_status (6 of the 7 named columns exist; `zip_code` is not the column name on prod — the address column set differs slightly, which does not weaken the finding). The anon key is compiled into every build, so the round widens this to every tester's device.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not visible in the UI, but it is the testers' OWN emails, phone, address and Stripe customer ids that go public the moment they sign up — and a tester round is precisely the moment you widen who holds the shipped anon key. The exposure predates TestFlight (the same key is already public in the web bundle), which raises urgency rather than lowering it. S effort; audit which portal reads lean on the open policy before narrowing to `auth.uid() = id` plus a display_name/avatar_url view.

confirmed.title: anon holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on notification_preferences and a policy that grants ALL to unauthenticated callers
confirmed.evidence: Policy "Service role full access to notification preferences" — roles {public}, cmd ALL, qual: (auth.uid() IS NULL). anon has SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE grants (has_table_privilege all true). auth.uid() IS NULL is exactly the anon case, so the policy meant for service_role also matches every anon caller. Live anon GET returns the row for user 74056c2a-866d-42b0-9e2a-d473c2484316 with every channel/type preference. I did not exercise the write (read-only lane) — grant + policy are the proof.
confirmed.fix: Drop the policy and rely on service_role's RLS bypass; REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the table from anon. Then re-probe. The same `auth.uid() IS NULL` shape may exist on other tables — grep pg_policies for it.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. pg_policy on public.notification_preferences: 'Service role full access to notification preferences', polcmd '*' (ALL), polroles = {} (PUBLIC), qual = `(auth.uid() IS NULL)` — which is precisely the anon case. has_table_privilege('anon', …) returns true for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE. Grant + permissive ALL policy is sufficient proof; the finder correctly did not exercise the write. The `auth.uid() IS NULL` shape is worth grepping for across pg_policies as the fix sketch says.
confirmed.judgeNote: Worse than a read: `auth.uid() IS NULL` matches anon exactly, and anon holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants, so an unauthenticated caller with the shipped key can rewrite or wipe a user's notification preferences. Drop the policy, REVOKE the write grants, re-probe — and make the pg_policies grep for the same `auth.uid() IS NULL` shape on other tables part of this same ticket.

confirmed.title: "Continue with Google" is the first button on the welcome screen and Google is disabled on Strata — the tester gets a raw server error
confirmed.evidence: GET /auth/v1/settings on Strata: "google": false (apple true, email true, everything else false). GET /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google → 400 {"error_code":"validation_failed","msg":"Unsupported provider: provider is not enabled"}. auth.identities has zero google rows — it has never worked. AuthService.signInWithGoogle catches, filters only ASWebAuthenticationSessionError.canceledLogin, then sets `errorMessage = error.localizedDescription`, so the welcome screen shows the raw string. This is the top button of three on the first screen a tester sees.
confirmed.fix: Either enable the Google provider on Strata (client id + secret + redirect) or remove the button from AuthScreenView for this release. Do not ship a first-screen button that cannot work.
confirmed.codeNote: Core fact CONFIRMED by my own read-only probe: GET https://bkvcixdmuyejfzcijpdg.supabase.co/auth/v1/settings returns "google":false (apple true, email true); GET /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google returns HTTP/2 400, x-sb-error-code: validation_failed, content-type application/json — no redirect. Two corrections. (1) WHERE is wrong: Google is the SECOND button, not the first. AuthScreenView.swift:77 is PatinaSignInWithAppleButton, :82 is Google, :85 is email — confirmed visually in shots/P/01-welcome-cold.png. (2) MECHANISM is wrong: signInWithOAuth (AuthService.swift:407-410) opens ASWebAuthenticationSession, which renders GoTrue's raw 400 JSON as a web page; there is no thrown SDK error to catch, and when the tester backs out of the sheet the ASWebAuthenticationSessionError.canceledLogin filter at :416 suppresses the banner entirely. So the tester does NOT see a red string on the welcome screen — they see raw JSON inside a browser sheet and then a silent dead-end. Severity stands: a non-functional primary auth control on the first screen.
confirmed.judgeNote: Top button on the first screen, guaranteed to fail for every tester, and the failure is a raw provider string. Cheapest T0 is deleting the button for build 1 — that also dissolves B-57 and half of P-02. Enabling Google instead buys A-71 (raw-hostname consent dialog) as a NEW T0, so removal is the right call for round 1.

confirmed.title: Sign in with Apple creates the tester as profiles.role = 'designer'
confirmed.evidence: handle_new_user honours only the literal 'homeowner' from raw_user_meta_data and otherwise inserts COALESCE(v_role,'designer'). sendMagicLink and signUp both pass role:"homeowner"; signInWithApple calls signInWithIdToken with no `data:` at all, so an Apple tester lands as a designer. Confirmed downstream on the live tester account: tester@patina.cloud has profiles.role='designer' and four designer-portal notification_log rows including the 'Designer Onboarding' sequence email "Your desk is ready". prod role spread: client 11, designer 8, homeowner 4, super_admin 1. (The provision_studio_on_designer trigger keys on is_designer IS TRUE, not role, so no phantom studio is created.)
confirmed.fix: Pass the same role metadata on the Apple path — supabase-swift's signInWithIdToken has no data: parameter, so follow success with auth.update(UserAttributes(data:["role":"homeowner"])). Better: have handle_new_user default to the consumer role and require a server-side grant for 'designer'.
confirmed.codeNote: Root cause CONFIRMED exactly. AuthService.swift:370-376 calls signInWithIdToken with no data: parameter; 00313_handle_new_user_client_role_hint.sql honours only the literal 'homeowner' and otherwise inserts COALESCE(v_role,'designer') — and that migration's own header admits it: 'OAuth (Apple/Google) signups that cannot pass creation metadata — the previous default designer is preserved… OAuth-client role correction is a separate client-side follow-on.' But the tester-visible half is misattributed: designer-onboarding enrollment (00292_designer_onboarding_enrollment.sql) is gated on profiles.is_designer, NOT on role (00050's role='designer' trigger_config is declarative jsonb with no evaluator), and tester@patina.cloud was created through the portal invite path, so its four notification_log rows do not demonstrate that an Apple iOS signup receives the drip. The iOS app never reads profiles.role (grep over Services/ finds only the 'role':'client' PostHog property and the two 'homeowner' writes). Real defect — server-side misclassification for funnel views and comms participant-role derivation — but not visible to a tester in the app.
confirmed.judgeNote: Mechanism confirmed in code; the tester@patina.cloud evidence is NOT proof of it — that account came from the studio-invite incident where it was invited as a designer, so its role and its 'Designer Onboarding' rows have another explanation. T0 regardless: Apple is the only fully working button on production, and every tester who uses it writes a wrong role into prod and can trigger a designer drip at a homeowner. That is cleanup work later, not a UI fix.

confirmed.title: 20 of the app's 36 iOS help surface keys have no Sanity document
confirmed.evidence: 246 helpContent docs exist, all published. Querying surfaceKey match "ios-app*" returns 16. Present: first-launch-tour/step-1..3, ios-app/home + 6 children, ios-app/product-detail + 5 children. Missing: ios-app/first-launch-tour (root), all 4 ios-app/companion/*, all 5 ios-app/profile*, all 5 ios-app/qr-auth*, all 5 ios-app/rooms*. Every existing doc is persona:"all" while the app's Persona enum is designer|maker|consumer|admin and the primary GROQ is `persona == $p`, so resolution rides entirely on the fallback chain.
confirmed.fix: Author the 20 missing documents, or make the '?' affordance hide itself when the fetch returns nil so a tester never taps into an empty panel. Confirm the persona fallback chain actually reaches persona-less/'all' docs.
confirmed.codeNote: EVERY NUMBER IS RIGHT; THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT. Re-verified live against kv3qrinl/production: exactly 16 ios-app/* helpContent docs — first-launch-tour/step-1..3, ios-app/home + 6 children, ios-app/product-detail + 5 children — all persona 'all'. SurfaceKeys.swift declares exactly 36 ios-app keys, so the 20 missing are precisely the set named (first-launch-tour root, 4 companion, 5 profile, 5 qr-auth, 5 rooms). But the tester-visible impact is near zero, for two reasons. (1) The missing docs feed only the tooltip layer, and ALL NINE HelpInfoIcon call sites pass an inline `fallback:` string (DailyGreetingHeader.swift:77, ProductDetailView.swift:454/:494, QRApprovalView.swift:122, QRScannerView.swift:161, YourSpacesView.swift:73/:133/:160/:202) — so every `?` glyph in the app renders real copy with no CMS at all, as shots/B/17 shows. HelpTooltip.handleTriggerTap (:150-158) already implements the finding's proposed fix: silent absence, no empty popover. (2) The six help-panel doors never read these docs anyway — they query contentType=='helpArticle' (SanityHelpClient.swift:296-303), of which zero ios-app/* exist; that is C5-02/R-10, not this. Also, the closing worry is disproven: fallbackPlan (:369-390) step 2 targets persona 'all' and demonstrably resolves — the live tour copy rendering in shots/B/14 and B/15 is proof the chain reaches these docs. Downgrade from major/testerVisible to minor/not-tester-visible: a content-debt item, not a TestFlight defect.
confirmed.judgeNote: Facts confirmed, tester impact OVER-STATED — I checked the consequence the finding fears and it does not occur. The worry is "a tester taps into an empty panel"; but HelpTooltip's silent-absence path (handleTriggerTap: if hasLoaded && effectiveBody == nil { return }) only fires when there is neither CMS content NOR an inline fallback, and I read all nine HelpInfoIcon call sites outside the Help module (DailyGreetingHeader:75, ProductDetailView:452/492, QRApprovalView:120, QRScannerView:159, YourSpacesView:71/131/158/200) — every one passes a well-written `fallback:` string (e.g. YourSpacesView:71 "Whole Home rolls every room into one figure…", QRScannerView:159 "Scan the QR code shown in your browser…"). So the 20 missing keys are invisible: the binary copy renders, and there is no dead affordance anywhere. The persona sub-claim is also a non-issue — C5-01 network-verified that persona=all resolves via fallback-chain step 2, and the tour proves it end to end by rendering CMS copy today. What remains is real but is CMS debt, not tester-facing: Kody cannot edit 20 of 36 iOS help surfaces without shipping a build. Minor, testerVisible false, T2. Its 'hide the ? when the fetch returns nil' fix idea is still the right one — but it belongs to C5-02's panel, not to the tooltips.

confirmed.title: client_designer_roster view does not exist on Strata — the app's designer-of-record read 404s
confirmed.evidence: Live probe: 404 {"code":"PGRST205","message":"Could not find the table 'public.client_designer_roster' in the schema cache"}. pg_class count 0. The client's own header comment cites '(00536)', one of the eight unapplied migrations. This is not an empty result — it is a 404 with a raw PostgREST body.
confirmed.fix: Ships with A3-03 (apply 00536). Until then the roster call should read as 'no designer yet' rather than an error.
confirmed.codeNote: BACKEND FACT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — I probed Strata directly: `select relname, relkind from pg_class join pg_namespace … where nspname='public' and relname in ('client_designer_roster','designer_clients')` returns only `designer_clients` (relkind 'r'). The view is genuinely absent, and 00536_client_side_server_gaps.sql in the repo is where it is defined. BUT the app-side framing is wrong on both counts. (1) Not tester-visible: the only caller is BadgeCountService.swift:200, `async let rosterFetch = try? RosterAPIClient.shared.listRoster()` — the 404 is swallowed by `try?` and apply() keeps the previous (empty) value; the service's own comment at :62-65 already documents the roster as 'Expected empty until a client SELECT policy on designer_clients exists', and :243-247 deliberately excludes it from the load verdict so it cannot mask a real failure. No error string, no spinner, no state reaches glass. (2) The fix ('the roster call should read as "no designer yet" rather than an error') is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — there is nothing to change in the app. Downstream impact on a round-1 tester is nil: `.roster` differs from `.none` only in carrying a designerId for direct-order attribution (DesignerRelationship.swift:31-43), `.roster.isLive` is false, and DesignerThreadOpener.swift:65 treats `.none` and `.roster` identically; the direct-orders flag is OFF on a first TestFlight launch. Severity major → minor, testerVisible → false. This belongs entirely to A3-03 (the 00533–00540 ledger gap) as a migration to apply, not as an app finding.
confirmed.judgeNote: The 404 is real (live probe, and the client's own comment cites the unapplied 00536), but the tester-impact framing over-states it. The ONLY caller is BadgeCountService.swift:200, `async let rosterFetch = try? RosterAPIClient.shared.listRoster()`, and apply() deliberately excludes roster from the load verdict — so the failure already reads as 'no designer yet', which is the fix the finding asks for. Nothing downstream diverges for round 1 either: DesignerRelationship.roster is not `isLive` (no Buy pre-emption change), and its only real consumer is direct-order attribution, behind a flag that is OFF. So: no visible defect, a real prod-readiness gap (every badge refresh fires a 404 with a PostgREST body into prod logs, and designer-of-record attribution is silently dead). Severity major→minor, testerVisible→false. T1 only in the bookkeeping sense — it costs no separate work if 00536 lands with the T0 migration apply (A3-03); if that apply slips, this stays harmless.

confirmed.title: increment_scan_upload_attempt RPC does not exist on Strata and is in no pending migration
confirmed.evidence: select count(*) from pg_proc where pronamespace='public'::regnamespace and proname='increment_scan_upload_attempt' → 0. Unlike the other missing objects this one is not created by 00533–00540 either — grepping the migrations turns up nothing. Every scan-upload retry path gets PGRST202 instead of an attempt counter.
confirmed.fix: Write the migration (mirror mark_scan_upload_complete's shape and grants: anon+authenticated EXECUTE, non-DEFINER) or drop the call and count attempts locally.
confirmed.codeNote: The missing-object half is confirmed: `select proname from pg_proc where pronamespace='public'::regnamespace and proname like '%scan_upload%'` on Strata returns only mark_scan_upload_complete, and grep over supabase/migrations/ finds no definition. But the consequence is refuted. The call site is RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle.swift:646-664, inside `stampUploadStarted`, wrapped in do/catch with an explicit documented fallback: on PGRST202 it PATCHes room_scans with {upload_started_at, status:'uploading'}. I verified on Strata that room_scans has status, upload_started_at, upload_progress and upload_error — so the fallback lands and no upload path breaks. 'Every scan-upload retry path gets PGRST202 instead of an attempt counter' is true but harmless: the only thing lost is an attempt counter nothing reads. Not tester-visible; severity major -> polish.
confirmed.judgeNote: Fact confirmed, impact over-stated. The call site at RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle.swift:645-665 wraps the RPC in do/catch with a deliberate fallback — on PGRST202 it PATCHes upload_started_at + status='uploading' directly, and the comment says so ('The RPC is optional (pending migration)'). So the upload state IS written and the tester sees nothing: the cost is one wasted round-trip per bundle and a lost attempt counter. Dropping testerVisible to false and severity to minor. It should not be read as an independent blocker either — the real prod-readiness item is A3-03 (Strata's ledger jumps 00532→00541, leaving client_designer_roster, profile_presence and get_direct_order_terms genuinely missing with no fallback), and this row is a small addendum to it. Write the migration or count attempts locally, whenever 00533-00540 land.

confirmed.title: fulfillment_orders / _order_items / _shipments have no client SELECT policy — a tester's real order shows nothing
confirmed.where: pg_policies for the three fulfillment_* tables
confirmed.evidence: Each table has exactly two SELECT policies: *_select_admin (authenticated, gated on a role_domain='admin' user_roles join) and *_select_agent_reader (agent_reader, true). There is no client-facing policy; 00540 is what adds fulfillment_orders_select_client et al. via fulfillment_po_belongs_to_caller(). anon probe returns 401 42501 (grant-denied); an authenticated non-admin gets an empty array. The app reads all three in FulfillmentAPIClient.
confirmed.fix: Ships with A3-03 (apply 00540). Until then order tracking silently renders empty for a real order — worse than an error.
confirmed.codeNote: Prod-verified exactly as written. pg_policies on Strata returns precisely two SELECT policies per table and nothing else: fulfillment_orders_select_admin / _select_agent_reader, fulfillment_order_items_select_admin / _select_agent_reader, fulfillment_shipments_select_admin / _select_agent_reader — roles {authenticated} and {agent_reader} respectively, no client-facing policy on any of the three. `fulfillment_po_belongs_to_caller` also does not exist (pg_proc count 0), confirming 00540 is the missing piece. testerVisible corrected to false for round one: with `direct-orders` OFF and `create_direct_order` unable to produce an order (A3-20), no tester can create a row to fail to read, so 'silently renders empty' is a flag-on hazard, not a first-launch one.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed and it needs no feature flag to bite — OrdersService is wired into SessionScope and feeds both the Studio hub and the Record foreground on Today, so an affected tester gets a silently EMPTY Ordered rail, which is worse than an error because nothing invites a retry. Sized the exposure on Strata read-only: exactly 1 fulfillment_order and 2 fulfillment_order_items exist in production today. So the blast radius for build 1 is one client. T1 — but promote to T0 if any round-one tester is attached to that client, which Kody should check before cutting the build. Deploy caveat that belongs on the ticket: applying 00540 on Strata drags pending 00533-00539 on a plain db push (RESUME), so this needs a selective apply, not a push.

confirmed.title: tester@patina.cloud's notification feed is four designer-portal messages, one deep-linking to a host the app does not claim
confirmed.evidence: 4 rows: type 'welcome_series' / template 'designer-welcome' with metadata.headline "Welcome. Replay the walkthrough anytime from the Help shelf." and deep_link "https://app.patina.cloud/help"; a 'Designer Onboarding' sequence email subject "Your desk is ready"; and two 'workspace_invite' rows (teammate_type 'designer'). The AASA for cloud.patina.app claims client.patina.cloud only, for /piece/*, /invoices/*, /proposals/*, /decisions/* — app.patina.cloud is not claimed, so that link leaves the app for Safari and lands on the designer portal.
confirmed.fix: Give the first round a clean, purpose-built client account (consumer role, no designer sequences), or filter the iOS notifications read to client-relevant types. Also make the app refuse to surface a deep_link whose host it cannot open.
confirmed.codeNote: Substance real, mechanism and counts wrong. Read-only query on Strata for user 86cdd0aa-403c-4154-ae63-69105425e506 returns 4 rows but only ONE is channel='in_app' (id adf06c58, type welcome_series, template designer-welcome); the other three are channel='email' and are excluded by NotificationsAPIClient.list()'s channel=in.(in_app,push) filter (Core/Network/NotificationsAPIClient.swift:65). So the bell shows one row, not four. The 'leaves the app for Safari' half is REFUTED: the app never reads metadata.deep_link — grep for deep_link/deepLink across NotificationsAPIClient.swift and Features/Notifications/ returns nothing, and AppNotification(from:) (NotificationsAPIClient.swift:127-162) decodes only entity_type/entity_id/title/body. The real, worse defect: that row has entity_type and entity_id NULL and no metadata.title or metadata.body, so AppNotificationType(serverType: 'welcome_series') falls through to the default (.newRecommendations, :218) and the tester's one bell row renders as 'New pieces for you' with an EMPTY body, a sparkles icon, an unread dot — and route == nil, so the chevron dead-ends (see C2-15). Keep major; corrected fix = a clean consumer account plus a title/body fallback that never invents a category the row does not carry.
confirmed.judgeNote: This is the account the first round actually opens against production, so it is not hypothetical. A homeowner's very first bell tap yields 'Your desk is ready', a designer-portal welcome telling them to replay a walkthrough from 'the Help shelf' they have never seen, and two workspace_invite rows written for designers — then a tap that ejects them to Safari on app.patina.cloud, a host the app does not claim. That is the whole illusion collapsing in one screen. Split the tiers: the DATA half (a purpose-built client-role account carrying a real proposal, invoice and decision, no designer sequences) is T0 ops work with no build attached, and it also arms the push primer that C2-04 says never fires, and it removes the routeless rows that make C2-15 visible. The CODE half (refuse to surface a deep_link whose host the AASA does not claim, or filter the read to client types) is T1.

confirmed.title: The advertised tester credential (tester@patina.cloud / 000000) does not work in the iOS app — the test-login fallback is portal-only
confirmed.evidence: test-account-login mints a GoTrue magiclink hashed_token that the CALLER must redeem — the designer portal does that in test-account-fallback.ts. Grepping all 435 Swift files for 'test-account-login' returns nothing; the only '000000' hit is the TextField placeholder at AuthenticationView.swift:326. AuthService.verifyOtp calls supabase.auth.verifyOTP(email:token:type:.email) straight at GoTrue, which holds no OTP for that address unless one was actually emailed. Live probe of the function with an empty body returns the correct fail-closed 403 invalid_credentials, so the function itself is healthy.
confirmed.fix: Either add the fallback to AuthService.verifyOtp (POST the pair, then verifyOTP with the returned token_hash when the plain path fails), or give first-round testers a mailbox they can read and drop the 000000 instruction from the invite.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified every claim. grep over apps/mobile for 'test-account-login'/'testAccountLogin' returns ZERO hits; the only '000000' in the whole app is the TextField placeholder at AuthenticationView.swift:326. supabase/functions/test-account-login/index.ts mints a GoTrue magiclink hashed_token the CALLER must redeem (the portal does that in apps/designer-portal/src/app/auth/test-account-fallback.ts); AuthService.verifyOtp (:593-597) calls supabase.auth.verifyOTP straight at GoTrue, which holds no OTP for that address. Also confirmed LIVE in the lane's own evidence: shots/P/28-verify-t5.png shows tester@patina.cloud + a code rejected with 'Token has expired or is invalid'. I raise severity to blocker — this is the credential the invite hands a first-round tester, and it cannot work.
confirmed.judgeNote: A process blocker rather than a code one: if the invite advertises 000000, the tester's first act fails. The free T0 is deleting that instruction from the invite and letting testers use their own mailbox; the in-app fallback (M) belongs at T1 only if Kody wants a shared account. Settle which before build 1 — do not ship an invite the app cannot honour.

confirmed.title: The three editorial stories have no hero images and claim a 3–5 minute read on ~400-character bodies
confirmed.evidence: All 3 rows published, hero_image_url NULL on every one (so DailyStory falls back to PatinaGradients — a coloured rectangle where the art should be). Body lengths are 387, 386 and 489 characters against read_minutes of 5, 3 and 4. "A defense of imperfect linen" is a 387-character stub billed as a five-minute read. This is the top card of the home feed and, with the catalogue empty (A3-01), the only content a tester sees.
confirmed.fix: Commission real bodies and hero images for at least these three rows, or compute read_minutes from the body and hide the badge below a threshold. A story finished in fifteen seconds after being promised five minutes is the most damaging first impression here.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified directly against Strata prod (read-only SELECT on public.editorial_stories): 3 rows, hero_image_url NULL on all 3, maker_avatar_url NULL on all 3, body_md lengths 489/386/387 against read_minutes 4/3/5. 'A defense of imperfect linen' is 387 chars billed at 5 min. Render path confirmed: DailyStoryCard.storyArtwork (DailyStoryCard.swift:120-127) falls back to story.heroGradient when heroImageURL is nil (gradient built at EditorialStoriesAPIClient.swift:136); the label is DailyStory.swift:31 `"\(readMinutes) min read"` composed with the date at DailyStoryCard.swift:22-25. One aggravator the finding missed: published_at on all three is 2026-07-04/05/06, so the card on a Sep-1 'Today' prints a date ~two months stale (e.g. 'JUL 4 · 5 MIN').
confirmed.judgeNote: Impact framing needs splitting, and the two halves belong in different places. The read_minutes lie is the T0 half and it is genuinely damaging: with the catalogue empty this card is the only content in the app, so the tester's entire sense of 'is there anything here' rests on it, and being promised five minutes then finishing in fifteen seconds is the moment they conclude the app is a shell. Fix that by computing read time from the body or suppressing the badge below a threshold — S, code-side, shippable in build 1. The hero-image half is over-stated: a PatinaGradients panel can read as a deliberate editorial treatment rather than a missing asset, and real bodies plus commissioned art is Kody's content work on a human timeline, not a build-1 gate. T0 for the badge, the copy commissioning tracks separately.

confirmed.title: Every product fetch pulls two 768-dim vectors the app never decodes — 20.7 KB per row, ~90% waste
confirmed.evidence: Measured live: GET /rest/v1/products?select=*,vendors!... &limit=1 returns 20,706 bytes for ONE row. embedding = 9,459 chars (45%), aesthete_vector = 9,462 chars (45%), search_vector 113. RawProductWithVendor decodes neither. This select feeds both fetchProduct(id:) and fetchProducts(ids:) — the latter is the whole saved Record, so 30 saved pieces ≈ 620 KB of vectors over cellular before a single image loads.
confirmed.fix: Replace `*` with the ~24 columns RawProductWithVendor actually decodes. One-line change, ~10x smaller payload on the Record and on every piece open.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism CONFIRMED and independently re-measured on Strata: `select length(row_to_json(p)::text), length(embedding::text), length(aesthete_vector::text) from products limit 3` returns 20651/9508/9487, 20689/9459/9462, 24061/9504/9727 — ~92% of the row is two vectors RawProductWithVendor (ProductAPIClient.swift:222-249) never declares. `productSelect` feeds fetchProduct(id:) (:133) and fetchProducts(ids:) (:163), whose only caller is RecordForeground.swift:213. TWO corrections. (1) WHERE is wrong: the select literal is ProductAPIClient.swift:122, not :113 (:113 is a doc-comment line). (2) SEVERITY is overstated at major/tester-noticeable: a first-round tester opens with zero saved pieces, so the 30-piece/620 KB Record case does not exist on the first run, and on the piece-open path 20 KB of JSON is small beside the product photos AsyncImage pulls on the same screen. Keep it as a T1 one-liner (high value per byte of change), not a major.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: productSelect is still `*,vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...)` at ProductAPIClient.swift:122. This is the blocking JSON round-trip before any image starts loading on Pieces and on the saved Record — the two screens the first five minutes live on — so a homeowner on cellular feels it as 'the app is slow' before they can name why. One-line column list, ~10x smaller payload, in-repo decode struct defines the exact column set. Cheapest large perceived-speed win in the whole ledger: T0.

confirmed.title: vendors is anon-readable including internal trade notes
confirmed.where: GET /rest/v1/vendors?select=* with the shipped anon key
confirmed.evidence: 4 rows returned to anon, with a `notes` column carrying internal buyer commentary: "trade is good so are the tunes" (brooks and dunn), "terms are fine" (K & K). The app only ever needs vendors.name / made_in / brand_story via the products embed.
confirmed.fix: Narrow the anon SELECT policy to the three columns the embed needs, or move the embed behind a SECURITY DEFINER view that projects only those columns.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED verbatim. pg_policy on public.vendors: 'Allow anon read access to vendors', polcmd 'r', polroles {anon}, qual `true`. 4 rows; `select string_agg(notes,' | ') from vendors` returns exactly 'trade is good so are the tunes | terms are fine | ∅ | ∅'. anon also holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants on vendors (table privileges true) — worth folding into the fix, which the finding does not mention.
confirmed.judgeNote: Four rows, and the embed only ever needs name/made_in/brand_story — but the exposed `notes` column is internal buyer commentary in an informal voice, which reads badly if anyone ever looks. Rides along with A3-04's RLS pass at near-zero marginal cost, which is the only reason it is T1 rather than T2.

confirmed.title: No vendor is is_patina_catalog and only one product is patina_managed — the buyability gate is structurally closed
confirmed.where: public.products / public.vendors; create_direct_order body on Strata
confirmed.evidence: count(*) filter (where patina_managed) = 1; count from vendors where coalesce(is_patina_catalog,false) = 0. create_direct_order raises 'product % is not available for direct purchase' unless patina_managed OR the vendor is is_patina_catalog. So at most one product on production could ever be bought, and it is the Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp.
confirmed.fix: Comes free with a real seeded catalogue (A3-01) — set patina_managed or flag the catalog vendor. Check before anyone turns the direct-orders flag on for a tester.
confirmed.codeNote: Prod-verified to the row. `count(*) filter (where patina_managed) = 1` of 15 products, and the one row is id a7fa2107-8d2e-4131-8b8f-f5dd9826fdac, name 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp'. `count(*) from vendors where coalesce(is_patina_catalog,false) = 0` of 4 vendors. The gate quoted from `pg_get_functiondef(create_direct_order)` is verbatim: `IF NOT (v_product.patina_managed OR COALESCE(v_vendor_catalog, FALSE)) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'create_direct_order: product % is not available for direct purchase'`. testerVisible corrected to false for round one (flag OFF). Distinct root cause from A3-13/A3-14 — this one is catalogue data, not the unapplied migration, so applying 00540 alone does not open it.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed and correctly scoped as a gate on flipping direct-orders rather than on build 1 — with the flag off the buyability gate is never consulted. Worth recording alongside it: production carries 15 products total, of which 1 is patina_managed, so the catalogue is the thinner problem and the buyability gate is the second-order one. Both come free with a real seeded catalogue (A3-01). Do not flip direct-orders for any tester until this is checked — a Buy path that refuses on 14 of 15 pieces reads as broken, not as curated.

confirmed.title: The production category vocabulary cannot fill the app's six-category model — every catalog row is 'lighting'
confirmed.evidence: Category distribution on prod: decor 12, storage 1, lighting 1, chair 1. The app's ProductCategory is seating|tables|lighting|storage|decor|textiles with placeholderGradient keyed to all six. `chair` normalizes to .seating correctly (U39's fix is real and needed), but there is no `tables`, no `textiles`, and the only catalog-visible row is lighting — so a category filter or a gradient-variety pass has nothing to work with.
confirmed.fix: Fold into the catalogue seed (A3-01): cover all six categories, and normalize the stored vocabulary to the enum's raw values so `chair` stops needing a translation layer.
confirmed.codeNote: Distribution confirmed EXACTLY on Strata (decor 12, storage 1, lighting 1, chair 1; 15 rows). But the framing conflates the whole `products` table with what iOS can see. get_aesthete_matches defaults p_layer='catalog', filters `p.layer='catalog' AND p.status='published'`, and FORCES catalog when auth.uid() IS NULL — so the app-visible production catalogue is exactly ONE row: 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp' (lighting, layer=catalog, 0 images, price_retail 2000 = $20). Every other row is layer='personal'. So the six-category model is starved because the catalogue is one row, not because the vocabulary drifted. Corollary: the `chair` row (PH5 Pendant Lamp, personal, DRAFT) can never be returned by get_recommendations, so ProductCategory(normalizing:) earns its keep only on the direct-fetch paths (ProductAPIClient.swift:272, ProductModel.swift:96) — U39's fix is still needed, but not for the reason given. Line cite drifts: enum at ProductModel.swift:289-299, `init(normalizing:)` at 302-317. Wholly subsumed by A3-01.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from minor: the visible symptom is that four of the six filter chips at the top of Browse return 'Nothing here yet' on production, and chips are the first thing a shopper touches. Not two engineering tasks with A3-22 — one catalogue-seed pass (fold into A3-01) that covers all six categories and normalises the stored vocabulary to the enum's raw values. If that seed does not happen the app reads as a demo to every tester regardless of which code findings get fixed.

confirmed.title: published_at is NULL on all 15 products and quality_score on all catalog rows, so every piece renders as 'new arrival' and the two match-score defaults disagree
confirmed.where: public.products; get_recommendations tier CASE; ProductModel.swift (matchLabel, tier); ProductAPIClient RawProductWithVendor.toProduct
confirmed.evidence: count(*) filter (where published_at is not null) = 0 across all 15 rows. get_recommendations computes tier as: quality_score>=80 → designer_selection; published_at NOT NULL → style_match; ELSE new_arrival. With both NULL every row is new_arrival. Separately match_score from the RPC is round(m.score*100) while the direct-fetch path defaults to `quality_score ?? 50` — so the same piece shows a different match number depending on which screen opened it.
confirmed.fix: Set published_at and quality_score as part of the catalogue seed. Reconcile the two match-score defaults so one piece has one number.
confirmed.codeNote: All numbers re-run on Strata and confirmed: total 15, published_at NOT NULL = 0, quality_score NOT NULL = 0 (NULL on ALL 15, not just catalog rows). get_recommendations tier CASE is verbatim as quoted; match_score is `LEAST(100, GREATEST(0, round((m.score*100)::numeric)))`. Direct-fetch default confirmed at ProductAPIClient.swift RawProductWithVendor.toProduct(): `matchScore: quality_score ?? 50`. THREE additions worth carrying: (1) the same two paths also disagree on TIER — toProduct() computes `(quality_score ?? 0) >= 80 ? .designerSelection : .styleMatch` and can NEVER produce .newArrival, so the identical piece is 'new arrival' in the grid and 'style match' on detail; (2) with one catalog row on prod, 'every piece renders as new arrival' means one piece; (3) prod's get_recommendations still carries the PRE-00533 RETURNS TABLE (no brand, dimensions, lead_time_weeks), so Product.brand is nil on every grid row in production — which also disarms the resolvedMakerName brand fallback.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from minor on the first half: with published_at and quality_score NULL on every row, EVERY piece is badged 'new arrival', so the app's curation vocabulary carries no information — a tester sees ten identical tier labels and concludes nothing is actually curated. Second half is the data side of C-11 (the direct-fetch `quality_score ?? 50` default is the 50 in that finding's 73/57/50); fix C-11 in code and this in the seed, once each. Same seed pass as A3-21.

confirmed.title: Guest browsing writes to production: get_recommendations inserts a match_events row per anon call
confirmed.where: public.get_recommendations / get_aesthete_matches (both SECURITY DEFINER, anon EXECUTE granted)
confirmed.evidence: get_recommendations get-or-creates the neutral client_style_profiles row at a fixed session_key for anon callers, and get_aesthete_matches unconditionally INSERTs one match_events row per call carrying session_key, user_id and the full result payload. anon has EXECUTE on both (has_function_privilege true). Every guest home refresh is therefore an unauthenticated write to two production tables. I deliberately did not call the RPC in this lane for that reason.
confirmed.fix: Acceptable by design for telemetry, but add a rate limit or sampling gate before a public TestFlight — an anon caller with the shipped key can grow match_events without bound.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED statically without calling the RPC. pg_get_functiondef(get_recommendations) §3 get-or-creates the neutral client_style_profiles row at the fixed key ae460000-0000-4000-8000-00000000e057 for callers with no profile, and `match_events` appears in the bodies of BOTH get_recommendations (offset 2728) and get_aesthete_matches (offset 15710). Both are prosecdef=true with has_function_privilege('anon', …, 'EXECUTE') = true. match_events currently holds 129 rows. Every guest home refresh is an unauthenticated write to two prod tables.
confirmed.judgeNote: Acceptable telemetry by design at round-1 scale — an invited list of homeowners will not grow match_events meaningfully, and with one catalogue row nothing works anyway. It becomes a real concern only when the shipped key is in more hands than an invite list, so the sampling or rate-limit gate belongs with the decision to widen, not with build 1.

confirmed.title: 21 SECURITY DEFINER views, one RLS-disabled public table, and leaked-password protection off

confirmed.judgeNote: Adjusted on scope, not on facts: as written this is an unbounded chore (1,207 lints) and will either be dropped or eat a week. Most of the 21 security_definer_view hits are this codebase's deliberate co-member RLS pattern, and the 21 rls_enabled_no_policy hits are the intended fail-closed shape — the finding says as much. Cut the ticket to three concrete items: turn on leaked-password protection (one dashboard toggle, do this in the T1 pass), _comms_backfill_legacy_map, and the anon-executable share_room_scan/revoke_room_scan_access functions.

confirmed.title: Every RLS policy on every table the app reads re-evaluates auth.uid() per row
confirmed.evidence: auth_rls_initplan hits products ×10, saved_items ×5, projects ×5, invoices ×5, notification_preferences ×5, profiles ×4, comms_threads/messages ×8, rooms ×2, room_scans ×2, editorial_stories ×2. multiple_permissive_policies: projects 46, notification_preferences 45, profiles 30, invoices 17, rooms/room_scans/saved_items/notification_log 15 each. confirmed.fix: Wrap as `(select auth.uid())` in each policy and merge the duplicate permissive policies. One migration, after the catalogue seed lands — not before.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED with exact numbers. get_advisors(performance) on bkvcixdmuyejfzcijpdg returns lint counts {multiple_permissive_policies: 1147, auth_rls_initplan: 441, unused_index: 416, unindexed_foreign_keys: 334}. Per-table initplan matches the claim item for item: products 10, saved_items 5, projects 5, invoices 5, notification_preferences 5, profiles 4, rooms 2, room_scans 2, editorial_stories 2. Per-table multiple_permissive: projects 46, notification_preferences 45, profiles 30, invoices 17, saved_items/rooms/room_scans 15 each. Tiering to cut for THIS program: it is an L-effort prod DB migration, invisible at today's row counts, outside the iOS app, and the finding's own fix sketch says to do it after the catalogue seed lands.
confirmed.judgeNote: Agreed on every axis, including the finding's own timing advice: at 15 products and 24 profiles this is unmeasurable, and it is an L-effort production migration touching every RLS policy the app reads — precisely the change you do not make in the week you first put the app in strangers' hands. Queue it behind the catalogue seed.

confirmed.title: 'client', 'homeowner' and 'designer' are three words for two kinds of person in profiles.role
confirmed.evidence: Prod distribution: client 11, designer 8, homeowner 4, super_admin 1. handle_new_user honours only 'homeowner' and otherwise writes 'designer'. The iOS app writes 'homeowner' on the magic-link and password paths and nothing on Apple. The portals seed 'client'. Nothing reconciles the two consumer words, and the fallback for 'no hint' is the privileged role rather than the unprivileged one.
confirmed.fix: Pick one word, migrate the rows, and flip handle_new_user's COALESCE fallback to that word so an unlabelled signup is never a designer.
confirmed.codeNote: Code and migration halves both verified. 00313_handle_new_user_client_role_hint.sql honours only raw_user_meta_data.role = 'homeowner' and COALESCEs to 'designer'; AuthService.swift:437 (signUp) and :563 (signInWithOTP) stamp 'homeowner'; signInWithApple (:370, signInWithIdToken) passes no metadata, so an Apple signup lands 'designer'. AuthService.swift:168's "role": "client" is a PostHog identify property — a fourth use of the word, not a DB write. Prod row counts not re-verified. Flagging that the fix's second clause (flip the COALESCE fallback off the privileged role) carries more weight than the naming half and may deserve its own entry under prod-readiness.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severely understated as polish/not-tester-visible. VERIFIED: signInWithApple (AuthService.swift:354-382) passes NO role metadata — captureAppleName writes only display_name — so 00313's COALESCE lands profiles.role='designer' for every Apple sign-in. 00313's own header admits this ('OAuth… the previous default designer is preserved… a separate client-side follow-on'), and 00050:95-97 arms an account_created drip on role='designer'. A homeowner who taps the most prominent button on the welcome screen becomes a designer in production and may receive the designer onboarding drip. That is a live prod defect, not a vocabulary preference. T0 = pass the homeowner hint on the Apple (and Google) path; the client/homeowner word migration is T2. Belongs to the auth/prod-readiness lens — hand to V1 to confirm whether the 00050 sequence is actually armed on Strata. Also noted: AuthService.swift:168 tags PostHog identity role='client' while the DB gets 'homeowner', so analytics and the DB disagree on the same person.

confirmed.title: U38/U39 lineage: the marketplace returns zero pieces on production
confirmed.evidence: prod-verified read-only: `select count(*) from get_recommendations(null,null,20,0)` -> 0 rows; `get_aesthete_matches(p_session_key := 'ae460000-0000-4000-8000-00000000e057', p_limit := 50)` -> 0. public.products holds 15 rows (8 status='published'), but product_style_spectrum and v_aesthete_catalog_input hold ONE row each, so the matcher has nothing to return. The July U39 code fix is genuinely in (tolerant FailableDecodable decode at ProductAPIClient.swift:96-111, category normalized not thrown at ProductModel.swift:96-99, error rendered with retry at RecommendationsView.swift:253-255) — the lie is gone, but the blank remains, and it is now real rather than a decode bug. Every Companion 'recommendations' row and the quiz's fixed 'View Recommendations' CTA (StyleResultView.swift:47-52, U38's fix) land on this screen.
confirmed.fix: Run the aesthete catalogue pass over the 8 published products (or seed product_style_spectrum rows) so the matcher returns them. Separately, give the zero-result grid a 'still curating' state rather than a bare '0 pieces chosen for your space' count.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-verified read-only on Strata myself: `select count(*) from get_recommendations(null,null,20,0)` → 0; public.products = 15 rows, 8 published; public.product_style_spectrum = 1 row. No client-side fallback exists — ProductAPIClient.fetchRecommendations (ProductAPIClient.swift:39-70) calls only the RPC and returns whatever it gets, and withholdingUnresolvedMakers can only shrink that further, so the browse grid and the Daily Room picks are both empty on a TestFlight install. One caution on the proposed fix: the 8 published prod rows are not a shippable catalogue — they include a row literally named 'Find a piece—or ask about one.', 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp' (no image at all), and 'Line Credenza, Large – Design Within Reach' duplicated. Running the aesthete pass over them as-is would replace a blank grid with that.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed blocker and the single worst thing in this set: the app's entire first-five-minutes loop (intro -> style quiz -> 'View Recommendations' -> save) terminates on an empty grid for every tester. The quiz is the app's promise; an empty result is the app breaking that promise in the first two minutes, and no amount of polish elsewhere survives it. Adjusted because the fix sketch under-specifies the cause: lane P (P-36) measured the binding constraint as the RLS layer filter, not the matcher — products_catalog_select_anon USING (layer='catalog') yields anon_visible_total = 1, anon_published = 1, anon_with_images = 0, and that one row is 'Smoke Test Ceramic Lamp' at $20.00 with no photograph. Seeding product_style_spectrum over the 8 'published' rows will not help if those rows are not layer='catalog' and anon-readable. Plan this as ONE row with P-36: seed a real catalog-layer catalogue with images, then run the aesthete pass. Keep the 'still curating' zero-state regardless — it is the safety net if the seed slips, and '0 pieces chosen for your space' is the current copy.

confirmed.title: A4-03: every remote save 400s on prod — saved_items.price_cents_at_save missing
confirmed.evidence: prod-verified: saved_items columns are brand_name,created_at,id,image_url,name,notes,price_in_cents,product_id,room_id,source,updated_at,user_id — no price_cents_at_save (migration 00535 is not applied; the applied set jumps 00532 -> 00541). CreateSavedItemPayload encodes `price_cents_at_save` unconditionally on every save path (RecommendationsViewModel.swift:211, ProductDetailViewModel.swift:180), so PostgREST answers PGRST204/400 and RoomsAPIClient.createItem throws through ensureOK. The piece stays in SwiftData and the tester is shown SavedItemMirror.deferredNotice on every save.
confirmed.fix: Apply 00535 (with the rest of 00533-00540) to Strata. Fixing it client-side by omitting the field would undo SP-14's price-moved line.
confirmed.codeNote: Re-verified read-only: public.saved_items on Strata is exactly brand_name, created_at, id, image_url, name, notes, price_in_cents, product_id, room_id, source, updated_at, user_id — no price_cents_at_save. CreateSavedItemPayload declares it (RoomsAPIClient.swift:143) and every call site passes a non-optional Int, so the key is always in the body and PostgREST answers PGRST204/400. The finding misses a third path: ARPlacementViewModel.swift:79. Two calibrations that do not change the verdict: the tester is not stopped and is not shown a raw error — the piece persists in SwiftData and the copy is designed and honest ('Saved on this phone. We couldn't reach your account just now.', SavedItem.swift:145) — so the blocker rests on data durability (the account copy is never written; saves are lost on reinstall or a second device), which does meet the brief's 'data loss' bar. Fix is a prod migration (00533-00540), no app change.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed. Saving is the one thing the app asks a homeowner to do, and on production every single save 400s: the tester taps the heart, gets the deferred-sync notice every time, and nothing survives a reinstall or a second device. A tester who curates ten pieces and loses them has no reason to open build 2. The fix is an ops step, not app code — apply 00533-00540 to Strata — and it is already on the standing OWED list. Two cautions for the plan: a plain `supabase db push` drags the whole pending set (the applied ledger jumps 00532 -> 00541), so use the selective-apply procedure; and do NOT paper over it client-side by dropping price_cents_at_save, which silently undoes SP-14's price-moved line.

confirmed.title: A4-04: Delete Account cannot work on production (function + RPC both absent)
confirmed.evidence: prod-verified: `delete-account` does not appear in Strata's deployed edge functions, and public.purge_client_account (migration 00538) does not exist. The app's Delete Account row therefore calls a 404 function that would in turn call a missing RPC. SP-20 built this against Apple guideline 5.1.1(v), which requires in-app account deletion for any app that creates accounts.
confirmed.fix: Apply 00538, then `supabase functions deploy delete-account`. Until then the row is a dead destructive control and a review blocker.
confirmed.codeNote: Independently re-verified against Strata today. `list_edge_functions` on bkvcixdmuyejfzcijpdg returns 90 functions and `delete-account` is NOT among them. `select proname from pg_proc join pg_namespace ... where nspname='public' and proname in ('purge_client_account','mark_client_account_purge_complete')` returns []. The repo has both (supabase/migrations/00538_client_account_anonymize.sql, supabase/functions/delete-account/), so this is an un-shipped deploy, not missing code. App side confirmed: AccountDeletionService.swift:34 endpointPath = "/functions/v1/delete-account", :78 treats any non-2xx as failure, so the tester gets AccountDeletionService.failureCopy (:38). Matches the standing fact that 00533–00540 are still pending on prod. Correctly a beta-review/5.1.1(v) blocker.
confirmed.judgeNote: Facts stand (V1's prod probe). Adjusting the FRAMING, not the severity. Two things the title conflates: (a) it is not a TestFlight distribution blocker — external beta review rarely exercises deletion, and nothing stops build 1 shipping; (b) it IS an App Store submission hard-gate (5.1.1(v)) and, more urgently for testers, a destructive control that currently 404s. T0 because the fix is server-side (apply 00538 + `supabase functions deploy delete-account`) and needs no binary — so it costs the build nothing. Two judgment calls for the fix program: verify the RPC against a throwaway production account before enabling it, and if it cannot be verified in time, the safer build-1 move is to HIDE the row (also S) rather than ship a 404 destructive control. Sequencing matters — see C1-15.

confirmed.title: U24/U44: the flag-off Today root has no door to Browse pieces or to design help
confirmed.evidence: enum HomeBlock has no browse case and no designer-CTA case. HomeComposition.blocks(for:) emits only header / record / nextMove / designerSeat (engaged+ only) / roomHero|houseRail|startWithARoom / newThisWeek / savedSummary (requires savedPieceCount > 0) / story / signInLine. W2's R3 hygiene deleted MarketplaceLinksSection and WorkWithDesignerCTA — the two components the July U24 fix lived in. The Pieces tab that replaced them is behind `house-first`, OFF for a first-round tester. The only remaining door is CompanionAreaBuilders.homeItems:64 recommendationsRow, inside the unlabeled orb. W6's own walker recorded it: waves/w6/walk.md:147 'the flag-off root has no piece browse from Today'.
confirmed.fix: Either target `house-first` for testers (A4-12), or restore a Browse/Saved affordance and a 'Get design help' row to the flag-off composition — U24's ruling was permanent affordances at every tier.
confirmed.codeNote:
REAL, correctly located, app-attributable — citations are line-accurate (HomeBlock = TodayExperience.swift:196-211; blocks(for:) = :273-297; DailyRoomView content block chain = :265-362), and MarketplaceLinksSection / WorkWithDesignerCTA have zero hits anywhere under apps/mobile/Patina (deletion confirmed). But the title overstates on the Browse half and understates on the design-help half.

DESIGN-HELP HALF — CONFIRMED, and stronger than written: CompanionAreaBuilders.homeItems never calls designerRow at all. Its three conditional rows are messageDesignerRow (needs designerRelationship.isLive), requestRow (needs activeDesignRequest) and studioRow (needs tier >= .engaged); a discovering-tier tester gets [recommendations, collections?, spacesOrScan] + universal tail. So for the brief's first-round tester there is NO 'Get design help' affordance on the screen OR inside the orb. DailyRoomView.swift:514's presentDesignServices fires only from the .resumeDesignRequest next-move arm, which requires a pending draft. CompanionActionProvider.nudge(for: .heroFrame) returns nil (CompanionContextProvider.swift:283-286), so no pill supplies one either.

BROWSE HALF — narrow it. Three doors the finding misses or mischaracterises: (1) NEW THIS WEEK draws at newThisWeekFloor >= 3 (blocks(for:) :290) and each card routes to .pieceDetail (DailyRoomView.swift:333-345) — a real, supply-gated piece door on the flag-off root; (2) the Next Move card IS an explicit browse door once an active room holds zero items — the .exploreActiveRoom copy reads verbatim 'Browse Patina's edit and begin shaping the room.' and performRoomMove routes it to .roomEmergence, i.e. the same grid C-lane shot 11-dark-browse.png photographed at flags OFF; (3) the orb is not 'unlabeled' — CompanionPresentation.swift:204-226 gives the resting dock the caption 'Next steps' for a fresh user (or the studio attention hint). No browse/shop word, so the wayfinding point survives, but the orb is captioned.

CORRECTED CLAIM: on the flag-off Today root there is no FIRST-CLASS browse affordance — no persistent Browse row/button — so a fresh, roomless, discovering-tier tester reaches the marketplace only via the Companion orb ('Your recommendations' -> .emergence(nil)) or a supply-gated NEW THIS WEEK rail; and the design-request flow has no Today-level door at that tier at all, on screen or in the orb. Severity major and testerVisible both stand (both conversion surfaces are affected, and U24's ruling was permanent affordances at every tier), but it is not a blocker: the orb keeps a working browse path, so T1 rather than T0. Where/effort unchanged; fix sketch unchanged.
confirmed.judgeNote: Code facts hold. Verified TodayExperience.swift:196-211 (HomeBlock has no browse/designer case) and blocks(for:) 273-297 (emits exactly header/record/nextMove/designerSeat/roomHero|houseRail|startWithARoom/newThisWeek/savedSummary/story/signInLine); DailyRoomView.swift:265-362 renders only those. W6's walk quote is verbatim at waves/w6/walk.md item 14: 'the flag-off root has no piece browse from Today'. ADJUSTED on two points. (1) The design-help half OVERSTATES: ProfileView.swift:157 carries an ungated 'Get design help' row (coordinator.presentDesignServices(roomId: nil)) and the Studio pill DOES draw on the flag-off root — DailyRoomView.swift:262 passes showsStudioControl: !coordinator.isHouseFirstRoot, and W6's leave-state records 'W2 root (no tab bar, floating Companion orb, Studio 5 pill)'. So design help is two taps away (Studio pill -> scroll to YOUR PROFILE), not absent. (2) The browse half UNDERSTATES if anything: the orb's only piece door is recommendationsRow -> .emergence, which AppCoordinator/Coordinator.swift:138 resolves to RecommendationsView — a recommendations feed, not a catalog — and CompanionActionRows.swift:109-116 sets its hint to 'Take the quiz first' for exactly the first-round tester (roomCount 0, no style profile). NEW THIS WEEK is the only other piece surface and it needs newThisWeekCount >= 3 (newThisWeekFloor) and has no see-all footer (NewThisWeekRail.swift:71-77), so it can be absent and never leads anywhere but pieceDetail. Net: a homeowner's first five minutes on Today read 'this is a room-scanning app' — the catalog and the designer, the two things Patina is for, have no labeled front door on the landing screen; the surviving paths are an unlabeled floating orb whose piece row tells you to go take a quiz, and a 'Studio' pill a homeowner will not read as 'shop'. Severity major (not blocker: nothing crashes, nothing dead-ends, the app is navigable) but testerVisible YES and loud. TIER T0 for the browse half, and the fix must NOT be A4-12: the brief's own standing fact is that PostHog's cache is empty on first launch, so a TestFlight build-1 install is flag-off on launch 1 no matter who Kody targets — flag-targeting cannot reach the first five minutes, which is the exact window this finding is about. T0 slice = restore a permanent Browse/Saved affordance to HomeComposition.blocks (a HomeBlock case + a row in DailyRoomView, mirroring what the deleted MarketplaceLinksSection carried under U24), effort S-M. The 'Get design help' half is T1 — a working if buried path exists, and a Today-level CTA is a real improvement rather than a missing door. Second-order cost that justifies T0: build 1 exists to learn how the app reads, and shipping a home with no shopping door means the first round reports on the wrong product; that distorts the whole first-week signal, not just one screen.

'Target the testers in PostHog' CANNOT fix this: FeatureFlags resolves synchronously from PostHog's persisted payload, which is empty on a fresh install, so a targeted tester still gets flags-off for the entirety of their first session — precisely the first five minutes this audit is calibrated against. confirmed.codeNote: Every cited source checks out. waves/w6/integration.md:396-407 lists 'The account-switch walk was never driven … unit-verified only' as Fable's still-open item 1; integration.md:51 confirms the 72 `static let shared` enumeration; waves/w6/x3-notes.md:210 records that the in-process switch to james.okafor@example.com 'could not be driven: simulator input delivery died'. The seam exists on main — Patina/Core/State/SessionScope.swift (protocol + 11 participants, reset/refresh), AuthService.swift:93, DesignerThreadOpener.swift:20 names it explicitly. waves/w5/walk.md:33-46 records the original misfire exactly as summarised (server refused rpc_start_project_thread, nothing leaked, the send failed). Enrichment for the plan: this audit's lane B DID drive a local in-process account switch (research/B.md:281-289 — signed in as james.okafor@example.com, saw the first-launch tour re-run and change from 'Step 1 of 2' to 'Step 1 of 3'), but never exercised a designer-thread send afterwards, so the specific write-RPC seam is still unwalked. confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed as a coverage gap, but the framing understates it. This is not hygiene: W5 already observed the real user-facing failure (DesignerThreadOpener resolving a second account against the first account's project id after an in-process Sign Out — the send failed for the user; the server correctly refused the cross-tenant rpc, so there was no leak), X3 built the SessionScope reset against 72 `static let shared` holders, and the walk that would prove the fix was never driven because HID delivery on that clone was dead. So the state today is: a known-broken seam, a fix that compiles and unit-passes, and zero evidence it works in the app. The gap itself is invisible to a tester; the defect behind it is not, which is why it earns T1 over T2. Not T0: a round-one homeowner has exactly one account and will not switch on day one. It becomes urgent the moment Kody demos two accounts on one device, or a tester signs out and back in during the first week. Fix is a walk, not code: sign out, sign in as the second account, send from a piece — on a clone with a passing HID preflight (scan_ui, tap a known control, screenshot, confirm the screen changed) so a dead-input clone cannot manufacture a pass or a fail.

confirmed.title: "Designers Pick" is missing its apostrophe and a raw slug is shown as a tag

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/A.md (116 findings A-01…A-116, 786 lines) + /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/A/ledger.md (116 PNGs, one line each)
confirmed.codeNote: Real, but neither string exists in the app source — I grepped both. They are server badge/category slugs run through String.badgeDisplayName (ProductDetailBlocks.swift:193-202), which names exactly four badges ('fsc_certified', 'handcrafted', 'made_in_usa', 'sustainable') and default-arms everything else through `.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: " ").capitalized`. That is why 'designers_pick' renders 'Designers Pick' (no apostrophe to restore) and a hyphenated key renders 'Accent-Chair' (only '_' is replaced, and .capitalized capitalizes after a hyphen). So the `where` should be that default arm, not 'the PROVENANCE section' — the fix sketch ('map category keys to display names in one place') is exactly right. Note SurfaceKeys.swift:113 already documents the intended label as "Designer's Pick".
confirmed.judgeNote: Adjusted: these are not two fixes, they are ONE root cause — raw DB keys rendered as display copy through `.capitalized` (which replaces underscores but not hyphens, so 'accent-chair' survives as 'Accent-Chair', and 'designers_pick' loses its apostrophe). That is a CLASS problem: ~14 `.capitalized`-on-a-raw-key sites across product detail, decisions, invoices, rooms and profile (ProjectDetailView.swift:201 already warns against exactly this pattern, and SurfaceKeys.swift:113 documents the intended "Designer's Pick"). Fix the class with one display-name map, not two strings. T1 — visible on the flagship screen, but a map is more than a build-1 string edit.

confirmed.title: Notification rows have inconsistent anatomy and the unread tint does not share a margin

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/A.md (116 findings A-01…A-116, 786 lines) + /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/A/ledger.md (116 PNGs, one line each)

So it is not 'inconsistent anatomy' as a bug — it is two row kinds rendered identically apart from their missing metadata, which is the real polish complaint. The tint/separator half is confirmed in shots/A/45-bell-signedin.png: .background(...interactive.opacity(0.08)) is applied to the full-bleed row (:288) while the hairline is .padding(.leading, 78) (:290-291) — 78 pt ≈ 234 px at 3×, not the 178 px quoted. The MISSING TIMESTAMP on the Invoice and Proposal rows is the half a homeowner registers — a money row with no 'when' reads as unanchored, and it is the same defect surfacing in C-53 as a phantom 'Just now' in the AX label, so fix the model once and both resolve. confirmed.title: A grey band sits under the product action bar in the home-indicator safe area
confirmed.evidence: The action bar's cream background stops ~25 pt above the bottom edge and a darker grey strip fills the remainder; the bar does not extend into the safe area. The Companion panel shows the same band (21-companion-menu-open.png).

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/A.md (116 findings A-01…A-116, 786 lines) + /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/A/ledger.md (116 PNGs, one line each)

So the seam is genuine, but the band is a subtly darker cream — a shadow gradient — not 'a darker grey strip', and the gap is ~36 pt, not ~25 pt (it matches Self.pinnedActBottomInset = 36 in ProductDetailView.swift and the safe-area inset). The bar paints with .glassEffect(.regular, in: .rect) (ProductDetailBlocks.swift:211-220) inside the safe area while the page background fills the home-indicator strip beneath it, which is the seam. No homeowner will say 'the action bar does not extend into the home-indicator inset'; they will register that the app is slightly off, which is exactly the difference the Apple-Design-Award bar is about. confirmed.title: The splash wordmark never reaches full opacity before the splash is dismissed
confirmed.evidence: onAppear animates wordmarkOpacity 0→1 over .easeOut(duration: 2.0) and the strata lines over 1.0 s after a 0.5 s delay (finishing at 1.5 s), but the phase gate is splashMinimumDuration = 1.5. The brand moment is cut at 75 % of its own fade: 01-cold-t2.png shows PATINA as light grey, 01-cold-t12.png shows the Welcome screen's identical wordmark near-black.
confirmed.fix: Shorten the wordmark fade to ~0.8 s (or raise the gate) so the mark is fully drawn before the cross-fade begins.
confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/A.md (116 findings A-01…A-116, 786 lines) + /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/A/ledger.md (116 PNGs, one line each)
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed, and the evidence is stronger than the finding cites. SplashView.swift:44 animates wordmarkOpacity 0→1 with .easeOut(duration: 2.0); the strata lines finish at 1.5 s (:50, 1.0 s after a 0.5 s delay); AppCoordinator.splashMinimumDuration = 1.5 (:81). The decisive frame is 01-cold-t3.png, which the finding does not use: it captures the cross-fade with BOTH wordmarks in a single frame — the splash's PATINA mid-screen is markedly lighter than the Welcome screen's PATINA above it, at the exact instant the splash is being dismissed. That is direct same-frame proof the mark never reaches full opacity, better than the t2-vs-t12 comparison the finding offers (which compares a mid-animation frame to a settled one). Canonical for the wordmark-fade cluster; R-17 folds in here.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised polish→minor. Confirmed in shots/A/01-cold-t2.png: 'PATINA' renders as pale grey against cream, then shots/A/01-cold-t12.png shows the same wordmark near-black on Welcome — the brand mark visibly jumps in weight as the splash hands off. The mechanism (2.0 s fade cut by a 1.5 s phase gate) means the app never once shows its own name at full strength. That is above pure polish for a brand-led product: R-17 independently read the same frame as 'a blank white screen', which is exactly how a tester will describe it. S fix (shorten the fade to ~0.8 s; do not raise the gate — slower launch is the worse trade). T1, bundled with A-01.

confirmed.title: A deleted room stays in Studio and the room count never updates
confirmed.where: Studio after deleting 'Audit Room B' — shots/B/48-signedin-studio.png, 49-studio-scroll1.png, 57-studio-bottom.png

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/B.md (356 lines) · shot ledger /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/ledger.md (85 rows) · 88 PNGs in /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed in shots/B/57-studio-bottom.png (deleted 'Audit Room B' still carded under YOUR ROOMS long after the delete) and pinned in code with a sharper mechanism than the finding gives. ProfileViewModel.loadData (Features/Profile/ViewModels/ProfileViewModel.swift:100-113) is a one-shot `context.fetch` into plain stored arrays `rooms` / `roomCount`; ProfileView calls it only from `.onAppear` (Features/Profile/Views/ProfileView.swift:177-179), and a tab root that stays mounted keeps the pre-delete snapshot. The asymmetry the finding senses is real and exact: YourSpacesView.swift:18 uses a live `@Query(sort: \RoomModel.createdAt, order: .reverse)`, so Spaces self-heals and Studio does not. RoomStore.delete does `context.delete(room); save()`, so the write itself is fine. Fix = make ProfileView use @Query, not a refetch.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified in shots/B/48, /49, /57: after a confirmed delete, Studio still says '2 ROOMS' and still renders 'Audit Room B'. Distinct root cause from B-04 (cache invalidation, not navigation) but the same tester story, and together they are what makes delete read as broken rather than merely awkward. The control account (James, 0 ROOMS) proves the stat is live, so this is a missed invalidation, not a hardcoded number. S effort. Ship both halves in build 1 or leave delete out of the tester's tour.

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/B.md (356 lines) · shot ledger /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/ledger.md (85 rows) · 88 PNGs in /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/

RoomSettingsView's delete does `RoomStore(context:).delete(room)` then `coordinator.goBack()`, which pops onto RoomProjectView, whose room lookup now misses and renders `notFoundState` (Features/Rooms/Views/RoomProjectView.swift:150-175). confirmed.judgeNote: Verified in shots/B/47-after-delete.png: a full-screen 'This room isn't on this phone / It may have been removed.' with a 'Your rooms' button, one second after the tester tapped Delete and confirmed. Two failures at once — the destructive action strands you on a dead screen instead of returning to the list, and the copy hedges ('may have been') about something the app just did itself. A tester's mental model after this is 'delete is broken and the app lost my room.' Creating a throwaway room and deleting it is a top-three thing a first-round tester does. However PatinaTabBar exists only under HouseFirstRoot (ContentView.swift:149-153, `coordinator.isHouseFirstRoot`), and house-first is a PostHog flag that is OFF on a first-launch TestFlight Release build per the brief — a first-round tester has no tab bar to re-tap. testerVisible should be false for round one.
confirmed.judgeNote: The observation is right and the diagnosis of tab-state preservation is a nice catch, but testerVisible must flip to false for this round: with flags off there is no tab bar in the app — ContentView.swift:149 only reaches HouseFirstRoot when isHouseFirstRoot is true, and PatinaTabBar has no other call site. So no round-one tester can re-tap an active tab. Genuine polish once house-first ships (scroll-to-top on re-tap is an iOS expectation), and it pairs naturally with the C6-39 tab-bar work. T2.

'LEAH WILL SEE THE PIECE AND / THE PRICE' wrapping and the product action bar left half-visible under the panel's bottom edge are craft, not comprehension. It is a bundle of four copy/layout items; all are S and all belong in build 2. The first-person/third-person half is the same decision as C5-22 — resolve once, apply to both.

confirmed.title: The notification pre-permission sheet has excellent copy in a badly composed layout
confirmed.evidence: The bell sits 36% down an otherwise empty sheet, ~500 px separates the body from the button, and left-aligned text sits above centred buttons. Copy: 'Before we interrupt you / We'll tell you when your designer sends something that needs you — a decision, a proposal, or an invoice. Nothing else.'
confirmed.fix: Centre the block vertically (or top-align it with the buttons pinned to the bottom) and align the buttons to the text.
confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/B.md (356 lines) · shot ledger /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/ledger.md (85 rows) · 88 PNGs in /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/
confirmed.codeNote: Both stated layout defects are wrong. PushPrimerView.swift:31-67 is Spacer(minLength:0) / block / Spacer(minLength:0) / button group — two equal spacers, so the block is vertically CENTRED in the space above the buttons, which is what shots/B/33-signedin-today.png shows (~510 px void above, ~470 below). And 'left-aligned text above centred buttons' is wrong: PatinaButton is .frame(maxWidth: .infinity), so the primary button's LEFT EDGE lands on exactly the same PatinaSpacing.lg padding as the text (measurable in the shot); only its label is centred, which is standard. The one genuine nit that survives: a single short screen of copy is presented at full sheet height, leaving two large voids — a .presentationDetents([.medium]) (or .fraction) would fit the content. Keep polish, corrected note.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified in shots/B/33-signedin-today.png, and I am softening one claim: the alignment complaint is overstated. A full-width capsule with a centred label above a centred text link, under left-aligned copy, is a standard and perfectly respectable iOS sheet idiom — Apple ships it. The genuine defect is vertical composition: roughly the top third of the sheet is dead space above the bell, and a second void separates the body from the buttons, so the whole thing reads as a layout that was never composed. Worth doing precisely because the copy is the best writing in the app ('Before we interrupt you… Nothing else.') and currently the layout is undercutting it at the exact moment you are asking for permission. S, build 2.

confirmed.title: The 'Add a new room' sheet mixes three background materials and two icon systems
confirmed.where: Add a new room sheet — shots/B/39-add-room.png
confirmed.evidence: A translucent blurred strip above the grabber, cream behind the two rows, then a grey band from y≈740 pt to the bottom edge inside the same sheet. 'Scan with camera' has a 90 pt tan tile with a ◎ glyph; 'Enter manually' has a bare blue-grey 📐 emoji with no tile.
confirmed.fix: Give the sheet one opaque background at a fixed detent and use the same tile treatment for both rows.
confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/B.md (356 lines) · shot ledger /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/ledger.md (85 rows) · 88 PNGs in /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/B/
confirmed.codeNote: Verified in shots/B/39-add-room.png and pinned to NewRoomSheet.swift:14-52. The sheet paints `PatinaColors.Background.primary` on a VStack that only claims its intrinsic height, and declares neither .presentationDetents nor .presentationBackground — so the host sheet's own material shows above and below the cream band, producing the three bands the finding describes. It also hand-draws a Capsule grabber at :15-19 instead of .presentationDragIndicator. One nuance on the icons: the code does pass an iconBackground for both rows (:29-31 clay, :39-41 Background.secondary), so the manual row is not literally tile-less — Background.secondary is simply near-invisible against the cream, which reads as no tile.
