confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from minor. Verified in shots/B/39-add-room.png and confirmed in NewRoomSheet.swift:28-45 — the 'icons' are literal text glyphs, icon: "◎" and icon: "📐", not SF Symbols or assets. One sits in a designed tan tile, the other is a bare blue-grey emoji. Add three background bands (blurred strip with ghost content bleeding through above the grabber, cream body, a grey dead band filling the bottom fifth from a detent mismatch) and this is the app's front door to its signature feature looking like a wireframe. The brief's bar names 'no placeholder' explicitly, and an emoji standing in for an icon is the textbook case. S effort, high visibility-per-hour — this is the cheapest large gain in the area.

confirmed.title: Companion orb is invisible in dark mode — hardcoded fill, 1.15:1 against the page
confirmed.evidence: Orb fill sampled (44,41,38) in BOTH appearances. Light page bg (250,247,242) → 13.53:1. Dark page bg (33,30,27) → 1.15:1. Only the 7.4:1 glyph inside reads; the disc has no border, no shadow, no elevation. With flags OFF this orb is the app's ONLY navigation hub.
confirmed.fix: Give the orb an adaptive fill (invert to a light disc in dark mode) or add a border/shadow token. Same fix covers the Companion panel fill, which is the identical literal.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed on shots/C/06-dark-launch-2.0s.png and again on shots/C/09-dark-spaces.png and /50-flagson-dark-tabroot.png: in dark mode the collapsed dock is a near-invisible disc — only the three-line glyph inside reads, and the disc has no border, no shadow and no elevation. Consistent with PatinaShadows (all tokens hard-coded Color(hex:"5C4A3C"), see C3-31) having no dark variant. Blocker severity holds for round 1 specifically: with every flag OFF this orb is the only navigation hub, so a tester in dark mode has no visible way in.
confirmed.judgeNote: Downgrading blocker to major on evidence, not on principle: shots/C/06-dark-launch-2.0s.png shows the 7.4:1 glyph clearly legible, so a dark-mode tester can still find and tap the hub — they are not stranded. But at 1.15:1 the disc has vanished and the glyph floats as an unexplained artifact over the house rail, which reads as a rendering bug. One adaptive token, effort S, on the app's only navigation affordance with flags off. Unambiguous T0.

confirmed.title: Companion status line is dark-on-dark in dark mode (1.11:1) while the title stays white
confirmed.evidence: Panel fill is the same (44,41,38) in both appearances and the title "Where to next?" stays white in both. The subtitle "5 things need your eye." measures brightest (193,190,185) = 7.8:1 in light, but its whole box maxes at (44,41,38) / darkest (36,33,30) = ~1.11:1 in dark. Still 1.11:1 with Increase Contrast ON (42-a11ytoggles-companion.png).
confirmed.fix: The panel is a fixed dark surface; the subtitle uses a colour that flips with the system appearance. Pin the subtitle to the panel's own on-dark secondary token.
confirmed.codeNote: REAL, and I pinned the exact line the lane inferred: CompanionHearthView.swift:402 styles the panel detail `.foregroundStyle(PatinaColors.Text.inverse.opacity(0.72))`. PatinaColors.swift:121-123 defines Text.inverse as `patinaDynamic(light: offWhite, dark: DarkPalette.background)`, i.e. #211E1B in dark — over the static charcoal panel (Background.dark = #2C2926, PatinaColors.swift:106/32) the 0.72 composite is (36,33,30), byte-for-byte the 'darkest (36,33,30)' the lane measured; I recompute WCAG at 1.108:1. Title stays legible because line 396 uses static `PatinaColors.offWhite`. The 'still 1.11:1 with Increase Contrast ON' claim is independently corroborated in research/C.md (colorSchemeContrast → 0 hits app-wide). ADJUSTMENT: severity blocker → major. Per the brief's own scale, blocker = cannot proceed / crash / data loss / beta-review blocker; an illegible status line is 'a tester notices and judges the app unfinished'. Keeping it T0 regardless.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity blocker→major by the brief's definition (invisible text, not a stopper). Confirmed from crop-dark-companion-header.png: '5 things need your eye.' is unreadable charcoal-on-charcoal while 'Where to next?' directly above stays white, so the Companion's opening line — the app's signature voice moment — simply vanishes for any tester whose phone is in dark mode, and stays vanished with Increase Contrast on. S fix (pin the subtitle to the panel's own on-dark token). Ships in build 1 with C-03.

confirmed.title: The fixed Companion orb and its caption overprint live content on every scrollable screen
confirmed.evidence: Orb {{169,724},{64,64}} + unlabeled caption container {{0,720},{402,120}} are fixed, and content is not inset for them. Measured collisions: composer — "5 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE" printed straight across the "Type a message…" placeholder and the orb breaks the composer's top divider; Studio — printed across "$4,250.00 remaining / Due Sep 6" (Invoice row y 747.3–828.7 vs orb y 724–788) and across "What's been bi[lled] and what's been paid"; Browse — covers the bottom 30 pt of both row-2 cards, eating the leading "r" of "room-aware edit"; Today @ XXXL — strikes through "Meadow Linen Sectional shippe[d]".
confirmed.fix: Add a bottom safe-area inset equal to the orb+caption height to every scroll container, or move the caption inside the orb. Note the flags-ON root has none of this because the orb becomes a tab.
confirmed.codeNote: The collisions are REAL and I re-verified two of them in the pixels: shots/C/26-dark-messages.png shows '5 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE' printed straight across the 'Type a message…' placeholder with the orb breaking the composer's top divider, and shots/R/00-preflight-before.png shows the orb cutting 'Leah Hart[well]' / 'Aspen Loft Re[...]' on the designer-seat card at DEFAULT text size. shots/C/ledger.md independently records the Studio, Browse, Room and XXXL-Today collisions. But the MECHANISM AND FIX ARE WRONG. (a) 'content is not inset for them' is false: ContentView.swift:185 applies `.companionHearthReservation(...)`. (b) The real faults are three: the reservation is 20 pt SHORT of the dock — CompanionSafeArea.swift:21 reservedHeight = 64+36+20 = 120 vs :40 dockHeight = 64+4+44+28 = 140, and the file's own comment at :33-38 admits '120 predates the caption and is 20 short of it, which is why a screen could satisfy the reservation and still be covered'; it is applied to the NavigationStack and per the same file's comment does not reach pushed destinations (Messages, Studio, Browse, Room, product); and most importantly a safeAreaInset only moves a scroll view's RESTING position, so content still travels under the dock while scrolling — which is exactly what both shots capture. (c) Therefore the proposed fix ('add a bottom safe-area inset equal to the orb+caption height to every scroll container') CANNOT solve what the shots show; the codebase already ruled the correct answer for this class — the dock yields to `.minimal` (CompanionSafeArea.swift:95-135, CompanionOverlay.swift:172-186). Route the fix through that ruling, not through a bigger inset. Severity blocker → major (tester can still scroll and act); tier stays T0 — this is the most-repeated visible defect in the app.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity blocker→major: nothing crashes and the tester can proceed, so it fails the brief's blocker test — but this is the highest-impact item in the area and the one that decides whether the app reads finished. Verified in shots/R/00-preflight-before.png: at rest on the signed-in home, before any scroll, the orb covers 'Leah Hart[well]' and 'Aspen Loft Re[novation]' — the tester's own designer and their own project — and the caption collides with the 'YOUR HOUSE' eyebrow. shots/C/26-dark-messages.png: '5 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE' is printed straight through the 'Type a message…' placeholder and the orb breaks the composer's divider. Decisive point for tiering: this is the flags-OFF root, which is exactly what a first-round TestFlight tester gets on first launch; internal walks done with house-first ON (orb becomes a tab) never see any of it, which is why it survived to now. T0. If the M-sized global inset threatens build 1, the cheap 80% is: move the caption inside the orb and inset only Today, the message composer and Studio.

confirmed.title: Four "?" controls at three sizes on one header; three share the identical label "More information"
confirmed.evidence: AX tree: questionmark.circle {{155.3,118},{44,44}} "More information"; YourSpacesView.HelpButton {{250,121},{36,36}} "Help"; questionmark.circle {{294,118.7},{44,44}} "More information"; questionmark.circle {{338,194.7},{44,44}} "More information". VoiceOver says "More information, button" three times with nothing to distinguish them.
confirmed.fix: Collapse to one help affordance per screen; give any remaining ones distinct labels naming their subject.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed in code and plainly visible in shots/B/38-signedin-spaces.png. YourSpacesView.swift:71, :131 and :158 are three `HelpInfoIcon`s, all inheriting the default `accessibilityLabel: "More information"` and hint "Shows additional information." (HelpInfoIcon.swift:73-74, :96-97), at sizes 14 / 14 / 12; plus YourSpacesView.swift:139-152 `YourSpacesView.HelpButton` (17pt symbol, 36×36, label "Help"). Four help affordances at three visual sizes in one header — the screenshot makes this read as unfinished even with VoiceOver off.
confirmed.judgeNote: The sighted half — four help affordances at three different sizes on one header — is what a tester judges; the three identical 'More information' labels are the a11y half of the same fix. Collapsing to one '?' per screen also dissolves two of C3-28's three call sites, so sequence this first. Overlaps the visual-system lane: fix once, not twice.

confirmed.title: Dynamic Type breaks headline text mid-word — "Good / afternoo / n." at XXXL, six fragments at AX sizes
confirmed.evidence: XXXL: "Good / afternoo / n." AX-XXXL: "TUESDA / Y · / SEP 1" and "Go / od / aft / er / no / on." filling the whole screen; "Wher / e to / next?" and "Your recomme / ndations" in the Companion; "Your / Space / s" on Your Spaces. Cause: display text sits in containers whose width is fixed by sibling chrome (bell, "?", the "Studio 5" pill, the "+") that does not reflow, so SwiftUI breaks the word rather than the layout.
confirmed.fix: Let the header stack switch to a vertical layout above .xxLarge (ViewThatFits / dynamicTypeSize check), and add minimumScaleFactor to the display strings.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified by reading both shots. shots/C/30-xxxl-today.png shows 'Good / afternoo / n.' broken mid-word; shots/C/35-ax3xl-today.png shows 'TUESDA / Y · / SEP 1' and 'Go / od / aft / er / no / on.' filling the screen. The stated mechanism is visibly correct: in both shots the bell, the '?' and the 'Studio 5' pill hold their row width (DailyGreetingHeader.swift:90-125), leaving the greeting a ~200pt column. Note the XXXL shot also shows collateral overlap not in the finding — '5 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE' strikes through a divider and the companion mark sits on 'Meadow Linen Sectional shipped'.
confirmed.judgeNote: The Dynamic Type finding most likely to actually reach a round-1 homeowner: XXXL is the standard slider max, no accessibility toggle required, and plenty of 45+ users already live there. 'Good / afternoo / n.' on the first screen after auth reads as broken, not as large. minimumScaleFactor is nearly free even if the ViewThatFits work slips.

confirmed.title: Bold Text and Increase Contrast have no effect on the app at all
confirmed.evidence: Pixel diff with identical content: the greeting region and the MOVED body region are byte-identical (0 differing pixels) with both toggles on; the one row that differs at all differs by 3.6% which the 2x crop shows is anti-aliasing. Source: legibilityWeight → 0 hits, colorSchemeContrast → 0 hits, reduceTransparency → 0 hits, differentiateWithoutColor → 0 hits across all Patina Swift. Consequence: the 2.66:1 meta text and the 1.11:1 Companion subtitle stay exactly as illegible with Increase Contrast on.
confirmed.fix: Add @Environment(\.colorSchemeContrast) and \.legibilityWeight branches to the colour and font tokens; add \.accessibilityReduceTransparency to the material surfaces.
confirmed.codeNote: Source half fully confirmed and decisive: `legibilityWeight`, `colorSchemeContrast`, `reduceTransparency` and `differentiateWithoutColor` each return ZERO hits across all of Patina + PatinaDesignKit. Two corrections. (1) 'No effect at all' overstates: surfaces built on system fonts do bold automatically without app code — FirstLaunchTour uses .caption/.headline/.body, and the 127 `.font(.system(size:))` sites are mostly SF Symbols. The accurate claim is that Patina's own custom-font stack (Inter/Playfair/DM Mono) and hand-rolled palette never branch on these values, so both toggles are inert wherever Patina's typography and colour are used — which is nearly everywhere. (2) The pixel-diff proof does not reproduce: my own diff of shots/C/40-reducemotion-today.png vs 41-a11ytoggles-today.png gives 41,221 differing pixels across bands up to full-row width with mean channel delta 244 — content drift between two launches, not anti-aliasing. The '0 differing pixels' claim should be dropped; the grep is what carries this finding.
confirmed.judgeNote: Down from major. A custom-font, hand-tokened app ignoring Bold Text and Increase Contrast is invisible to a tester — nothing looks broken, it simply fails to respond, and most non-system-font apps behave the same way. Sequencing matters more than severity: fix the base palette (C6-11/12/13) first, because that removes most of the reason a user would reach for Increase Contrast, then re-measure what is left.

confirmed.title: Settings row icons are focusable and labelled with raw SF Symbol names — "hand.tap", "circle.lefthalf.filled", "brain.head.profile"
confirmed.evidence: AXImage nodes: hand.tap → AXLabel "hand.tap"; circle.lefthalf.filled → AXLabel "circle.lefthalf.filled"; brain.head.profile → AXLabel "brain.head.profile". Two more carry duplicated or wrong labels: bell → "Notifications" (same as the row text and the switch), antenna.radiowaves.left.and.right → "Cellular Data" while the row says "Upload scans on cellular". Net effect: every preferences row is announced two or three times.
confirmed.fix: .accessibilityHidden(true) on all decorative row icons; make the row a single accessibility element combining label + switch value.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed at every cited line. SettingsView.swift:119 icon "hand.tap", :127 icon "antenna.radiowaves.left.and.right", :247 `Image(systemName: "brain.head.profile")`, :295 `Image(systemName: "circle.lefthalf.filled")` — none carries `.accessibilityHidden(true)`, and no row applies `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, so each unlabelled SF Symbol announces its raw symbol name and every row is spoken two or three times. `settingsToggleRow` (:393) puts `.accessibilityLabel(label)` on the Toggle (:415), which is the duplicated-'Notifications' case.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raw SF Symbol names as labels ('hand.tap', 'brain.head.profile') plus rows announced two or three times. Same 'hide decorative iconography, label the control, combine the row' pass as C-09/C-36 — bundle all three so Settings is done once.

confirmed.title: Every product card is announced as a "pop up button", and its rotor actions duplicate ("Save" and "Save to favorites")
confirmed.evidence: Cards are role AXPopUpButton / role_description "pop up button" e.g. "Heirloom Oak Dining Table by Nordic Atelier, $4,200, 57% match", while the hint says "Double-tap to view details." custom_actions = ["Skip","Save","Save to favorites","More actions"] — two actions with the same apparent meaning. The visible heart and "…" buttons are not separate AX elements, so the sighted and VoiceOver affordances do not match.
confirmed.fix: Use .isButton, drop the duplicate Save action, and expose the heart's saved/unsaved state as an AXValue.
confirmed.codeNote: Real, but the mechanism and fix in the finding are both wrong — correct them before handing this to a builder. The card is ALREADY a `Button` (RecommendationsView.swift:286-289), so `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` is a no-op. The 'pop up button' role comes from `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` at :318 unioning the nested `Menu` (menuButton, :521-542) into the card's element; the duplicate action pair is that same combine absorbing saveButton's label 'Save to favorites' (:517) alongside the explicit `.accessibilityAction(named: "Save")` at :326. Fix is to hide the nested save/menu controls from the combine (or switch to `children: .contain`), not to re-declare the trait. Canonical for this root.
confirmed.judgeNote: Down from major on tester impact — no sighted consequence. Canonical for the product-card role (B-31 is the twin). One thing to actually investigate rather than relabel: 'Save' and 'Save to favorites' appearing as two custom actions suggests a genuinely duplicated action wired in code, which is worth a look beyond the a11y fix.

confirmed.title: The same product shows three different match scores in one session: 73%, 57%, 50%
confirmed.evidence: Pieces tab card AX label "…$4,200, 73% match"; room-scoped grid card AX label "…$4,200, 57% match"; product detail renders the pill "50% match". Same piece, same session, one tap apart.
confirmed.fix: Compute the match once against a single scope and pass it through, or label each score with its scope ("73% for your home / 57% for the Guest Bedroom").
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed, and the mechanism is now fully pinned — the three numbers come from three different sources, only two of which are scores. 73% = unscoped get_recommendations. 57% = the same RPC with p_room_id set, which turns on the t_context term (_aesthete_context_term over the room's width/length) and re-weights w_avail, so a genuinely different number. 50% is NOT a score at all: the product-detail path is fetchProduct(id:) → RawProductWithVendor.toProduct(), which sets `matchScore: quality_score ?? 50`, and quality_score is NULL on every seeded row AND on all 15 production rows — so EVERY product detail opened by id or deep link shows exactly 50%, on prod as well as locally. Lane A independently hit the same contradiction (shots/A/18-product-detail.png: card 41%, detail 50%). Fix sketch is right; it should also say the detail number must stop being a constant.
confirmed.judgeNote: 73% → tap → 50% on the same piece one tap apart is the trust-killer of the pair: a number that changes when you touch it reads as the app making it up. Confirmed adjacent to A3-22 — the 50 is the direct-fetch `quality_score ?? 50` default landing on a NULL column. Fix it with A-34 as one decision (compute once, against one scope, present as a band); scope-labelling the two numbers is the worse answer because it asks a homeowner to hold two mental models.

confirmed.title: The message thread has no header at all — the tester is never told who they are messaging
confirmed.evidence: The complete AX tree is: Back, heading "TUESDAY · SEP 1", StaticText "Project conversation opened.", the composer, Send, plus the orb. No title, no "Leah Hartwell", no avatar — after arriving from a button literally labelled "Message your designer".
confirmed.fix: Add a conversation header with the designer's name, avatar and project.
confirmed.codeNote: Code-confirmed, not just AX-confirmed. ThreadDetailView.swift:70 is literally `.patinaScreen(title: nil)`, and the comment at :66-69 concedes it: "This screen has no in-body header to source a title from … a per-thread title is a follow-up." PatinaScreenChrome.swift:69-71 hides the system nav bar entirely and draws a title only `if let title`, so with nil the screen has a back chevron and nothing else. shots/C/26-dark-messages.png shows exactly that: chevron, "TUESDAY · SEP 1", one line of text. Correctly located, correctly severed.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed and it is a known deferral, not an oversight: ThreadDetailView.swift:65-68 carries the comment 'chrome title left nil rather than inventing unsanctioned copy; a per-thread title is a follow-up' and passes .patinaScreen(title: nil). That reasoning was right when the copy was unsanctioned; it is wrong to ship. The tester arrives from a button that names a person and lands on an anonymous page — combined with C-14 and C9-05 the whole first frame reads as a stub someone forgot to finish. These three are one edit in one file, which is why all three are T0 rather than one being held back.

confirmed.title: The message thread's only content is a system log line, "Project conversation opened."
confirmed.evidence: Verbatim, the sole message body. There is no designed empty state; ~600 pt of dead space follows before the composer.
confirmed.fix: Replace with a real empty state ("Say hello to Leah — she usually replies within a day") and suppress the audit line.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed on both ends. The string is server-seeded: supabase/migrations/00103_comms_rpcs.sql:167 (and 00540:702) INSERT `'Project conversation opened.', TRUE` into comms_messages when rpc_start_project_thread creates the thread, and MessagingAPIClient.swift:228 documents it. ThreadDetailView renders any `message.system` row as a centred muted caption (:164-172) with no filter, so the audit row IS the content. Dead space measured off the shot: content ends ~137 pt, composer top ~782 pt — ~645 pt, so the finding's "~600 pt" is if anything conservative. Note for the fixer: suppress client-side only — the designer portal reads the same row.
confirmed.judgeNote: Upgraded in certainty, not severity: this is PRODUCTION reality, not a local-seed artifact. supabase/migrations/00103_comms_rpcs.sql:167 (re-emitted at 00540_direct_orders_attribution.sql:702) does `VALUES (v_thread, NULL, 'Project conversation opened.', TRUE)` inside thread creation, and MessagingAPIClient.swift:228 documents it. Every first-round tester who taps 'Message your designer' on a project therefore lands on a screen whose entire content is a database audit line written in the passive voice. That is the single most developer-smelling string a homeowner will meet in the first five minutes, and it sits on the app's signature promise. Server-side suppression is not required for build 1 — ThreadDetailView already routes message.system to a separate row type, so the client can drop or replace this one string locally.

confirmed.title: The message composer has no accessibility label and exposes its placeholder as the field's value
confirmed.evidence: type AXTextField, AXLabel null, AXValue "Type a message…". VoiceOver announces an empty field as though it already contains text. The field is also only 17 pt tall.
confirmed.fix: .accessibilityLabel("Message") and use a real placeholder rather than a value; raise the tap target to 44 pt.
confirmed.codeNote: One of three claims survives. CONFIRMED: ThreadDetailView.swift:266 `TextField("Type a message…", text: $viewModel.draft, axis: .vertical)` has no `.accessibilityLabel` — real defect, one-line fix. REFUTED: placeholder-as-AXValue on an empty text field is standard UIKit/SwiftUI behaviour that every iOS app exhibits, not a Patina bug. REFUTED: 'only 17 pt tall' mis-reads the AX text frame — the field carries `.padding(.vertical, 10)` and `.padding(.horizontal, 14)` before its background (:271-273), so the tappable region is ~37pt (still under 44, but not 17), and the send button is already correct at `.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)` (:281).
confirmed.judgeNote: Split it. The 17pt composer tap target is sighted, and designer-to-homeowner messaging is a core product promise — a message field you can barely hit is felt in week one, so take that with C6-23. The missing label and placeholder-as-value are T2 with C6-10.

confirmed.title: The greeting "?" tooltip clips its own copy at the top AND the bottom, and the trigger is unreachable by VoiceOver
confirmed.evidence: The popover's text node is {{53.7,180.8},{194.7,86.3}} — 86.3 pt of text inside a ~75 pt bubble, vertically centred, so both ends are cut. Verbatim string: "Today keeps Patina focused: one useful next move, one editorial story, and one active room." On screen "Today keeps Patina" is half-cut by the bubble's top edge and "and one active room." is cut off below it. The trigger is absent from the Today AX tree entirely (only DailyRoomView.HelpButton appears), so VoiceOver cannot reach it. The bubble is also translucent enough that "Good afternoon." and "NEEDS YOU" bleed through.
confirmed.fix: Size the bubble to its content, make it opaque, and either give the trigger a real accessibility label or delete it (it duplicates the "?" 100 pt away).
confirmed.codeNote: Read shots/C/07-dark-greeting-help.png myself: the bubble visibly clips 'Today keeps Patina' at the top edge and 'and one active room.' below it, and it is translucent enough that 'Good afternoon.' and the NEEDS YOU rows read straight through it. The string is verbatim in DailyGreetingHeader.swift:76-79. Cause is code-visible: HelpTooltip's popover content (HelpTooltip.swift:113-127) sets only `.frame(maxWidth: 240)` and `.presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)` — no presentationSizing and no height, so the popover takes a default height the text overflows. The VoiceOver half is supported by contrast rather than assumption: the identical `questionmark.circle` / 'More information' element DOES appear in the Your Spaces AX tree three times (C.md:93-96) but is absent from Today's, and the one structural difference is DailyGreetingHeader.swift:85-88 wrapping the greeting VStack in `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` + `.accessibilityLabel("Today")`. The trigger itself is labelled (HelpInfoIcon.swift:97-99), so the container wrapper is where to look.
confirmed.judgeNote: Canonical for the inline greeting '?'. Text clipped at BOTH ends of its own bubble, on the home screen, in the first five minutes — a tester reads that as an unfinished build, not a subtle bug. Root cause of the VoiceOver gap is visible in DailyGreetingHeader.swift:87-89: the VStack takes .accessibilityElement(children: .contain) + .accessibilityLabel("Today"), which swallows the HelpInfoIcon (:75-79). The T0 fix is deletion, not sizing: the trailing DailyRoomView.HelpButton (:114-125) already opens the same panel, so removing the inline icon closes the clipping, the AX hole, the duplicate control and the wrapped headline in one S change.

confirmed.title: Dark-mode text contrast fails WCAG on the de-emphasised rows: meta 2.66:1, body 4.27:1
confirmed.evidence: Brightest stroke pixels against the card (44,41,38): "AUG 31 · NEW" = (120,103,81) → 2.66:1 (fails AA and AA-large); "A new story from the workshop." = (143,139,134) → 4.27:1 (fails AA body). For reference the primary row text is 12.42:1 and the eyebrows 5.94–8.91:1, so only the de-emphasised tier fails. Increase Contrast does not raise it (see C-07).
confirmed.fix: Raise the dark-mode de-emphasised ink to ≥4.5:1 (body) and ≥3:1 (meta).
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed on shots/C/06-dark-launch-2.0s.png — the MOVED tier is visibly a different, dimmer ink than every other row on the card. The measured values are consistent with the tokens: DarkPalette.textMuted #B5A487 and textSecondary #D8C9B4 (PatinaColors.swift:80-84) were tuned against the #211E1B canvas, but these rows sit on Background.secondary #2C2926, a lighter surface, which is where the AA margin is lost. Worth telling the fixer: the dark ramp is right for the canvas and wrong for the card.
confirmed.judgeNote: Visually confirmed on the same dark shot: 'A new story from the workshop.' and the AUG 31 meta are visibly washed out against everything around them. This is the home screen, in dark mode, on the tier of content the app is trying to make you care about. Effort S — raise two token values.

confirmed.title: "Your studio", "Your profile" and the "Studio" pill all land on one screen, and the promised "Portal" does not exist
confirmed.evidence: The Companion advertises "Your studio — PROJECTS · MESSAGES · DECISIONS" and "Your profile — STYLE · SETTINGS · PORTAL" as separate destinations; both, and the Today header's "Studio 5" pill, open the same profile+studio hub. No "Portal" row exists anywhere on it.
confirmed.fix: Split profile from studio, or relabel the Companion rows to match the single destination and drop the Portal promise.
confirmed.codeNote: Two legs confirmed, one refuted — the title as written is wrong. CONFIRMED: the Today 'Studio 5' pill routes to `.profile` (DailyRoomView.swift:256 `onStudioTap: { coordinator.navigate(to: .profile) }`) and the Companion 'Your profile' row routes to `.profile` (CompanionActionRows.swift:36-39); both mount ProfileView, and shots/C/16-dark-studio.png and 27-dark-profile.png are byte-identical (md5 b49a348d2c882cb3d374646e68f9a4ec). CONFIRMED: the Portal promise is empty — that row's hint is 'Style · Settings · Portal', grep for Portal across Features/Profile/ returns nothing, and ProfileView's action rows are Retake Style Quiz / Get design help / Settings (:154-162). REFUTED: 'Your studio' does not land there — CompanionActionRows.swift:51-54 routes it to `.projectList`, which ContentView:362 mounts as ProjectListView (a searchable project list), a different screen. The lane's own evidence supports the refutation: 14-dark-studio.png is not the studio hub but the Heirloom Oak product detail (the tap missed), and neither research/C.md nor shots/C/ledger.md records a landed tap on 'Your studio'. Restate the finding as: three surfaces named Studio point three ways — the Today pill to the profile hub, the Companion 'Your studio — Projects · Messages · Decisions' to a bare project list with no decisions or messages on it, and the STUDIO heading inside ProfileView — plus a Portal that does not exist. Severity down from major: the collision is a naming/copy defect in small type, not a dead end.
confirmed.judgeNote: Real and squarely in the first five minutes, but the framing needs one correction and one addition. CORRECTION: the Companion's "Your studio" routes to .projectList (CompanionActionRows.swift:52), not .studio — the identical pair is the Today header's "Studio N" pill (DailyGreetingHeader.studioControl → .studio) and "Your profile" (.profile), both mounting ProfileView (ContentView.swift:344-351). ADDITION that strengthens it: Patina/Features/Shared/PatinaPortalLinks.swift has ZERO call sites — the Portal was cut but the promise still ships in the row hint. Why T0: with flags off the Companion sheet is the only nav hub (research/C.md:364) and the Studio pill sits in the Today header, so a round-1 tester meets all three doors before minute five, and "Portal" is a promise they will chase and not find. T0 scope is the copy half ONLY — drop "· Portal" from CompanionActionRows.swift:37 and make the two row labels honest about where they land; that is an S edit. The structural split of profile from studio is the M work and belongs in T1/T2.

confirmed.title: Two different sheet chromes: Settings has no dismiss control and no grabber, Help has both
confirmed.evidence: Settings: neither scan_ui (5 buttons: Account, Sign in on the web, Sign Out, Delete account, Forget recent context) nor describe_screen contains a Done/Close, and no drag indicator is drawn — the only exit is an undiscoverable swipe. The Help sheet has a grabber AND an X.
confirmed.fix: Pick one sheet pattern and apply it everywhere; give Settings a Done button.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed in source and on shots/B/21-guest-settings.png. SettingsView.swift wraps in a NavigationStack and sets .toolbarTitleDisplayMode(.inline) at :168 but declares NO toolbar item and no presentationDragIndicator; @Environment(\.dismiss) at :16 is never wired to a control. The screenshot shows a sheet with neither grabber nor Done. HelpPanelSheet.swift:107-118 has the ✕ AND :122 .presentationDragIndicator(.visible). Broader confirmation: presentationDragIndicator is set on exactly 2 of 18 detent sheets app-wide (see C3-23).
confirmed.judgeNote: Holding at major. Swipe-to-dismiss is near-universal iOS literacy in 2026, so this is not a true dead end — but a homeowner who opens Settings and sees no Done, no X and no grabber has a moment of feeling trapped, and the Help sheet one tap away has BOTH. Inconsistency is what makes it read as a bug rather than a style. Effort S; fold into one patinaSheet() with C3-23.

confirmed.title: "Delete account" has no destructive treatment, and both it and "Sign Out" carry a navigation chevron
confirmed.evidence: SettingsView.DeleteAccountButton renders with the same weight, colour and trailing "›" as the benign "Account" row; only its trash icon tile differs. iOS convention is a destructive tint and no disclosure indicator on an action.
confirmed.fix: Tint destructive rows, drop the chevron on action rows, and move Delete account into its own footer group.
confirmed.codeNote: Code-verified exactly. SettingsView.swift:86-93 routes 'Delete account' through settingsButtonRow → settingsRow (:357-391), which draws `Text(label).foregroundStyle(PatinaColors.Text.primary)` at :368-370 and an unconditional `Image(systemName: "chevron.right")` at :374 — identical weight, identical colour and the same disclosure chevron as the benign 'Account' row at :68. Only the 32pt tile fill (terracotta at 0.15 opacity, :361) differs. Sign Out (:78-85) likewise carries the chevron on what is an action, not a navigation. Independently visible in shots/A/54 (light) and shots/A/60 (dark). Note for the fix lane: AccountView's Delete account (:188-192) DOES use PatinaColors.terracotta on the text — so the two surfaces already disagree, which strengthens the finding.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed in code and in my own read of shots/A/54: settingsRow (SettingsView.swift:355-389) unconditionally draws a trailing chevron.right, settingsButtonRow wraps it, and the label uses PatinaColors.Text.primary — so 'Sign Out ›' and 'Delete account ›' are typographically identical to the benign 'Account ›'. Only the 32pt tile tint differs. A row that reads as navigation but performs an irreversible action is the safety issue in this area; the confirmation alert is the only thing standing between a mis-tap and deletion. Canonical finding for destructive-row treatment — B-14's surviving half folds in here. T1 (needs a binary, and the alert mitigates the immediate risk), but it should be the first item in the Settings pass.

confirmed.title: Pieces tab renders a missing product image as a blank cream rectangle, with overlay chrome at 2.01:1 on it
confirmed.evidence: Tile fill (220,216,210) with no placeholder, skeleton or icon. On it the heart/"…" circles measure (154,153,149) vs the tile = 2.01:1, and the "% match" pill's text-to-pill contrast is 1.86:1 (versus 4.86:1 over a dark photo).
confirmed.fix: Add a branded image placeholder and a failed-load state; give the overlay chrome a guaranteed scrim so it holds contrast over light photography.
confirmed.codeNote: Half of this duplicates A-36 and half is genuinely new. DUPLICATE half: the blank cream tile is the same `else product.placeholderGradient` branch at RecommendationsView.swift:362-370 that A-36 reports — same root, same fix, should be merged. SURVIVING unique content, and it is worth keeping: (1) the overlay chrome has no guaranteed scrim — the heart and ⋯ are `Circle().fill(.ultraThinMaterial)` (:504-508, :526-530) and the match pill is `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)` (:375-382), and ultraThinMaterial over a light tile in dark mode inverts to a light-on-light wash; (2) placeholderGradient (ProductModel.swift:236-245) has no dark-mode variant, so the missing image renders as a BRIGHT CREAM SLAB on a near-black page — visible in the cited shot, which I re-read and confirms both. The 2.01:1 / 1.86:1 / 4.86:1 figures are the reviewer's own sampling; I did not re-measure pixels, but the wash is unmistakable in the shot.
confirmed.judgeNote: Half of this duplicates A-36 (same missing-image root cause, different surface) — fix both in one pass. Not collapsed into A-36 because the second half is independent and must survive: the heart/⋯ chrome at 2.01:1 and the match pill at 1.86:1 fail over ANY light tile, not only a blank one, so a guaranteed scrim is still owed once real light-background photography lands. Placeholder half T0 with A-36; the scrim half is T1 if it has to be split.

confirmed.title: On the room detail the orb covers the inner bottom corner of both "Edit dimensions" and "Edit budget"
confirmed.evidence: Orb {{169,700},{64,64}} → x 169–233, y 700–764. RoomProjectView.EditDimensions {{20,665.3},{176,48}} → x 20–196, y 665–713. RoomProjectView.SetABudget {{206,665.3},{176,48}} → x 206–382, y 665–713. 13 pt of overlap on each, stealing hit area from both.
confirmed.fix: Same bottom-inset fix as C-03.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified independently by reading shots/C/10-dark-room.png: the companion orb visibly sits over the lower inner corner of both 'Edit dimensions' and 'Edit budget', and the arithmetic in the finding checks out (orb y 700-764 vs buttons y 665.3-713.3 = 13pt vertical overlap; orb x 169-233 vs EditDimensions x 20-196 and SetABudget x 206-382). RoomProjectView applies no bottom safe-area inset for the orb. Sim-verified, not device-verified. Note for synthesis: this is one instance of an orb bottom-inset family (the finding itself points at C-03), so the fix should be one shared inset, not a per-screen patch.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified visually in shots/C/10-dark-room.png: the companion orb straddles the gap between 'Edit dimensions' and 'Edit budget' and clips the inner bottom corner of both capsules — it reads as a z-order bug, not a floating control. The measured 13pt overlap steals hit area from two of the room detail's three CTAs. Listed as a duplicate of the global bottom-inset issue (C-03) because one safe-area fix clears it everywhere, which is exactly why it is T0: cheapest possible fix, and the room detail is where it happens to land on top of primary buttons rather than empty space.

confirmed.title: The launch screen is a blank rectangle whose colour does not match the app ground, in both appearances
confirmed.evidence: Dark: pure black (0,0,0) → app ground (33,30,27). Light: pure white (255,255,255) → app ground (250,247,242). No wordmark, no logo, no motif — UILaunchScreen_Generation YES. The first ~1 s is a bare coloured slab that visibly pops when content appears.
confirmed.fix: Add a launch screen storyboard with the app ground colour and the PATINA mark (the mark already exists on the Welcome screen).
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED on config and on pixels. project.pbxproj carries INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation = YES at :690 and :738 and NO INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_* background/image key in either config; Patina/Info.plist has no launch key at all — so the generated screen resolves to systemBackground. Sampled the cited PNGs directly: 04-dark-launch-0.4s.png = RGB(1,1,1), 43-light-launch-0.35s.png = RGB(255,255,255), both flat across the frame. App ground is PatinaColors offWhite #FAF7F2 (PatinaColors.swift:17), so the pop is real in both appearances. Canonical entry for the launch-screen defect; C3-17 duplicates it and B-56 half-duplicates it.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity raised minor→major and made PRIMARY of the cold-launch cluster (B-56, C3-17 fold in). This is frame one of the product for every tester on every launch: a pure-white or pure-black slab that pops to cream/graphite reads as an unfinished build before a single pixel of Patina is shown, and no later polish recovers a bad first second. Fix is S (a launch-screen colour key with a dark variant plus the existing wordmark) and carries no behavioural risk — ship it in build 1.

confirmed.title: "1 ROOMS" — pluralisation bug on the profile stat (the accessibility label gets it right)
confirmed.evidence: Rendered "1 / ROOMS" while the AX label for the same node is the correct "Rooms: 1". Confirmed as a plural rule and not a data issue: with two rooms it correctly reads "2 ROOMS" (53-flagson-studio.png).
confirmed.fix: Use a String.LocalizedStringResource with an inflection rule for the visible label too.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified as a static label, not a data artefact: ProfileView.swift:201 and :207 both call statItem(value: "\(viewModel.roomCount)", label: "Rooms"), and statItem (:223-235) renders the label through MonoLabel (uppercased) while its accessibilityLabel is "\(label): \(value)" — hence the rendered '1 / ROOMS' beside the correct AX 'Rooms: 1'. Fix must also cover the sibling savedStat (:214-220), which has the same shape.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised minor→major. '1 ROOMS' is the single most recognizable amateur-hour tell in consumer software, and EVERY first-round tester has exactly one room. VERIFIED the root cause is simpler than stated: ProfileView.swift:201,207 pass a hardcoded `label: "Rooms"` — there is no inflection rule to fix, just a hardcoded plural, so this is a genuinely small change (the AX label is right because it is composed elsewhere). T0.

confirmed.title: Tab bar is text-only with no icons, colour-only selection, uneven widths and an unlabeled fifth item
confirmed.evidence: Four text labels plus a bare three-line glyph. Item widths 84/84/84/84 then 54 for the Companion — not evenly divided. Selection is signalled only by white-vs-tan text; no icon, no indicator. AX-wise the tabs are correct AXTabButtons with proper AXValue selection (that part is GOOD).
confirmed.fix: Add icons, an explicit selected indicator, equal widths, and either label the fifth item or move it out of the tab bar.
confirmed.codeNote: Visually accurate — shots/C/50-flagson-dark-tabroot.png shows four text-only labels plus a bare three-line glyph, selection carried by white-vs-tan text alone, uneven widths. BUT testerVisible must flip to FALSE for this audit's bar: the tab bar only exists on the house-first root, and the brief's standing fact is that a TestFlight Release first launch has every flag OFF (research/A2-config.md line 64 confirms Release has no launch-arg path and an empty PostHog cache). The lane's own shot filename says 'flagson'. No first-round tester sees this on first launch; it becomes T0-shaped only when Kody targets a tester in PostHog.
confirmed.judgeNote: Setting testerVisible FALSE for build 1: this is the flags-ON (house-first) root, and every flag is off on a TestFlight first launch. It only becomes visible if Kody targets a tester in PostHog — which is on the OWED list and likely lands in week one, so T1 rather than T2. Worth noting the tab bar is AX-correct (proper AXTabButtons with AXValue selection); the gap is purely visual — no icons, colour-only selection, uneven widths, an unlabeled fifth item.

confirmed.title: The tab bar ignores Dynamic Type entirely
confirmed.evidence: At accessibility-XXXL the tab labels stay at their default ~17 pt beside ~60 pt body text. All five still fit and stay legible, but a user who needs large type gets a nav bar that never grows; iOS's own tab bars switch to a large-content viewer at AX sizes.
confirmed.fix: Adopt the system tab bar, or add a large-content viewer for the custom one.
confirmed.codeNote: Core claim refuted. The tab bar does NOT ignore Dynamic Type — PatinaTabBar.swift:100 applies `.dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility2)`, so labels grow through accessibility2 and then cap, with `.minimumScaleFactor(0.7)` at :90 and a comment at :92-99 citing the walk IDs (w3-n2-09, w3-n3-11) that drove the cap after uncapped labels truncated mid-word and collided. The finding's own evidence concedes 'all five still fit and stay legible'. The only true residue is the fix line — no large-content viewer at AX sizes — which was never the stated defect.
confirmed.judgeNote: Down from minor: the finding concedes all five labels still fit and stay legible, and the flags-off build 1 has no tab bar at all. Real craft gap, low stakes; revisit with house-first.

confirmed.title: Flags-ON Studio tab: no bottom content inset, so the Invoice row is clipped mid-line by the tab bar
confirmed.evidence: "Invoice / $4,250.00 remaining" is cut through the middle of the second line by the tab bar's hairline; the bar has no material so there is no visual explanation. A floating "Your Studio" pill also sits top-left where a back button would be, duplicating the tab bar's own "Studio" label on a tab root.
confirmed.fix: Add .safeAreaInset for the tab bar and remove the redundant title pill.
confirmed.codeNote: PRIMARY CLAIM REFUTED. 'No bottom content inset' is false: HouseFirstRoot.swift:56 mounts the bar as `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) { bar }` — precisely the fix the finding asks for — and ProfileView additionally ends its stack with `Spacer().frame(height: 120)` (:167). The bottom inset therefore exists twice over and the last row is fully reachable. Shot C/53 is the UN-SCROLLED first frame of content longer than the screen, so a partially visible row at the bottom edge is ordinary scroll-under, not clipping. SURVIVING HALF (real, but polish): PatinaTabBar.swift:63-70 paints the bar with opaque `PatinaColors.Background.primary` plus a 1 pt pearl hairline and no material, so content vanishing under it reads as a hard cut rather than as scrollable content passing behind glass — that is the actual craft gap, and the fix is a `.ultraThinMaterial`/scroll-edge treatment, not an inset. The redundant 'Your Studio' pill in the back-button slot is the same object as B-27; fold it there. Severity minor → polish, and rewrite the title to name the material, not the inset.
confirmed.judgeNote: Both halves confirmed, but flag-gated: the four-tab bar is house-first, which is OFF on a TestFlight first launch, so no round-1 tester sees this in build 1 — testerVisible stays true because it appears the moment Kody targets a tester in PostHog. The pill half ('Your Studio' capsule top-left on a tab root, duplicating the bar's own 'Studio') is the same PatinaScreenChrome overlay as B-27 and should be fixed there — kept separate rather than dupOf because the primary claim is the missing bottom inset, which is its own S fix (.safeAreaInset for the tab bar; MoneyScreenMetrics.bottomClearance(houseFirst:) already exists and is applied on the money screens but not on this root). Also worth noting from shots/C/53: the bar has no material, so content passing under it reads as clipped rather than layered — the same missing-material problem as B-27, at the other edge. T2 unless house-first flips in week one, in which case T1.

confirmed.title: The notification badge grows over its bell and, at accessibility sizes, replaces it entirely
confirmed.evidence: At XXXL only a sliver of the bell shows behind the "3"; at AX-XXXL no bell is visible at all — just a gold disc with a numeral. The "Studio 5" pill also truncates to "St… 5".
confirmed.fix: Cap the badge's scaling relative to its anchor, or move the count into the accessibility label only.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed and under-rated. Read both shots: at XXXL (C/30) only a sliver of the bell shows behind the '3'; at AX-XXXL (C/35) there is no bell at all — a gold disc with '3' sitting on top of the date, which itself has broken to 'TUESDA / Y · / SEP 1' — and the Studio pill has truncated to 'St… 5'. Mechanism is exact in code: the bell is `.font(.system(size: 17, weight: .regular))` in a fixed `.frame(width: 36, height: 36)` (DailyGreetingHeader.swift:95-99) — a literal point size that does not scale — while UnreadBadge uses the scaling `PatinaTypography.captionSmall` with `minWidth/minHeight 14` and no dynamicTypeSize cap (:180-193), and the Studio title is `.lineLimit(1)` at :147-150. Raising minor → major: at accessibility sizes the notifications affordance is not merely crowded, it is gone and colliding with the date.
confirmed.judgeNote: XXXL is a non-accessibility size that ordinary people genuinely run, and at XXXL the badge already eats most of the bell — so this is not the rare edge case its AX-XXXL evidence makes it look like. A gold disc with a numeral where the bell should be is not catastrophic (it is still tappable and still means 'notifications'), but 'St… 5' truncating in the same header is the tell that the row was never laid out for scaled text. S fix, T1, same header pass as C-18.

confirmed.title: "More information available." is baked into non-interactive accessibility labels, and duplicated on two overlapping nodes
confirmed.evidence: Verbatim labels: "MEMBER SINCE SEP 1, 2026. MORE INFORMATION AVAILABLE." (shouted caps on a plain StaticText with no action); "Style: Style Explorer. More information available." on BOTH the decorative sparkle {{147.7,325.3},{13.7,20.3}} and the label {{167.3,327.5},{87,16}}, so VoiceOver reads the same sentence twice in a row; "Saved items: 0. More information available."
confirmed.fix: Remove the promise from labels that carry no action; hide the sparkle; drop the caps.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed at every line. ProfileView.swift:86, :108, :220 bake 'More information available.' into labels (also QRApprovalView.swift:231). The shouted caps at :86 are explained: the label sits on a `MonoLabel`, whose body applies `.textCase(.uppercase)` (MonoLabel.swift:35 → UppercaseModifier) and that reaches the spoken string — the same leak as A-111. The doubled sentence at :108 is because the label is applied to an `HStack` containing `Text("✦")` plus the badge Text with no `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, so it propagates to both children.
confirmed.judgeNote: Canonical for display styling leaking into spoken strings — shouted caps, the appended 'More information available.' promise on non-interactive text, and the duplicate on the decorative sparkle. Distinct root from C-09 (leaked copy vs leaked glyph), same work sitting.

confirmed.title: Identical truncated boilerplate on every browse card: "Selected from Patina's room-aware edit for Gu…"
confirmed.evidence: The same sentence repeats on all six visible cards, truncated mid-word and inconsistently — "for Gu…" on three, "for Gu." on one. "room-aware edit" is internal product jargon. The Pieces tab drops this line entirely and reads much cleaner.
confirmed.fix: Delete the line (as the Pieces tab already does) or move it to a one-time section note.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. RecommendationsView.recommendationRationale (:413-421) falls back to "Selected from Patina's room-aware edit for \(scopedRoomName)." whenever there is no taste portrait, and it is applied per-card via BrowseCardInfo.rationale (:409) rendered at :578-579 — so in a room-scoped grid every card carries the identical sentence. StyleProfile.swift:376 duplicates the same string. 'room-aware edit' appears nowhere a homeowner would have been taught it.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised minor→major. Six identical sentences on one grid, truncated mid-word and inconsistently ('for Gu…' / 'for Gu.'), carrying internal jargon ('room-aware edit') — that is the composite of every 'unfinished' signal in one viewport, on a core browse screen. The fix is deleting a line, and the Pieces tab already proves the screen reads better without it. Duplicated at RecommendationsView.swift:419 and StyleProfile.swift:376 — delete both. T0.

confirmed.title: Two competing primary-button styles: solid gold vs near-white pill
confirmed.evidence: "Sign proposal" and "Pay $4,250.00" are solid tan/gold; "Browse pieces for the Guest Bedroom" and "Ask Leah to source this" are near-white. The Sign In sheet then uses gold for the DISABLED state and near-white for the enabled one, so gold means both "primary" and "disabled" in the same app.
confirmed.fix: One primary token; pick a different disabled treatment.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed across four shots. Gold: PatinaButton style:.clay at ProposalDetailView.swift:165 ('Sign proposal'), InvoiceDetailView.swift:219, DecisionDetailView.swift:425, DecisionDeferSheet.swift:59, ProposalSignSheet.swift:69 — plus the same clay fill hand-rolled on shots/A/72 ('Get design help with this room') and shots/P/23 ('Verify'). Not verified: the sub-claim that the Sign In sheet uses gold for DISABLED and near-white for enabled — PatinaButton.swift:82 disables via .opacity(0.5) on whatever style is passed, so if that reads as gold-means-disabled it is a per-call-site style choice; treat that half as unconfirmed.
confirmed.judgeNote: Scoping this to its sharp half for T0: on the Sign In sheet gold is the DISABLED state and near-white is the ENABLED one, so on the app's first interactive screen the affordance colour means the opposite of what it means everywhere else. That is a comprehension failure, not a taste one. The wider gold-vs-white primary unification across proposal/invoice/room/product is T1.

confirmed.title: Three money formats for the same figure across adjacent screens
confirmed.evidence: Your Spaces shows "$0 total" and "$9.0K" on one screen; Today shows "budget $9,000" for the same room's budget; invoices show cents on every figure.
confirmed.fix: One currency formatter with an explicit abbreviation rule.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed and worse than filed. There are two shared helpers — PatinaCurrency.format (CurrencyFormatting.swift:19-29, numberStyle .currency, cents shown) and PatinaCurrency.formatWholeDollars (:31) — plus the same ad-hoc abbreviation expression `"$\(String(format: \"%.1f\", Double(dollars) / 1000))K"` copy-pasted in FIVE files: ProductModel.swift:184, SavedItem.swift:81, RoomBudgetBar.swift:70, RoomGalleryCard.swift:151, WholeHomeCrossRoomBar.swift:51. Three formats on adjacent screens is the symptom; five copies of one un-shared rule is the cause.
confirmed.judgeNote: Three formats for money, two of them ('$0 total' and '$9.0K') on the SAME screen, is the kind of incoherence a homeowner feels as sloppiness about their money specifically — the one domain where they are least forgiving. T1 not T0 because 'one currency formatter with an explicit abbreviation rule' is a real decision (when do you abbreviate?), not the S-effort string edit it is labelled.

confirmed.title: The invoice "Pay" button is below the fold with no pinned bar, unlike the product page which pins one
confirmed.evidence: invoiceDetail.pay {{24,721.3},{354,52}} only appears after scrolling past the line items; the product detail by contrast pins PurchaseActionBar. Two redundant reassurance lines also sit under the button at different sizes: "Payment opens securely in Safari." and "Pay securely by card or bank transfer."
confirmed.fix: Pin the pay action; keep one reassurance line.
confirmed.codeNote: Primary claim confirmed, one detail wrong. Confirmed: the invoice Pay button is in-flow at the bottom of the ScrollView (InvoiceDetailView.swift:211-235, after line items, memo and payments), while ProductDetailView.swift:583-640 genuinely pins `PurchaseActionBar` as a glass action bar with its own bottom clearance — two payment-adjacent screens, two patterns. Wrong: they are NOT 'at different sizes' — both are `PatinaTypography.captionSmall` (10 pt), and shot A/50 shows them at identical size. Drop that clause from the write-up.
confirmed.judgeNote: Kept separate rather than folded into B-28 because it carries an independent item that would be lost. The pinning half genuinely shares B-28's root cause — the pay action is not pinned — so schedule the two together and let B-28's T0 fix pin it. The second half is its own two-minute cut and I confirmed it in source: InvoiceDetailView:226-231 stacks 'Payment opens securely in Safari.' and 'Pay securely by card or bank transfer.' back to back, two reassurance lines saying nearly the same thing at the same weight, directly under the money button. Keep one. The A/B pattern break the finding names (product detail pins its bar via pinnedActBottomInset, invoice does not) is accurate and is the strongest argument for the pin.

confirmed.title: On the signature screen the only action is "Sign proposal" — no decline, no way to ask a question
confirmed.evidence: scan_ui full-screen returns exactly two interactive elements: Back and proposalDetail.sign — on a screen that states "Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale." The detail also shows "Product Selections", "Investment" and "Timeline" as three consecutive headings with no content between them, and "Investment" duplicates the INVESTMENT card at the top.
confirmed.fix: Add "Ask a question" / "Request changes" beside Sign, and hide empty sections.
confirmed.codeNote: Both halves verified. (1) `signFooter` (ProposalDetailView.swift:159-173) offers exactly one act, `PatinaButton("Sign proposal")`; there is no decline, no request-changes, no ask — on a document whose seeded Terms section reads 'Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale.' (2) The empty-heading claim is real and is an APP bug, not just seed shape: `ProposalNarrativeBlock` filters on `!body.isEmpty || !title.isEmpty` (ProposalDetailBlocks.swift:52) and then draws the title alone when the body is nil, and `supabase/seed/proposals.sql:89-94` gives 'Product Selections', 'Investment' and 'Timeline' `body = NULL` — a designer-authored proposal from the portal carries the same structural section types, so this reproduces on production. 'Investment' also duplicates the `MonoLabel(text: "Investment")` summary card at :119. One caveat on the evidence: the Companion mark IS on screen in shot C/20 (bottom-right) though scan_ui did not return it, so 'exactly two interactive elements' slightly understates the tree. Arguably major rather than minor — a no-exit signature screen for an $18,500 contract.
confirmed.judgeNote: Primary half confirmed and worth doing: the app can DISPLAY status 'declined' (ProposalDetailView:109) but a client has no way to set it, and scan_ui's two interactive elements on a screen stating 'Deposits are non-refundable' / 'Custom items are final sale' means Back is the only alternative to signing. Adding 'Ask a question' is cheap — the designer-thread route already exists (openDesignerThread in the money failure banner). Secondary half does NOT match main and must be re-walked before anyone schedules it: every block in ProposalDetailBlocks.swift is `if !isEmpty`-guarded (:81, :120, :167, :195, :237), the labels are Scope / Selections / Timeline / Payment schedule / Not included, 'Product Selections' appears nowhere in the app, and 'Investment' is rendered exactly once (:119). Whatever the walker saw, it was not three empty headings from this code.

confirmed.title: The two cards stacked on Your Spaces have different widths, so their right edges do not align
confirmed.evidence: Whole Home card {{20,178.7},{312,76}} (right edge 332) versus Guest Bedroom card {{20,270.7},{362,243}} (right edge 382) — the Whole Home card is narrowed to make room for a trailing "?" that lives outside it.
confirmed.fix: Move the "?" inside the card (or delete it, see C-05) and set both cards to the same width.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed on shots/C/09-dark-spaces.png: the Whole Home card's right edge stops visibly short of the Guest Bedroom card's, and the trailing '?' sits outside the card in the gap that narrowing created. Visible on the flag-off root, so it is in a first-round tester's path.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raising polish to minor. Misaligned right edges on two stacked cards is exactly the craft failure a design-literate person spots in half a second, and Your Spaces is a top-level destination. The cause is instructive: a card was narrowed to make room for a help '?' that lives outside it — the same help-glyph proliferation as B-26. Fix both together.

confirmed.title: The bottom action bar has no material in dark — 1.06:1 against the page
confirmed.evidence: Bar fill sampled (35,33,31) against page (33,30,27) = 1.06:1; only a hairline marks it, so content slides behind an essentially invisible slab and the questionmark.circle beneath it is invisible-but-tappable until you scroll. The same flat-slab treatment is used on the flags-ON tab bar.
confirmed.fix: Use a proper bar material with a scroll-edge effect.
confirmed.codeNote: Measurement confirmed on shots/C/13-dark-product-scrolled.png — the bar is essentially a flat slab distinguished only by its hairline. But the diagnosis needs correcting for the fixer: this is NOT an un-materialed bar. ProductDetailView.swift:630 documents it as a PT-5-7 Liquid Glass bar and ProductDetailBlocks.swift:213-214 applies .glassEffect(.regular, in:.rect) behind an `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)` guard. So the fix is not 'use a proper bar material' — it is that glassEffect resolves to ~no separation on the warm-graphite canvas here, and this reading is simulator-only. Re-measure on a device before spending effort.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raising polish to minor for the hit-target half: a 1.06:1 bar in dark means content slides behind an essentially invisible slab AND the questionmark.circle beneath it is invisible-but-tappable. A tester tapping and getting an unexpected sheet is a small trust cost. Product detail is a core surface. Effort S.

confirmed.title: Two empty states stacked on the room detail
confirmed.evidence: A "0 / SAVED PIECES" stat card is immediately followed by "✦ / A blank canvas / Browse pieces for the Guest Bedroom" — the same message told twice, back to back. The browse screen one tap later then says "10 pieces chosen for this room", which contradicts the "blank canvas" framing.
confirmed.fix: Suppress the stat card when the count is zero, and align the "saved" / "chosen" vocabulary.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified in shots/C/10-dark-room.png: a '0 / SAVED PIECES' stat card sits directly above the '✦ / A blank canvas / Browse pieces for the Guest Bedroom' empty state — the same nothing stated twice in two visual idioms. The saved/chosen vocabulary mismatch the finding raises is a separate copy issue on the browse screen; I did not re-verify that screen's '10 pieces chosen for this room' string, so treat that clause as unverified while the stacked-empties half is confirmed. Polish is the right severity.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from polish on the strength of the screenshot. shots/C/10-dark-room.png shows more than redundancy: the '0 / SAVED PIECES' card, then ~150pt of dead vertical space, then '✦ / A blank canvas / Browse pieces for the Guest Bedroom'. Every new tester's first room detail looks like this — the empty state is the DEFAULT state, not an edge case, so this is a first-five-minutes screen and it currently reads as unfinished rather than calm. The vocabulary contradiction the finder caught is the sharper half: 'a blank canvas' one tap before 'ten pieces chosen for this room'. S effort. Suppress the zero stat card, design the empty room detail as a deliberate screen, and align saved/chosen.

confirmed.title: Notification rows read as run-on sentences and announce a timestamp that is not on screen
confirmed.evidence: Labels concatenate without punctuation: "Unread. A sign-off needs you Design Development sign-off — drawing set B 9h ago". The read rows carry "Just now" in the label ("Invoice $4,250.00 remaining · Due Sep 6 Just now") while no timestamp is rendered for them. "Mark all read" is a 16 pt tall target and the "Notifications" title has no heading trait.
confirmed.fix: Split title/description into label and value, drop the phantom timestamp, add the header trait.
confirmed.codeNote: All four sub-claims check out against code and the captured AX tree. Run-on: accessibilityLabel(for:) joins parts with a bare ' ' and no punctuation (NotificationFeedView.swift:302-313). Phantom timestamp: that same function appends notification.timeAgo unconditionally, including for isStudioFallback rows whose timestamp the view deliberately does NOT render (:270-274) — hence 'Invoice $4,250.00 remaining · Due Sep 6 Just now'. Target size: research/C.md:17 records the 'Mark all read' AXFrame as {{297.3,126},{80.7,16}} — 16 pt tall, and the code confirms it (Button with .font(uiSmall) and no padding/minHeight, :26-33; the .padding on the HStack sits outside the button's frame). Header trait: Text('Notifications') at :19-21 carries no .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader). Confirmed as written.
confirmed.judgeNote: Flipping testerVisible to true on one item the finder bundled into the VoiceOver group: a 16 pt tall 'Mark all read' target is a miss-prone control for every tester, not only VoiceOver users, and it sits in the navigation bar where fat-fingering it hits Back instead. The rest is correctly scoped — run-on labels, the phantom 'Just now' (same root as A-86's missing timestamp slot, fix once), and the missing heading trait. A first round invited personally by Kody is unlikely to include a VoiceOver user, which is what keeps this out of T0, but the brief's bar names correct VoiceOver explicitly, so it does not slide past build 2. S.

confirmed.title: The Companion identifies itself two different ways on the same identifier, and its subtitle is squeezed to an 88 pt measure
confirmed.where: Product detail vs everywhere else; shots/C/12-dark-product.png, 03-light-companion.png
confirmed.evidence: On the product detail companion.bubble is {{338,768},{44,44}} labelled "Patina companion — menu" with hint "Opens quick actions for this screen."; everywhere else it is 64 pt, centred, labelled "Patina companion" with hint "Opens the Companion." — one identifier, two components, three positions. Separately the sheet's subtitle box is {{100,358},{88,31.7}} inside a 314 pt panel, forcing "5 things need / your eye." to wrap with ~44 pt of unused width beside it.
confirmed.fix: One Companion component with one label; widen the subtitle measure to the panel.
confirmed.codeNote: SPLIT VERDICT. The identifier half is REAL and code-confirmed: `companion.bubble` is set on two different components with two different labels and hints — CompanionOverlay.swift:763/766 (minimalView) and :789 (companionMarkButton) both say 'Patina companion — menu' / 'Opens quick actions for this screen.', while CompanionHearthView.swift:147-149 says `presentation.accessibilityLabel` ('Patina companion', CompanionPresentation.swift:142) / 'Opens the Companion.' The AX dump in research/C.md corroborates both strings. The FRAMING IS WRONG: the 44 pt bottom-right variant is not a 'per-screen accident'. It is the documented, ruled yield — CompanionOverlay.swift:172-186 hands `.minimal` to pieceDetail, arPlacement, accessibility text sizes and pinned-footer money routes, with the full rationale written out in CompanionSafeArea.swift:95-135 ('Ruling 1: the orb yields'). The fix as written ('one Companion component with one label') would re-break the money screens the yield exists to protect; the correct fix is one label/hint pair across both components, keeping the yield. Subtitle half: the early wrap with unused width beside it is visible in shots/C/03-light-companion.png, but '88 pt measure' is the Text's rendered bounds from the AX tree, not the width the layout offered — the number reads as a constraint and is not one.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity polish→minor. Both halves verified at source: CompanionOverlay.swift:763 and :789 label the product-detail bubble 'Patina companion — menu' while CompanionPresentation.swift:142 labels every other instance 'Patina companion' — one identifier, two components, three positions. The 88pt subtitle measure is visible in crop-dark-companion-header.png. Split the work: the measure widening rides along with C-02's header edit in build 1 at no extra cost; unifying the two components into one is the T1 half. R-12 and A-47 are the same finding seen from walks.

confirmed.title: Mixed capitalisation within single lists, and mono numerals use a slashed zero
confirmed.evidence: Settings mixes "Sign Out" and "Haptic Feedback" (Title Case) with "Delete account", "Sign in on the web", "Upload scans on cellular" (sentence case); the profile list mixes "Retake Style Quiz", "Get design help" and "Settings". The mono instrument face renders zeros slashed — "18Ø SQ FT", the Archive count "0" — which reads as a code editor next to the serif display type.
confirmed.fix: Pick sentence case throughout; consider a non-slashed zero for client-facing numerals.
confirmed.codeNote: Two claims, different fates. The casing half duplicates C5-10 (SettingsView.swift:81/89/121, ProfileView.swift:154 all verified) and should be folded there. The slashed-zero half — the mono instrument face rendering '18Ø SQ FT' — is a typeface/visual-system finding, not copy, and I did not verify it in code; it should be re-filed under visual-system so a font-feature fix (kZeroKind / ss0x on the mono face) is scoped against the right owner.
confirmed.judgeNote: Split. The casing half is a duplicate of C5-10 — drop it there, C5-10's evidence is stronger. The SURVIVING unique content is the typographic one: the mono instrument face renders slashed zeros ('18Ø SQ FT', the Archive '0'), which reads as a code editor sitting inside serif display type. That is a real design-system observation nobody else made, and it should not be lost in the casing merge. T2 because it is a typeface/feature-setting decision (disable the slashed-zero stylistic set) with more risk and less first-week payoff than it appears.

confirmed.title: Failed-sign-in error leaks onto the Welcome root, shifts the stack 33 pt, and the mis-tap lands the tester in the inescapable guest flow
confirmed.where: Welcome home + Sign In sheet; shots/P/34-cancel-from-password.png, 35-welcome-shifted-33pt.png, 30-relaunch-after-cancel.png
confirmed.evidence: After tester@patina.cloud + wrongpassword123 was rejected, tapping Cancel dismissed the sheet AND rendered "Invalid login credentials" in bare red text on the Welcome screen, between "Start with a piece you love" and Sign in with Apple. That line pushes the auth stack down exactly 33 pt: guestButton moves 552.25-603.75 -> 584.92-636.42, passwordButton 619.00-633.67 -> 651.67 (Terms/Privacy footer stays at 785.33). I then tapped y=626 aiming for "Have a password? Sign in" at its last-seen position; 626 now falls inside "Look around first", and the app went into the guest carousel. Cold relaunch after that shows the guest intro as root with only Onboarding.SkipButton + Onboarding.PrimaryButton.0 — sign-in gone. Controls: Cancel from email-entry (21-after-cancel.png) and Cancel from the OTP step with no failure (37-cancel-from-otp.png) both return to an unshifted Welcome with no leak; the leak is specific to a failed attempt.
confirmed.fix: Never render sheet errors on the auth root; if a root status is needed, reserve its space so nothing moves. Fix P-18 independently so the guest flow is escapable.
confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt
confirmed.codeNote: Both auth-attributable halves CONFIRMED. The leak: AuthenticationView's Cancel (:50-52) only calls dismiss() — AuthService.errorMessage survives, and ContentView.swift:60 passes it straight into AuthScreenView's banner; shots/P/35-welcome-shifted-33pt.png shows 'Invalid login credentials' in bare system red on the ROOT. The shift: AuthScreenView.swift:65-73 (same root as A-70), footer unmoved because it sits below the Spacer at :143. Severity lowered from blocker: the blocker rating rests on P-18's 'inescapable guest flow', which the code contradicts — from .main a guest reaches the auth chooser via NotificationFeedView.swift:195, CompanionOverlay.swift:682, and ProductDetailView.swift:253. The mis-tap is still real and still lands the tester somewhere they did not aim for.
confirmed.judgeNote: The worst five seconds in the app: one typo produces a raw backend string on the ROOT screen, a 33pt shift, and a tap at the remembered position drops the tester into a guest flow whose sign-in door they then cannot find (B-12). Two S-effort fixes, both T0: clear errorMessage on the phase change so sheet errors never render on the auth root (same fix as C1-20), and reserve the banner's space instead of inserting it.

confirmed.title: After one tap on "Look around first", the sign-in screen is unreachable on every later launch and the quiz restarts from zero
confirmed.evidence: Launch 1 = Welcome (Apple/Google/email/"Have a password? Sign in"). After one guestButton tap and 4 quiz answers, terminate+launch lands on the guest intro page 1, not Welcome; a 3rd cold launch is identical (describe_screen returns the same 7 nodes). Only controls are Onboarding.SkipButton and "Start Your Journey". Skip's AX help reads "Skips the introduction and continues to style questions." and it lands on quiz Q1 at "STEP 1 OF 5 / 20%" with the four earlier answers discarded. No Back, no Close, no swipe-back anywhere in the flow.
confirmed.fix: Persist quiz progress; put a persistent "I already have an account — Sign in" on every guest onboarding and quiz screen; make the guest flow dismissible back to the Welcome root.
confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt
confirmed.codeNote: Real, and the code is more damning than the finding claims — but not a blocker. Confirmed: AppCoordinator.derivePhase() (:258-271) returns .auth only when `!signedIn && !guestModeOptIn`, and guestModeOptIn initialises from the PERSISTED GuestSessionStore (:92), so one tap on "Look around first" (AuthScreenView.swift:104-108 calls GuestSessionStore.shared.optIn()) makes the Welcome root unreachable for good. StyleQuizView.swift:60-72 carries an explicit comment that during onboarding "there is deliberately NO ✕ … Onboarding users finish the (short) quiz instead" — so the absence of an exit is designed, not accidental, and shots/P/14-relaunch2-root.png confirms the carousel offers only Skip and "Start Your Journey". On progress: persistence DOES exist (StyleQuizViewModel.swift:68-98, key styleQuiz.savedProgress.v1) but is written only by the ✕ dialog's "Save progress & exit" (StyleQuizView.swift:82), a control onboarding never renders — so a hard kill genuinely discards every answer, exactly as observed. Two corrections. (1) The title is wrong: it is the WELCOME ROOT that is unreachable, not sign-in — once the 5 questions are done, AuthenticationView is reachable from the companion menu (shots/A/21), the notifications empty state (29/30) and the home CTA (28). (2) Severity blocker→major: the tester can proceed by answering five questions, so this is not a dead end, a crash, or meaningful data loss. Still T0 — an invited tester who mis-taps the guest button is forced through a quiz they don't want before they can sign in.
confirmed.judgeNote: Downgraded blocker→major on the brief's own definition: the tester CAN proceed. Verified in shots/P/14-relaunch2-root.png (relaunch 2 = guest intro page 1, controls are only Skip and 'Start Your Journey'), but lane A's walk shows the route out exists — finish the 5 questions and the home carries both a 'Studio' pill and a sign-in prompt. So it is a forced 5-question toll and an undiscoverable escape, not a dead end. That still makes it the worst first-run trap in the audit and it is aimed squarely at this round's population: Kody is inviting people who already have accounts, and one curious tap on 'Look around first' hides sign-in from them on every later launch behind a button that says 'Start Your Journey'. The cheap, low-risk half — a persistent 'Already have an account? Sign in' on every guest onboarding and quiz screen — is S and ships in build 1. Quiz-progress persistence can follow at T1. T0 for the affordance.

confirmed.title: "Continue with email" uses an emoji envelope and "Continue with Google" a plain letter G, on the app's first screen

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt

AuthScreenView.swift:82 icon:"G", :85 icon:"✉"; PatinaButton.swift:160-163 renders `Text(icon).font(.system(size:16))` inside the Button label with no .accessibilityHidden and no button-level .accessibilityLabel, so the glyph is both the visual and the first word of the spoken label. Three icon idioms in one three-button stack on the first screen is the clearest 'unfinished' signal in the whole audit, and it is the first thing a homeowner sees. Half of it evaporates if A3-06 removes the Google button; the envelope swap plus accessibilityHidden is minutes of work.

confirmed.title: An invalid email produces no message at all — the button silently does nothing

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt

confirmed.title: After a failed code the success and error banners show at once, and Verify is pushed off the bottom of the sheet

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED in code and shot. successMessage is set at AuthViewModel.swift:194 and cleared only by clearForm (:356), the 'use a different email' button (AuthenticationView.swift:398) and the resetPassword timer — verifyOtp's failure path (:235-240) never touches it, so both banners render stacked; shots/P/28-verify-t5.png shows the full-bleed green banner directly above the narrower centre-inset red one, exactly as described. Pair with C1-37 and C9-08 and make 'a first-time tester can enter a code and submit it on an iPhone 17 Pro' the single T0 acceptance test for the whole email flow.

confirmed.title: At the largest Dynamic Type size the first screen collapses: every button label truncates, text breaks the gutters, no scroll

See our Privacy Policy." with Decline / Accept, covering the "1. Acceptance of Terms" heading. Full site chrome incl. hamburger nav.

confirmed.title: The OTP field's placeholder is "000000", exposed as its accessibility value, and a filled field looks almost identical to an empty one

Keep the label and the placeholder-choice fixes, drop the 'exposed as its accessibility value' framing as a defect.
confirmed.judgeNote: Up from minor. The compound is what earns T0: a tester sees '000000' sitting in the field (reads as a prefilled code), taps a tan Verify that looks enabled but is disabled (C1-17), and nothing happens — on the one screen that gates the whole app. Treat the OTP screen as a single T0 pass: placeholder, filled-state affordance, button state; the AXValue fix rides along free.
