confirmed.evidence: Welcome button "Continue with email"; sheet "We'll email you a sign-in code" and "Email me a code"; password-sheet footer "Use magic link". The app sends a 6-digit code, not a link.

The naming inconsistency is confirmed and is worse than filed — five names across one file: AuthenticationView.swift:120 'Continue with email', :136 'sign-in code', :234 'We sent a magic link to', :243 'Click the link in the email to sign in.', :260 'Resend magic link', :312 'Enter your sign-in code', :603 'Use magic link'. But the headline claim — "'magic link' is factually wrong… The app sends a 6-digit code, not a link" — is REFUTED: Strata's GoTrue magic-link template was patched 2026-07-12 to append '

Or enter this code: {{ .Token }}

' with mailer_otp_length=6, so the production email carries BOTH a link and a code. The defect is that the app names one mechanism five ways and offers two competing sent-panels, not that any single word is false.

Three names for one mechanism would be minor anywhere else; here it is in the sign-in flow, where a tester who cannot get in does not file a bug, they delete the app. And 'Use magic link' is factually wrong — it sends a 6-digit code — so a tester taps it, goes to their inbox looking for a link, and finds a number. confirmed.evidence: After wrongpassword123 was rejected, the system AutoFill sheet "Save Password? — Securely store your password so it's filled automatically the next time you need it." appeared over the Welcome screen. The app is inviting the keychain to memorise a password that does not work.

confirmed.ledger: /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/research/P.md (full ledger, 336 lines) · /Users/kody/Code/patina-merged/artifacts/ios-testflight-polish-2026-09-01/shots/P/ledger.md (shot-by-shot) · 40 numbered PNGs + 10 timing PNGs in shots/P/ · logs: research/P-log-launch.txt, P-log-signin.txt, P-log-deeplink.txt

The app does not signal anything to AutoFill: the password field is a bare SecureField with NO .textContentType (AuthTextField, AuthenticationView.swift:654-707) and there is no ASCredentialIdentityStore call anywhere. iOS's heuristic save prompt fires on its own after a secure-field submit plus view dismissal, and 'only signal after success' is not an available lever in that state. This is downstream of C1-08 — adding .textContentType(.password)/.newPassword is what gives the app control here — so fold it into that fix rather than tracking it separately.
confirmed.judgeNote: Watch the interaction rather than scheduling this alone: C1-08 asks to add .textContentType(.password), which makes iOS MORE likely to offer to save — including after failures — and there is no clean API to suppress the system prompt. Re-check it as an acceptance detail of C1-08.

confirmed.codeNote: First half CONFIRMED and slightly undercounted: `grep -c 'com.apple.coredata:error' research/P-log-launch.txt` = 442 lines, all at t+0.17 s, all from the App-Group store path .../Shared/AppGroup/<uuid>/Library/Application Support/default.store not existing, ending in a successful recovery — self-heals, cosmetic in the log. Second half REFUTED for the tester: the two `[com.patina.app:Supabase] [error] ... errSecItemNotFound` lines (P-log-launch.txt:792,797) come from SupabaseDiagnosticsLogger, which is wrapped in `#if DEBUG` at Core/Network/SupabaseClient.swift:15-37 and passed as `nil` in release (:47-51). Its real cost is to the team — 450 error lines at t+0.17s is the noise that hides a genuine first-install failure when a tester reports one, so it is worth doing before the round for diagnostic hygiene, not for the tester. S effort, T2.

confirmed.title: Quiz submit shows nothing for up to 30 seconds — isSubmitting has no reader
confirmed.evidence: submitQuiz() sets isSubmitting = true but no view reads it. isComplete — the flag StyleQuizView.onChange routes off (:106-118) — is set only in the RPC completion/catch. ProductAPIClient sets timeoutInterval = requestTimeout = 30.0s. After the fifth answer the screen sits on Q5 with the option highlighted and nothing moving.
confirmed.fix: Render a 'Reading your answers…' state off isSubmitting; drop the quiz RPC timeout to ~8s (the local result is already the fallback).
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed, and one detail makes it worse. `isSubmitting` is written at StyleQuizViewModel:162/185/195 and read by NOTHING outside the class — repo-wide grep shows the only isSubmitting readers are DesignRequest* and Decisions*, different types. `isComplete`, which StyleQuizView.onChange:106-118 routes off, is set only inside the RPC's completion/catch. APIConfiguration.swift:147 requestTimeout = 30.0 and ProductAPIClient.applyHeaders:30 stamps it on every request including processStyleQuiz. Worse: submitQuiz():161 guards on `!isSubmitting`, so the tester's repeat taps on the still-enabled Continue silently no-op for the whole window. Final answer → up to 30s of a screen that does not react.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: submitQuiz() sets isSubmitting with no reader anywhere, then awaits ProductAPIClient with a 30 s timeout. This is the final tap of the entire first-run flow. On a good network it is a 0.5-2 s dead pause; on cellular it is up to 30 s of a screen that looks frozen, and the tester force-quits — which, with C1-28, discards all five answers, and with C1-03 they cannot skip the retry. That chain is the worst failure sequence in the area. S effort: a 'Reading your answers…' state plus an ~8 s timeout, since the local result is already computed as the fallback.

confirmed.title: Welcome screen has no in-flight state for any of its four sign-in buttons
confirmed.evidence: AuthScreenView's whole input surface is five closures + showGuest + errorMessage. No isLoading parameter, and AuthService.isLoading is never read here. The Apple id-token exchange and the Google OAuth open both leave the screen fully interactive with zero feedback; buttons re-fire on a second tap.
confirmed.fix: Thread AuthService.shared.isLoading in; disable the stack and spin the pressed row.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. AuthScreenView's entire input surface is the five closures + showGuest + errorMessage (AuthScreenView.swift:17-30) — no isLoading parameter exists, and neither ContentView.swift:36-70 nor AuthSheet.swift:50-72 reads AuthService.isLoading. Both call sites fire their Tasks with no disabling, so the Apple id-token exchange (AuthService.swift:359-383, which does set isLoading) and the Google OAuth open leave the whole stack live and re-tappable.
confirmed.judgeNote: On cellular the Apple id-token exchange is a 1-3s dead zone on the first screen with zero feedback and buttons that re-fire on a second tap. 'Is this thing on' is the first judgement a tester makes about an app, and threading the existing isLoading through is S. T0.

confirmed.title: Auth fields declare no textContentType: no Passwords autofill, no keychain save, no keyboard flow
confirmed.evidence: AuthTextField sets only keyboardType and autocapitalization. No .textContentType(.username/.emailAddress/.password/.newPassword), no .submitLabel, no @FocusState, no .onSubmit. iOS offers no saved-password fill on Sign In, never offers to save a new password on Create Account, and Return does not advance email → password.
confirmed.fix: Add .textContentType per field, a @FocusState chain and .submitLabel(.next/.go).
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED and canonical (C6-41 is the same finding). AuthTextField (AuthenticationView.swift:654-707) sets only keyboardType and textInputAutocapitalization; call sites :185-211. I grepped the whole app: exactly THREE .textContentType calls exist (DecisionDetailView.swift:417, ProposalSignSheet.swift:55, and AuthenticationView.swift:328's .oneTimeCode) — the email and password fields set none. Also confirmed app-wide: one @FocusState (SavedNoteSheet.swift:20), one .onSubmit (RoomSettingsView.swift:121), two .submitLabel, both on search fields. P-32 is downstream of this.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not T0: round-1 testers arrive by Apple or email code, where AutoFill matters least. But a password-manager user tapping a field that offers nothing reads as a broken form, and the @FocusState chain it asks for is the same edit as C9-08's auth half — do them together in build 2.

confirmed.title: 85 lines of the email flow — including the only 'Enter code instead' button — are unreachable
confirmed.evidence: magicLinkSentView needs `magicLinkSent && !showOtpEntry`. sendMagicLink() sets both true (AuthViewModel:189-195); the only writers clearing showOtpEntry (:394-403, clearForm :368) clear magicLinkSent in the same gesture. Dead with it: the 'We sent a magic link… Click the link in the email' copy, its Resend, the AX id auth.magicLink.enterCodeButton, and showOtpEntryForMagicLink().
confirmed.fix: Delete the branch, the view and the view-model method.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED by exhaustive state analysis. magicLinkSentView is gated on `magicLinkSent && !showOtpEntry` (AuthenticationView.swift:176-181). sendMagicLink sets magicLinkSent=true (:189) AND showOtpEntry=true (:192) in the same call; the only two writers that clear showOtpEntry — AuthenticationView.swift:395-398 and clearForm (AuthViewModel.swift:368) — clear magicLinkSent in the same gesture (:396, :359); showOtpEntryForMagicLink (:206-211) only ever SETS it. No reachable state satisfies the branch, so :222-300 is dead, taking the 'Resend magic link', 'Enter code instead' (auth.magicLink.enterCodeButton) and 'Click the link in the email' strings with it. This is load-bearing for C5-07 and C5-33, whose copy findings partly cite dead code.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity major with testerVisible false is internally inconsistent — nobody sees dead code; I have set it minor/true-by-proxy. I confirmed the branch shape in AuthenticationView (magicLinkSentView sits behind mode == .magicLink && magicLinkSent, after the showOtpEntry branch). Its real value is that this dead branch is what misled C5-07 into reporting live 'magic link' copy. Delete it in the same edit as C5-07's copy pass.

confirmed.title: The guest→account claim sheet can be requested while another sheet owns the screen, then never presents — and the account's rooms never hydrate
confirmed.evidence: The claim is raised inside the auth-state event and presented only by `.onChange(of: localStoreClaim.isAsking)` — no `initial: true` — on CompanionOverlay, which mounts only in .main (ContentView:76-79,197). Two orderings break it: (a) sign-in from the .auth phase (reachable via DeepLinkHandler:167 flipping a guest out of guest mode), so isAsking is already true before the overlay exists; (b) sign-in inside AuthSheet, whose onChange dismiss (AuthSheet:79-81) is animating while the claim asks for a sheet from a presenter underneath. The file's own comment (:46-57) states the consequence: isAsking stays true forever, keep()/startFresh() never run, and settleLocalStore's `guard !claimPending` suppresses the account's hydrate for the whole sign-in.
confirmed.fix: Add `initial: true` to the onChange and hoist the claim onto ContentView so it does not depend on which sheet is mid-animation.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed as a latent defect at code level; correctly located and honestly rated at 0.7. `.onChange(of: localStoreClaim.isAsking)` (CompanionOverlay.swift:557-563) carries no `initial: true`, and CompanionOverlay mounts only inside the .main phase (ContentView.swift:197 and HouseFirstRoot.swift:59) — so a claim already raised before the overlay exists is never presented. The raise happens synchronously inside the auth-state event: startAuthStateListener → settleLocalStore(for:) → reconcileLocalStoreOwner → LocalStoreClaim.askIfNeeded (AuthService.swift:255-288). The consequence is not speculation — settleLocalStore's `guard !claimPending else { return }` (:262) provably suppresses reconcileSharedStore for the whole sign-in, and the file's own comment at CompanionOverlay.swift:46-57 spells out the same failure. The sheet's `.onDisappear { if isAsking { keep() } }` safety net only helps once the sheet has actually presented, so it does not cover either ordering. Not sim-reproduced (needs guest work plus a sign-in raised outside .main); the code reading stands on its own.
confirmed.judgeNote: Mechanism verified by reading (LocalStoreClaim.keep()/startFresh() are the only callers of hydrate(); the onChange has no initial: true), but the impact framing needs tempering: lane A's walk DID get the claim sheet to present on the AuthSheet path (research/A.md A-79 quotes its copy verbatim), so the common in-app sign-in ordering works. The exposed path is the deep-link/magic-link one, where DeepLinkHandler flips a guest out of guest mode from the .auth phase and CompanionOverlay mounts after isAsking is already true — plausible for exactly this round, since testers arrive by email. When it fires the consequence is permanent and silent: the sheet never presents, keep() never runs, and settleLocalStore's guard suppresses the account's hydrate for good — the tester signs in and their rooms simply are not there, with no error to report. Split the fix: `initial: true` is a one-line S that covers the ordering and is a cheap T0 add-on; hoisting the claim onto ContentView is the M half. T1.

confirmed.title: The emailed link and the typed code give two different first runs — the link skips onboarding entirely
confirmed.evidence: One email carries both a 6-digit code and a link. Typing the code runs verifyOtp and leaves onboarding untouched → carousel + quiz. Tapping the link runs handleMagicLinkURL and then unconditionally marks onboarding complete → straight to an empty home, no quiz, no style profile, so every recommendation surface is unpersonalised. The justifying comment ('implies the user already went through whatever onboarding the web surface required') is untrue for a brand-new account created by that same email.
confirmed.fix: Set the flag only when the account is not new (gate on an existing StylePreferenceModel / profiles.created_at), or drop it.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed, and I verified the premise the finding asserts rather than proves. supabase/templates/magic-link.html interpolates BOTH {{ .Token }} and {{ .ConfirmationURL }}, so one email really does carry a 6-digit code and a link. AuthService.sendMagicLink passes redirectTo = "patina://auth/callback" (:561) — a custom URL scheme, not an applinks path, so the link does reopen the app rather than dead-ending in Safari (worth noting: AASA lists only /piece,/invoices,/proposals,/decisions, which would NOT have covered a universal-link callback). DeepLinkHandler.swift:131-150 then sets AppSettings.shared.hasCompletedOnboarding = true unconditionally at :143, with the justifying comment at :136-140 quoted accurately. So the two halves of one email produce two different first runs, and the link path leaves a brand-new account with no quiz and no style profile. Correctly located; effort S is right (the flag flip is one line).
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed by reading DeepLinkHandler.swift:131-150 — hasCompletedOnboarding is set unconditionally on the magic-link branch, and the justifying comment ('implies the user already went through whatever onboarding the web surface required') is simply untrue for a brand-new account. Impact is larger than 'two testers get different apps': if Kody's invited testers mostly tap the link rather than retype the code — the natural behaviour when reading email on the phone that has the app — then the entire onboarding and quiz never runs for the round, and every personalised surface has nothing to personalise from. That silently invalidates the first-round signal, not just the first run. S fix, but it needs a product call on whether magic-link arrivals should still get the quiz, which is why it is not T0. T1.

confirmed.title: Nothing in the app can set or edit your name, and the one writer writes where the app does not read
confirmed.evidence: captureAppleName is the app's only name write (grep: one UserAttributes call site), fires only on the first Apple authorization, and writes GoTrue user metadata — not profiles.display_name. handle_new_user (migration 00313) copies metadata → profiles on INSERT only, and the update lands after the row exists. The email-code path sends no display_name at all. ProfileService.displayName reads profiles first. AccountView shows an email and a date, no name, no edit affordance anywhere in Settings/Account/Profile.
confirmed.fix: An editable name row in Account writing both profiles.display_name and user metadata; ask for a name once in onboarding.
confirmed.codeNote: Mostly CONFIRMED, one claim wrong. Verified: exactly one UserAttributes call site app-wide (AuthService.swift:394, inside captureAppleName, fired only on the first Apple authorization and writing GoTrue metadata AFTER the profiles row exists — 00313 INSERTs with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING); the email-code path sends only role, no display_name (AuthService.swift:563); ProfileService.displayName:189-190 reads profiles first; AccountView.swift:109-147 shows an email and a date with no name and no edit affordance, and SettingsView.swift:60-77 has none either. WRONG: 'the app's only name write'. signUp passes display_name in signup metadata (AuthService.swift:437-440) and handle_new_user copies it into profiles at INSERT — so the password Create Account path DOES set the name correctly. Corrected finding: no way to EDIT a name anywhere, and the primary (email-code) path never captures one.
confirmed.judgeNote: Compounds badly with Apple's Hide My Email: an Account screen whose only identity is a privaterelay address, with no name and no edit affordance anywhere in the app. Build 2 — asking for a name in onboarding is a design decision, not a patch, and the profiles vs metadata write split needs a real fix rather than a quick one.

confirmed.title: A guest's saves, rooms and quiz never reach the account, by construction
confirmed.evidence: Three one-way valves. (1) SavedItemMirror.shouldAttempt(isAuthenticated:) is false for a guest; its doc claims 'SP-06's claim step carries the guest's local work across at sign-in', but LocalStoreClaim.keep() only refrains from deleting and calls reconcileSharedStore(). (2) RoomMerge.Plan documents keepLocal as 'This mirror is read-only: nothing here pushes' and untouched as 'Rooms that never synced. Never merged into an account'. (3) process_style_quiz is GRANT EXECUTE … TO authenticated only, so a guest's submission is rejected and the local result is silently kept; nothing re-submits after sign-in.
confirmed.fix: On the claim's 'Keep them', enqueue: POST each local TableItemModel to saved_items, POST each remoteId==nil room, and re-POST the stored StylePreferenceSnapshot through process_style_quiz.
confirmed.codeNote: All four citations verified verbatim. (1) SavedItem.swift:137-139 — `static func shouldAttempt(isAuthenticated: Bool) -> Bool { isAuthenticated }`, under a doc comment (:125-134) that does claim "SP-06's claim step carries the guest's local work across at sign-in". (2) RoomSyncCoordinator.swift:58-65 — keepLocal documented "This mirror is read-only: nothing here pushes", untouched documented "Rooms that never synced. Never merged into an account (SP-06)". (3) LocalStoreClaim.swift:74-77 — keep() only clears isAsking and calls hydrate(), which is `RoomSyncCoordinator.reconcileSharedStore()`, a pull; nothing pushes. (4) process_style_quiz is granted to `authenticated` only — I grepped every migration: 00067:238 and 00246:190 grant it to authenticated, and no migration anywhere grants it to anon (by contrast 00246:308 explicitly grants get_recommendations to anon, so the omission is deliberate, not an oversight). No re-submit path exists in the app: the only caller is ProductAPIClient.swift:198 / APIConfiguration.swift:245, both on the quiz-completion seam. Correctly located; effort L is right.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed at the code level — I read LocalStoreClaim.keep(): it clears isAsking and calls reconcileSharedStore(), nothing uploads. Adjusting the framing from 'a missing feature' to 'a promise the app makes and breaks': the sheet lane A captured says verbatim 'Keep them and they become yours' (research/A.md A-79). A tester who hearts a piece as a guest, signs in, taps 'Keep them', and finds it gone has caught the app being untrue — worse than the same gap with honest copy. Split the tier accordingly and treat the copy as the T1 scope: make the sheet say only what actually happens (S, ships in the first week and removes the dishonesty). The real migration — saved_items push, unsynced-room push, re-POST of the stored StylePreferenceSnapshot through process_style_quiz, which also needs a grant change since the RPC is authenticated-only — is L and belongs at T2. Ledger tier T1 for the copy; carry the L body forward as T2.

confirmed.title: Settings → Account is a dead end for a guest, and Settings offers no way to sign in
confirmed.evidence: The 'Account' NavigationLink and 'Sign in on the web' sit outside the `if authService.isAuthenticated` guard; only Sign Out and Delete account are inside it. A guest sees person.circle.fill, 'Not signed in', 'Email —', 'Member since —', and one button that opens a QR scanner requiring the session they lack. There is no 'Sign in / Create an account' row on either screen.
confirmed.fix: A signed-out Account state that is one sentence and a 'Create your account' button raising presentedSheet = .auth; hide the QR row for guests.
confirmed.codeNote: Code-verified line for line. SettingsView.swift:62-70 (Account NavigationLink) and :71-76 ('Sign in on the web') sit ABOVE the `if authService.isAuthenticated` at :77; only Sign Out and Delete account are inside it. AccountView for a guest resolves to person.circle.fill + 'Not signed in' (:119-123), 'Email —' (:135, the `?? "—"` branch), 'Member since —' (:243-245 guard), and the QR button (:161-180) which is outside the :183 guard. There is no .auth affordance on either screen — AppCoordinator.PresentedSheet has a `.auth` case (ContentView.swift:111-112) that neither screen ever raises. Guest mode is reachable (AppCoordinator.derivePhase :258-270 returns .main when guestModeOptIn); shots/B/19 and /21 walk it. Confirmed as written.
confirmed.judgeNote: Highest-leverage finding in this area — it sits on the conversion path. Code confirms it: SettingsView.swift:61-76 puts the Account NavigationLink and 'Sign in on the web' OUTSIDE the `if authService.isAuthenticated` guard (only Sign Out / Delete account are inside, :76-95). A guest who does the obvious thing — open Settings, tap Account — lands on person.circle.fill / 'Not signed in' / 'Email —' / 'Member since —' and one button that opens a camera QR scanner requiring the session they don't have. Not a blocker: AppCoordinator has a `.auth` sheet and NotificationFeedView.swift:195 + CompanionOverlay.swift:682 do raise it, so sign-in is reachable elsewhere. But Settings→Account is where a homeowner looks for 'sign in', and a beta round is measured on how many guests convert. Fix is S and self-contained (a signed-out Account state + a 'Create your account' row raising presentedSheet = .auth).

confirmed.title: Delete account runs a 30-second network call with no in-flight state
confirmed.evidence: Both surfaces declare `@State private var isDeletingAccount` and neither reads it — no spinner, no .disabled, no label change. deleteAccount() sets timeoutInterval = 30s. After confirming the destructive alert the row is unchanged; a second tap re-opens the alert whose confirm silently no-ops on `guard !isDeletingAccount`. On production this call currently 404s (A4-04), so the real experience is: tap, confirm, nothing for 30s, then one sentence.
confirmed.fix: Read isDeletingAccount — disable the row and swap the label for a ProgressView.
confirmed.codeNote: Core claim CONFIRMED, duration claim wrong. Verified: `@State private var isDeletingAccount` is declared at AccountView.swift:20 and SettingsView.swift:28, written at AccountView :88/:103 and SettingsView :220/:235, and read ONLY by the re-entrancy guards at AccountView:87 and SettingsView:219 — it appears in neither view's body, so there is no ProgressView, no .disabled, no label swap on either surface. A second tap does re-present the alert and its confirm silently no-ops. AccountDeletionService.swift:65 sets timeoutInterval = APIConfiguration.requestTimeout = 30.0 (APIConfiguration.swift:147). ADJUST the description: 'nothing for 30s' is the worst case, not the real one — on prod the endpoint 404s (A4-04) and URLSession returns in well under a second, so today's actual experience is tap → confirm → an immediate failure sentence. The 30s dead window only materialises on a hung/slow connection. Keep major (a destructive action with zero in-flight feedback), correct the wording.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed as written; the defect is masked today because the 404 returns fast and shows the failure sentence. The important consequence the finding doesn't state: A4-04's server fix CREATES this defect's visible form. The moment delete-account works, a tester who confirms gets 30 seconds of a completely unchanged row with no spinner, and a second tap silently no-ops on `guard !isDeletingAccount`. So the two are coupled — do not deploy delete-account to production until a build carrying the in-flight state has shipped, or take the A4-04 'hide the row' path in build 1 and land both together in build 2. T1 rather than T0 only because it needs a binary; the sequencing rule is the real deliverable here.

confirmed.title: The splash holds 1.5s on every cold launch and its own animation never finishes
confirmed.evidence: splashMinimumDuration = 1.5 is an unconditional floor in derivePhase() (`Date() < splashMinimumDeadline` ⇒ .launching), applied even when the session restores instantly. The wordmark animates .easeOut(duration: 2.0), so it is still short of full opacity when the phase flips at 1.5s. Sign-out pays the floor again via beginSplashTransition.
confirmed.fix: Bring the wordmark fade to ≤1.2s and drop the floor to ~0.6s (or 0 when isAuthStateReady is already true).
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED verbatim. AppCoordinator.swift:77 `splashMinimumDeadline: Date = Date().addingTimeInterval(1.5)`, :81 `static let splashMinimumDuration: TimeInterval = 1.5`, and derivePhase() at :258-262 returns `.launching` when `Date() < splashMinimumDeadline` regardless of auth readiness — an unconditional floor. SplashView.swift:44-47 animates the wordmark `.easeOut(duration: 2.0)` and :49-51 the strata lines `.easeOut(duration: 1.0).delay(0.5)`, so the mark is cut short of full opacity when the phase flips at 1.5 s; :53-58 documents that the view deliberately never self-completes. beginSplashTransition (AppCoordinator.swift:276) re-arms the same floor on sign-out.
confirmed.judgeNote: Minor in isolation but T0 because it is S-effort and sits inside the first three seconds: ~1s init + 1.5s unconditional floor + 0.5s crossfade ≈ 3s to content, with the wordmark visibly cut mid-fade at 1.5s of a 2.0s animation. Sign-out pays it again, so a tester switching accounts feels it twice. Caveat for the fixer: dropping the floor alone buys little while PatinaApp.init() still costs ~1.2s (C7-12) — align the animation to the deadline first, and gate the shortened floor on isAuthStateReady.

confirmed.title: .launching has no timeout: if auth readiness never lands, the splash is terminal
confirmed.evidence: derivePhase() returns .launching whenever !isAuthStateReady, and isAuthStateReady is set only from inside the `for await` over supabase.auth.authStateChanges (AuthService.swift:127-141). If the stream never yields — a failing keychain read is the recorded precedent, documented at Core/Network/SupabaseClient.swift:16-22 — there is no deadline, no retry, and SplashView deliberately never self-completes.
confirmed.fix: A 5–8s watchdog that forces .auth with a one-line 'We couldn't reach Patina — try again'.
confirmed.codeNote: The CODE FACT is confirmed — derivePhase() (AppCoordinator.swift:258-262) has no deadline on `!isAuthStateReady`, the only Task.sleep in the file is the splash-deadline tick (:156-160), isAuthStateReady is set only from markAuthStateReady() inside the authStateChanges loop (AuthService.swift:117-126, 136), and SplashView never self-completes. But the CITED PRECEDENT is refuted by this program's own evidence: P-log-launch.txt:792,797 show exactly the 'failing keychain read' case (`Failed to retrieve session: errSecItemNotFound` x2) and the stream still yielded — the app left `.launching` and reached Welcome in the same launch. supabase-swift with `emitLocalSessionAsInitialSession: true` (SupabaseClient.swift:56-58) emits `.initialSession` with a nil session rather than staying silent. So the terminal splash is a theoretical hole with no observed trigger: downgrade to polish / not tester-visible, and treat the watchdog as cheap insurance rather than a known failure.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity raised minor→major: framing understates it. A terminal splash is the one failure a TestFlight round cannot survive — the tester cannot proceed, cannot describe it beyond 'it never opened', and cannot be helped without shipping a whole new build. Probability is low (keychain-read precedent) but impact is total and the fix is an S-effort watchdog. Pure insurance you buy before build 1, not after.

confirmed.title: Sign-out never clears the navigation stack, so the next account remounts the previous one's screen
confirmed.where: App/Coordinators/AppCoordinator.swift:206-230,276-280 (only :330 and :694-698 reset the path, neither on the sign-out path)
confirmed.evidence: beginSplashTransition() moves the phase and reschedules the deadline; recomputePhase clears presentedSheet on the .auth/.launching transition and nothing else. SessionScope.reset() clears the data singletons thoroughly (SessionScope.swift:45-59) but not navigationPath or TabNavigationModel. On the next sign-in legacyMainContent remounts NavigationStack(path:) with the stack the previous account left.
confirmed.fix: Clear navigationPath and pop every tab to root inside beginSplashTransition().
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED as code truth (not observed on device). beginSplashTransition (AppCoordinator.swift:276-280) only moves splashMinimumDeadline and recomputes; recomputePhase (:206-230) clears presentedSheet on the .auth/.launching transition and nothing else. The only two navigationPath resets are :330 (the .heroFrame route inside navigate) and :693-694 (resetToThreshold), neither on the sign-out path. SessionScope.reset() clears eleven data singletons, not navigation. Low tester impact for a first round (one account per device), which is why it is T2 rather than T1.
confirmed.judgeNote: Needs two accounts on one device, which round 1 will rarely produce (one tester, one phone, one invite). Real bug, and it will bite Kody's demo device first. Build 3.

confirmed.title: Session expiry ejects to the welcome screen with no explanation
confirmed.evidence: A revoked or rotated-out refresh token makes the SDK drop the session and emit .signedOut from whatever request was in flight. The phase machine flips .main → .auth and renders AuthScreenView with errorMessage == nil. Nothing tells the person their session ended or that their place was saved.
confirmed.fix: Set a one-line notice ('You were signed out — sign in to pick up where you left off') when the .auth arrival carries a pendingReturnRoute.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED and canonical for the silent-eject family (C7-18 and C-55 fold in here). The SDK drops the session and emits .signedOut from whatever request was in flight; AuthService.refreshSession's catch (:674-678) calls applySession(nil) and rethrows without setting errorMessage, so recomputePhase flips .main → .auth and ContentView renders AuthScreenView with errorMessage == nil — a bare Welcome screen. I confirmed the ingredient the fix needs already exists: pendingReturnRoute is set at AppCoordinator.swift:214-216 on exactly this transition and drained at :250, so keying the notice on it is a two-line change.
confirmed.judgeNote: Canonical for the silent-ejection cluster (C7-18, C-55). One sentence of copy when .auth is entered carrying a pendingReturnRoute. Cheap, and it is the whole difference between 'the app logged me out' and 'the app broke' in a tester's feedback note. Build 2.

confirmed.title: The quiz RPC's HTTP status is ignored, so a rejection is parsed as a profile
confirmed.evidence: `let (data, _) = try await session.data(for: request)` discards the response. A 401/403 (every guest — the RPC grants authenticated only) or a 500 returns a PostgREST error object, which StyleProfileResult.from(serverResponse:fallback:) (QuizModels.swift:166-201) walks field-by-field, finds nothing, and silently replaces with the local result. The sibling method three functions up does guard the status and throws ProductAPIError.http.
confirmed.fix: The same status guard fetchRecommendations already has.
confirmed.codeNote: The defect is real; the stated consequence is not established. Real: ProductAPIClient.swift:214 `let (data, _) = try await session.data(for: request)` discards the response, while fetchRecommendations at :60-66 does guard the status and throws ProductAPIError.http — an inconsistency inside one file, and any error body would be walked field-by-field by StyleProfileResult.from(serverResponse:fallback:) and silently replaced by the local result. Not established: 'a 401/403 (every guest — the RPC grants authenticated only)'. Migrations grant process_style_quiz only TO authenticated (00067:238, 00246:190) and the app creates no anonymous Supabase session (GuestSessionStore is a local UserDefaults flag; no signInAnonymously anywhere), so a guest calls as PostgREST `anon` — yet shots/A/13 shows a guest receiving the server-authoritative 'Warm Modern'. Supabase's default privileges evidently grant anon EXECUTE on the walked stack (MEMORY records the same trap on prod). So the guest path is silently succeeding, not silently failing; fix the missing status guard on its own merits.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correctly marked not tester-visible — the local fallback is a reasonable profile — but T1 rather than T2 because it is the guard that makes A-25 diagnosable at all: today the app cannot distinguish 'server answered' from 'server refused' and will silently swallow both. The sibling fetchRecommendations three functions up already has the exact guard, so this is a copy-paste fix.

confirmed.title: Quiz answers survive only an explicit "Save progress & exit"
confirmed.evidence: saveProgress() writes styleQuiz.savedProgress.v1 and is called from exactly one place — the confirmation dialog's 'Save progress & exit', which itself only exists on the non-onboarding mount. A call, a home-swipe or a kill mid-quiz loses every answer, and the onboarding tester cannot reach the save at all.
confirmed.fix: Call saveProgress() on .onDisappear / scenePhase != .active; restore already covers both mounts.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed by grep. saveProgress() (StyleQuizViewModel:80-85) has exactly one caller — StyleQuizView.swift:82, the 'Save progress & exit' button inside the confirmationDialog, which is reachable only from the exitButton, which renders only `if onComplete == nil` (:69-75). The onboarding tester therefore cannot reach the save at all, and restoreSavedProgress() (:94-99) has nothing to restore. There is no .onDisappear/scenePhase hook. Directly compounds A-15/B-21: the only escape from the exitless quiz is a force-quit, which costs every answer.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raising from minor to major and pulling into T0. In an OPTIONAL quiz, losing progress is an annoyance; in a mandatory gate it means a tester who takes a phone call mid-quiz — which will happen — must redo the whole thing to enter the app at all, with no skip. saveProgress() has exactly one caller, inside a dialog the onboarding mount never shows. One .onDisappear/scenePhase call; restore already covers both mounts.

confirmed.title: Features/FirstLaunch's coordinator, state machine and metrics are dead code
confirmed.evidence: grep for FirstLaunchCoordinator, FirstLaunchState and WalkInvitationChoice across Patina/, PatinaTests/ and PatinaUITests/ returns only the declaring files. The live onboarding machine is OnboardingFlowHost.Step (four cases, :33-44). ~525 lines of a second, contradictory onboarding model ship in the binary — and research/A4-reconciliation.md cites FirstLaunchCoordinator.swift:101-113 as its evidence that U33 is fixed, which is not where the fix lives (OnboardingFlowView.quizPage:55-60 is).
confirmed.fix: Delete the three files; keep CameraPermissionView and OnboardingFunnel, which the host does use.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. FirstLaunchCoordinator.swift (254 lines), FirstLaunchState.swift (144), FirstLaunchMetrics.swift (127) = 525; grep across Patina/, PatinaTests/, PatinaUITests/ finds FirstLaunchCoordinator, FirstLaunchState and WalkInvitationChoice only inside those files. Live machine is OnboardingFlowHost.Step (:31-38, four cases). Two additions for the fix: FirstLaunchMetrics is also referenced by Patina/Core/Persistence/FirstLaunchDataStore.swift:38-56, itself dead (only named as a string in PatinaTests/SessionIsolationTests.swift:269) — that is four files to delete, not three, or the build breaks; and the @Entry environment key `firstLaunchCoordinator` (FirstLaunchCoordinator.swift:253) is never set or read. The A4 mis-citation is confirmed: research/A4-reconciliation.md:77 marks U33 'fixed' citing FirstLaunchCoordinator.swift:101-113 (dead code); the live fix is OnboardingFlowView.swift:54-60 `quizPage` — 'Your camera comes later — only when you choose to scan a room.'
confirmed.judgeNote: 525 lines in the binary costs a tester nothing, so this is polish on severity — but T1 on sequencing, same logic as A1-07. First-run is the highest-value surface in a TestFlight round, so the fix program will be editing onboarding in week 1, and two contradictory onboarding models with only one live is exactly how a week-1 fix lands in the dead file. Delete the three files before that lane opens. Separately: I checked the U33 claim and there is NO verification gap — the live fix is present (OnboardingFlowView.swift:7 carries the U33 comment, quizPage:55). research/A4-reconciliation.md just cites the wrong file; that is a one-line documentation correction, not a re-verification.

confirmed.title: "Privacy Policy" and "Terms of Service" open the same page
confirmed.evidence: termsURL and privacyURL are both https://patina.cloud/terms; the comment concedes it ('the app knows no separate privacy route'). This is the one legal claim the first screen makes, on the consent line directly under the sign-in buttons.
confirmed.fix: Publish /privacy and point at it; until then render one link labelled 'Terms & Privacy'.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED verbatim. AuthScreenView.swift:175-176 reads `private static let termsURL = URL(string: "https://patina.cloud/terms")!` and `private static let privacyURL = URL(string: "https://patina.cloud/terms")!` — identical, with the comment at :173-174 conceding it ('Combined Terms & Privacy page — mirrors the URL behind SettingsView's "Terms & Privacy" Support row'). Tiered T0 despite minor severity: App Review requires a working privacy-policy link and this is a one-line fix on the first screen.
confirmed.judgeNote: Adjusted up from minor: this is the one legal claim the first screen makes, sitting on the consent line directly under the sign-in buttons, and App Review requires a working privacy-policy link. Understating it as 'minor' risks it sliding past build 1 for the sake of a two-line change. Either publish /privacy or render a single link labelled 'Terms & Privacy' — both are S and both close it before ship.

confirmed.title: A QR deep link silently ejects a guest to the welcome screen
confirmed.evidence: `coordinator?.guestModeOptIn = false` with no message, no sheet and no record of why. It also does not clear GuestSessionStore, so the next cold launch restores guest mode and the ejection looks random. It is also the ordering that makes C1-10 reachable.
confirmed.fix: Raise presentedSheet = .auth over the current screen (the AuthSheet pattern U21 established) instead of changing the phase.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED and canonical (C2-23 is the same finding). DeepLinkHandler.swift:163-169 sets coordinator?.guestModeOptIn = false and returns with nothing presented, while handle() has already returned true so nothing upstream explains it. The sub-claim about persistence is right too: only the coordinator's in-memory flag is cleared — GuestSessionStore.shared is untouched here (AuthService.swift:188 clears it only on .signedOut), and AppCoordinator.swift:92 seeds guestModeOptIn from GuestSessionStore.shared.isOptedIn at init, so the next cold launch restores guest mode and the ejection reads as random.
confirmed.judgeNote: Canonical over C2-23. QR sign-in is the designer/Field path; a round-1 homeowner will not meet it. Real — and the non-cleared GuestSessionStore makes the NEXT launch look random, which is the nastier half — but build 3.

confirmed.title: The Reveal spells the aesthetic name one letter per view, at a fixed 42pt, in a stack that cannot wrap
confirmed.evidence: HStack(spacing: 0) { ForEach(chars.indices) { Text(String(chars[i])).font(.custom("PlayfairDisplay-Light", size: 42)) } } with .fixedSize. An HStack of single characters cannot line-break, and .font(.custom(_:size:)) without relativeTo: ignores Dynamic Type entirely. The .accessibilityLabel on the HStack does not collapse the children (no accessibilityElement(children:)), so VoiceOver reads the name letter by letter. The spectrum bar carries no label or value, and `normalized[safe: index] ?? 0.2` invents a fifth of the bar when the engine returns fewer values.
confirmed.fix: One Text with a per-character opacity mask, relativeTo: .largeTitle, and .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).
confirmed.codeNote: Code facts all confirmed at RevealView.swift:80-93 — `HStack(spacing: 0)` of per-character `Text`s at `.font(.custom("PlayfairDisplay-Light", size: 42))` with no `relativeTo:` (so Dynamic Type is ignored outright), `.accessibilityLabel(Text(profile.aestheticName))` at :92 with no `.accessibilityElement(children:)`, and the spectrum bar at :97-119 carrying no label or value with `normalized[safe: index] ?? 0.2` at :107. Two corrections: the `.fixedSize` at :91 is vertical-only (`horizontal: false`), and the VoiceOver failure mode is label propagation — applying a label to a container without making it an element repeats the WHOLE name on every letter, rather than spelling it out. Not verified on a device/sim in this audit.
confirmed.judgeNote: The letter-by-letter VoiceOver reading is T2, but two sighted risks on a hero first-five-minutes moment justify a look now: a non-wrapping HStack of 42pt characters has no way to fit a long aesthetic name on a 402pt screen, and `normalized[safe: index] ?? 0.2` DRAWS AN INVENTED fifth bar when the engine returns fewer values. That second one is a data-honesty bug, not an accessibility bug — hand it to the product/copy lane so it is not lost in an a11y backlog.

confirmed.title: The phase change is animated twice, with two different curves
confirmed.evidence: `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.5), value: coordinator.phase)` on the ZStack and `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.4)) { phase = newPhase }` in recomputePhase both fire for the same mutation; the branches also carry their own .transition(.opacity). Splash→welcome and welcome→onboarding read as a soft double-fade.
confirmed.fix: Keep the coordinator's withAnimation and drop the view modifier (or the reverse), once.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed verbatim: ContentView.swift:81 `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.5), value: coordinator.phase)` and AppCoordinator.swift:227-229 `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.4)) { phase = newPhase }` both fire on the same mutation, and the branches carry their own .transition(.opacity). Genuine S fix. Part of the same untended motion layer as C3-19.
confirmed.judgeNote: Two animations on one mutation, 0.5s and 0.4s, plus per-branch transitions — and it fires on splash→welcome, the first thing a tester ever sees. A soft double-fade is subtle enough that nobody names it, but launch is exactly where crispness registers subconsciously. Deleting one of the two is a one-line change.

confirmed.title: Six digits entered does not verify, and the green success banner stays up over the red failure
confirmed.evidence: The field caps at six digits and Verify enables at six, but nothing submits — the tester must dismiss the number pad (which covers the button) and tap. On a wrong code verifyOtp clears otpToken and sets errorMessage, while successMessage ('We emailed you a 6-digit code', set at :194) is never cleared, so both banners render stacked. This is the only working sign-in path on production (A3), so its friction is the funnel.
confirmed.fix: Auto-verify on the sixth digit; clear successMessage when an error lands.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. The auto-verify half is the distinct claim and it holds: AuthenticationView.swift:338-346's onChange only strips non-digits and caps at six, Verify enables at six (:376), and nothing calls verifyOtp on change — so the tester must dismiss a .numberPad that has no Done key (C9-08) to reach a button sitting below the fold (P-22). The stacked-banner half duplicates P-22; merge the two when planning the fix so 'clear successMessage on error' is written once.
confirmed.judgeNote: Under-rated at polish — raise to major/T0. This sits on the ONLY sign-in path that works on production (A3-06 kills Google, A3-16 kills the shared credential, Apple mis-roles the user), and 'six digits typed, nothing happens, the number pad covers Verify' is exactly where the funnel ends. Auto-verify on the sixth digit is S and defuses the C9-08 dependency for this screen on its own.

confirmed.title: SplashView.onComplete is dead and ContentView's comment describes behaviour that does not exist
confirmed.evidence: The closure is required by the initializer and deliberately never invoked; ContentView passes an empty one under a comment claiming 'Splash's intrinsic 2s onComplete fires after the animation' — a stale claim sitting directly above the phase machine every reader starts with.
confirmed.fix: Drop the parameter and the comment.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. `var onComplete: () -> Void` (SplashView.swift:16) is required by the memberwise init and SplashView.swift:55-59 states it is 'retained for API compatibility but is intentionally not invoked'. ContentView.swift:27 is the only mount besides the file's own #Preview:71. Nuance that softens the framing: ContentView:28-33 does open with the false 'Splash's intrinsic 2s onComplete fires after the animation', but the next three lines correct it ('The phase observer is what actually transitions out of `.launching`… this closure is a no-op kept only because SplashView's API requires one'), so no reader is left with the wrong model — a stale first sentence, not a misleading comment.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correct and trivial. The only thing raising it above pure noise is location: the stale comment sits directly above the launch phase machine, and cold launch is a first-impression surface the program will touch in week 1. So do not schedule it as a standalone ticket — delete the parameter and the comment inside whatever commit next touches splash or launch timing. If nothing touches splash, T2 cleanup is fine and nobody is harmed.

confirmed.title: The email-code sheet's header contradicts the panel under it
confirmed.evidence: After the code is sent the header still reads 'Continue with email' / 'We'll email you a sign-in code — no password needed' while the body says 'Enter your sign-in code' / 'Enter the 6-digit code from your email' — two headings and one instruction, twice.
confirmed.fix: Switch the header to 'Check your email' once magicLinkSent is true.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. headerTitle (:116-123) returns 'Continue with email' for .magicLink unconditionally and headerSubtitle (:125-139) returns "We'll email you a sign-in code — no password needed" — neither consults magicLinkSent. formContent (:174-181) swaps only the body beneath that unchanged header, into either magicLinkSentView ('Check your email' / 'We sent a magic link to') or otpEntryView ('Enter your sign-in code' / 'Enter the 6-digit code from your email'). Two stacked headings in both branches.
confirmed.judgeNote: Two headings and one instruction, twice, on the screen where a tester is waiting for a code and most likely to think something has gone wrong. Correctly scoped as polish, but it sits in the same file and the same pass as P-30's T0 naming fix — schedule them together and it costs nothing extra. T1.

confirmed.title: The sign-up confirmation link opens the website; the resend's opens the app
confirmed.evidence: signUp passes only email, password and data, so GoTrue falls back to the project SITE_URL; resendVerificationEmail passes the app's custom scheme. The recovery panel's copy — 'Tap the link in that email, then come back here to sign in.' (AuthenticationView.swift:434) — is written for the first case and wrong for the second, which signs them in directly.
confirmed.fix: Pass redirectTo on signUp too and make the panel copy match.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. AuthService.signUp (:441-445) passes only email, password and data — no redirectTo — so GoTrue falls back to SITE_URL, while resendVerificationEmail (:514-518) passes emailRedirectTo: patina://auth/callback. The recovery panel's copy at AuthenticationView.swift:434 ('Tap the link in that email, then come back here to sign in.') is written for the first case and wrong for the second. Reachability confirmed: my Strata probe returns mailer_autoconfirm:false, so signUp really does return a user with no session and really does route to this panel — but only via the password Create Account path, which is the secondary route behind 'Don't have an account? Sign Up' (:632).
confirmed.judgeNote: Only bites testers who create a password account, which some will. The visible half is the panel copy being written for the wrong one of the two paths; both are one small edit. Build 2.

confirmed.title: The style conversation dead-ends silently if both scoring engines fail
confirmed.evidence: `let fallback = try? await LocalAestheteEngine().score(request); if let fallback { … }` with no else. onFinished? is never called, no error is set, and the container stays on the pause screen. The comment concedes the shape: 'The HTTP stub currently throws; LocalAestheteEngine should always succeed.'
confirmed.fix: An else branch that surfaces a retry, or make the local engine non-throwing.
confirmed.codeNote: Verbatim confirmed at StyleConversationViewModel.swift:229-240: `let fallback = try? await LocalAestheteEngine().score(request); if let fallback { … }` with no else — onFinished? is never called, no error state is set, and the comment concedes the shape ('The HTTP stub currently throws; LocalAestheteEngine should always succeed'). Correctly filed as low-probability (both engines must fail) and not tester-visible on the shipped quiz-first path — the style conversation is reached via the walk-first scan flow, which is behind the onboarding_walk_first PostHog flag and therefore OFF for a first-launch TestFlight tester.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correctly flagged as low probability (the source comment says the local engine should always succeed). Also low first-round exposure: Style Conversation is a Companion surface, and on a flag-off first launch testers reach the quiz, not this. Still a silent dead-end with no error and no retry, which is the pattern this audit keeps finding — worth the else branch when the area is next opened.

confirmed.title: Dead code in the auth button component
confirmed.evidence: AuthButton.iconImage (:152-155) has no caller; the .apple variant appears only in the file's own #Preview (:206) — the real Apple button is PatinaSignInWithAppleButton.
confirmed.fix: Remove both, or wire iconImage up as part of C1-24.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified. `AuthButton.iconImage` (PatinaDesignKit/Sources/PatinaDesignKit/Components/PatinaButton.swift:152-155) has no reader — the body renders `Text(icon)` at :159-162 instead, which is exactly why the Welcome screen ships an ✉ glyph as text rather than an SF Symbol. `.apple` is constructed only at :206 in the file's own #Preview; the two live call sites are AuthScreenView.swift:82 (.google) and :85 (.email), and the real Apple button is PatinaSignInWithAppleButton.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed, no tester impact, and correctly identified as a ride-along. Do not open a ticket: fold both the unused iconImage and the .apple variant into C1-24's auth-button work, where whoever is already in PatinaButton.swift can decide in context whether iconImage gets wired or removed. Deleting it standalone risks a pointless conflict with that lane.

confirmed.title: Onboarding completion and the quiz's saved progress are device-global and survive sign-out
confirmed.evidence: hasCompletedOnboarding is a UserDefaults flag with no account in the key, and neither signOut() nor LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData() touches it — nor styleQuiz.savedProgress.v1. A second account on the device never sees the carousel or the quiz, lands on an empty home with no style profile, and can inherit the first person's half-finished quiz answers. Sibling of A4-10, which found the same shape in the taste portrait.
confirmed.fix: Scope both keys per-user, or clear them alongside LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData().
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. hasCompletedOnboarding is a plain UserDefaults key with no account in it (UserDefaultsBacked.swift:55, :84) and styleQuiz.savedProgress.v1 likewise (StyleQuizViewModel.swift:68, written :83, removed only by :89). Neither AuthService.signOut (:479-497) nor LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData touches them — and that method's own comment shows the shape was found and fixed once already for the taste portrait (it calls StyleProfileStore.shared.reset() for exactly this reason) but the quiz-progress key was missed. derivePhase (AppCoordinator.swift:267) then routes a second account straight to .main. Low first-round impact (one account per tester), hence T2.
confirmed.judgeNote: Round 1 is one account per device, so the second-account symptom mostly hits Kody's demo phone. The inherited half-finished quiz answers are the genuinely ugly part if it does happen. Build 3, alongside A4-10's sibling in the taste portrait.

confirmed.title: A cold-launch notification tap is handled twice (route pushed twice, markOpened twice)
confirmed.evidence: didFinishLaunchingWithOptions installs the UNUserNotificationCenter delegate at :42 and then calls handleNotificationPayload(userInfo, source: "cold_launch") for launchOptions[.remoteNotification] at :44-46. iOS then also calls userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:) at :141-147, which calls handleNotificationPayload(userInfo, source: "tap"). There is no dedupe on notification_log_id and no launch flag. Each call runs DeepLinkHandler.shared.navigate(to: resolved) -> coordinator.openExternal (a push) and NotificationsAPIClient.markOpened.
confirmed.fix: Dedupe on notification_log_id, or drop the launchOptions branch entirely — the UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate covers the tap case on every supported iOS.
confirmed.codeNote: Double handling is real code truth — AppDelegate.swift:44-46 (launchOptions[.remoteNotification]) and :141-147 (didReceive) both call handleNotificationPayload with no notification_log_id dedupe and no launch flag, which is exactly the pattern Apple's own guidance says to drop once UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate is installed. But the stated consequence overstates: the duplicate PUSH only materialises when DeepLinkHandler.configure(coordinator:) (PatinaApp.swift:102-105, root .onAppear) has already drained pendingRoute before didReceive arrives; in the other ordering DeepLinkHandler.navigate stashes into pendingRoute (DeepLinkHandler.swift:44-50) and the second call simply overwrites it with the same route, collapsing to one navigation. The guaranteed effect is a duplicate markOpened PATCH, which is idempotent (same opened_at/status body). Downgrade major → minor.
confirmed.judgeNote: Downgrading from major on impact, not on mechanism (the double-fire is real — iOS populates launchOptions[.remoteNotification] AND calls didReceive on a cold-launch tap). Unreachable in round 1 because C2-05 means no push is ever sent, so testerVisible is false for build 1. When push does go live the symptom is confusing rather than damaging: the destination is pushed twice, so Back lands the tester on the same screen again and they think the app ignored them — plus a duplicated markOpened that further muddies the metrics C2-17 is already muddying. Ships with C2-05 in the same week-one landing; the cleanest form of the fix is deleting the launchOptions branch outright, since the delegate covers the tap case on every supported iOS.

confirmed.title: Universal link arriving before configure(coordinator:) is dropped, yet reported handled
confirmed.evidence: `if let coordinator, coordinator.phase == .launching { coordinator.pendingDeepLink = url } else { coordinator?.openExternal(route) }; return true` — when coordinator is nil (configure runs from ContentView's .onAppear, PatinaApp.swift:102-105, while .onOpenURL is registered on the same view at :99-101) the else branch is a silent no-op and the method still returns true. The widget branch (:286-290) and the APNs branch (:46-52) both stash into pendingRoute for exactly this case; only the universal-link branch does not.
confirmed.fix: Use the same stash-or-open pair the widget branch uses: when coordinator == nil, set pendingRoute = route.
confirmed.codeNote: The code asymmetry is exactly as quoted and is real: DeepLinkHandler.swift:64-71 returns true after `coordinator?.openExternal(route)`, a silent no-op when coordinator is nil, while the widget branch (:284-291) and navigate(to:) (:44-49) both stash into pendingRoute, and configure() replays it (:34-39). configure is called only from ContentView's .onAppear (PatinaApp.swift:102-105), verified as the only call site. Downgraded because the window is unproven: no lane's evidence shows onOpenURL firing before onAppear, and for a round-1 (signed-out) tester the link dies anyway on the C2-21 path whether or not it is stashed. One-line fix, correct location — treat it as a sub-item of the single deep-link entry fix, not a standalone major.
confirmed.judgeNote: Adjusted up from the stated 0.6/major framing: the trigger is understated. coordinator == nil is precisely the cold-launch window — app not running, tester taps a client.patina.cloud link in Mail, .onOpenURL fires against a ContentView whose .onAppear has not yet run configure() — and cold launch from an email is THE canonical universal-link path for a first-round tester, not an edge race. Returning true while dropping the route also means nothing downstream can compensate. Confirmed by inspection: the widget branch (:286-290) and the APNs branch (:46-52) both stash into pendingRoute for exactly this case and the universal-link branch does not, so the fix is the existing pattern applied to one more branch (S). Not marked dupOf C2-21 deliberately — C2-21's fix (queue on phase) does not touch the nil-coordinator path, and collapsing them risks shipping half the fix.

confirmed.title: Settings "Notifications" toggle is inert on every side (defaults ON, never asks, never honoured)
confirmed.evidence: The row binds settings.notificationsEnabled (default true, SettingsService.swift:30) to user_settings.push_notifications. It never calls PushTokenService.requestAuthorizationAndRegister(), never reads UNUserNotificationCenter.notificationSettings(), and never deletes the device token. Server-side, grep for `push_notifications` across supabase/functions/ returns nothing — apns-send reads device_push_tokens only.
confirmed.fix: Drive the row from notificationSettings().authorizationStatus: .notDetermined -> present the primer; .denied -> one sentence + openSettingsURLString. Make apns-send honour user_settings.push_notifications, or delete the row.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified on all three sides. App: SettingsView.swift:109-117 binds the row straight to SettingsService.setNotificationsEnabled; SettingsService.swift:123-130 only upserts user_settings.push_notifications and notification_preferences.channels_push — it never touches UNUserNotificationCenter, never calls PushTokenService.requestAuthorizationAndRegister(), never deletes the token row. Default is `true` (SettingsService.swift:30), so the switch shows ON before iOS has ever asked. A primer DOES exist (PushPrimerView.swift:53 is the only caller of requestAuthorizationAndRegister app-wide) — the Settings row simply is not wired to it. Server: `grep -rn push_notifications supabase/functions/` returns zero hits; apns-send/index.ts:130,139,198 reads and prunes device_push_tokens only, and consults neither user_settings nor notification_preferences. Confirmed as written, effort M is right.
confirmed.judgeNote: 'Never asks' over-states it — the app DOES have a proper notification primer: shots/A/41-push-prompt.png shows a designed 'Turn on notifications' / 'Not now' screen raising the real iOS prompt during onboarding. The Settings row not calling requestAuthorization is true but is not the defect a tester meets. The defect that survives, and is sharper than filed, is the LIE: the row defaults ON (SettingsService.swift:30) and never reads UNUserNotificationCenter.notificationSettings(), so a tester who tapped 'Not now' or 'Don't Allow' at the primer later opens Settings and sees 'Notifications' switched on — directly contradicting iOS Settings, which they can check. Plus the server half stands (apns-send reads device_push_tokens only), so turning it off changes nothing. Major, T1: it needs both an app change and an edge-function change (M), and it is a second-week discovery rather than a first-five-minutes one.

confirmed.title: A first-round tester can never be asked for notification permission
confirmed.evidence: PushPrimerTrigger.shouldPresent requires hasMoneyMoment(in: rows) — a .proposal/.invoice/.decision row. presentPushPrimerIfEarned() (DailyRoomView:199-204) is the only product-code caller of requestAuthorizationAndRegister() (grep: the other hits are PushTokenService itself and InvoiceReminderService's separate [.alert] ask). There is no Settings path (C2-03) and no onboarding step.
confirmed.fix: Keep Q7's earned ask, but add a second explicit door: a Settings row that presents the same primer, sharing the once-per-install gate.
confirmed.codeNote: Title overstates — the ask IS reachable for any client with a proposal/invoice/decision in the feed, and PushPrimerTrigger.hasMoneyMoment (PushPrimerView.swift:84-91) counts the locally-composed Studio fallback rows too, so it fires on the first money moment either way (ruling Q7: 'the permission is earned'). Also mis-located: the only product caller of requestAuthorizationAndRegister() is PushPrimerView.swift:53, not presentPushPrimerIfEarned. What IS confirmed and is the real defect: there is no second door. SettingsView.swift:112-117's 'Notifications' toggle routes to SettingsService.setNotificationsEnabled (:123-130), which writes user_settings.push_notifications and notification_preferences and never touches UNUserNotificationCenter. And for the actual round-one account there is no money moment — Strata shows tester@patina.cloud with 0 invoices / 0 proposals / 0 decisions (research/A3-prod.md:282) — so push cannot be exercised at all in round one. Keep major with the corrected framing.
confirmed.judgeNote: The severity holds; the title overstates the round-1 case. Once A3-15 seeds a client account with a real proposal/invoice/decision, hasMoneyMoment is true and the primer DOES present — so 'can never be asked' is conditional on the account, not structural. Reframe it as the gap that genuinely bites over a week: there is no second door. A tester who taps 'Not now' (a rational first reflex on day one), or who was denied via C2-09, has no path back anywhere in the app — no Settings row, no onboarding step — and is silently opted out of the entire notification product for the round. That is the shape that loses you week-two retention data. M effort, build 2: one Settings row presenting the same primer, sharing the once-per-install gate, plus C2-09's status read so it can hand off to Settings when already denied.

confirmed.title: Sign-out leaves the previous account's screens on the navigation stack
confirmed.evidence: Sign-out runs presentedSheet = nil + beginSplashTransition() + signOut(). recomputePhase clears only presentedSheet when leaving .main (:223-225). navigationPath / tabs.paths / tabs.stacks are never cleared: `navigationPath = NavigationPath()` appears only in navigate(to: .heroFrame) (:330) and resetToThreshold() (:694, reachable only from the Companion .startOver intent). LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData() has no coordinator reference.
confirmed.fix: In beginSplashTransition() (or on the .main -> .auth/.launching transition) clear navigationPath, screenStack, every tabs stack, and reset tabs.selected = .today — the reset resetToThreshold() already spells out.
confirmed.codeNote: Real on main (d7287c3f8) and correctly located; every cited line number is exact. AppCoordinator:223-225 clears only presentedSheet when leaving .main; beginSplashTransition (:276-280) touches only splashMinimumDeadline + recomputePhase. `navigationPath = NavigationPath()` exists at exactly two sites — :330 (navigate(to: .heroFrame)) and :694 (resetToThreshold, whose only caller is :603, the Companion .startOver intent) — and TabNavigationModel.popToRoot is likewise reached only from resetToThreshold. LocalStoreReset.swift:24-72 has no coordinator reference, and AppCoordinator is not a SessionScope participant (SessionScope.swift:45-57, 11 participants). ContentView.swift:161-171 binds NavigationStack(path:) directly to coordinator.navigationPath and the coordinator outlives the phase flip, so re-entering .main re-mounts the retained stack. No test references signOut or beginSplashTransition, so nothing pins it. Two corrections that RAISE, not lower, the likelihood: (a) SettingsView:208-215 is not the only sign-out site — AccountView.swift:57-73 runs the identical presentedSheet=nil + beginSplashTransition() + signOut() triple, so the fix must live in the coordinator, not the view; (b) the settings sheet's real entry points are ProfileView.swift:161 and StudioHubView.swift:132 — both PUSHED routes (.profile/.studio) on the flag-off root that a first-round tester runs — plus CompanionOverlay.swift:680, which floats over any pushed screen. So the ordinary sign-out gesture nearly always fires with a non-empty navigationPath, and sign-in (or 'Continue as Guest', which also lands .main via guestModeOptIn) re-mounts Studio/Profile/detail instead of home. Add a secondary effect the entry misses: on a FORCED sign-out, :213-216 sets pendingReturnRoute = currentScreen while the path survives, so on re-auth recomputePhase's openExternal(route) pushes the same route on top of the restored stack — a duplicate entry where Back lands on the same screen twice. Fix as sketched (clear navigationPath, screenStack, every tabs stack, tabs.selected = .today) but place it in beginSplashTransition/the .main→.auth|.launching branch of recomputePhase so both sign-out call sites and the forced path are covered.
confirmed.judgeNote: Mechanism confirmed by reading. ContentView.swift:22-78 switches the root on `phase`, so the `.main` branch is torn down on sign-out while the coordinator survives; nothing on the sign-out path (SettingsView:208-215, AccountView:69/97, AuthService.signOut:479-497, LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData) touches `navigationPath`/`tabs`. `navigationPath = NavigationPath()` exists only at AppCoordinator:330 (.heroFrame) and :694 (resetToThreshold, reachable only from the Companion .startOver intent). On the next sign-in the retained path re-mounts the previous stack. Two things the write-up misses, both raising impact: (1) `.styleResult(result: StyleProfileResult)` (Coordinator.swift:71) carries a real payload, not an id — a retained path re-renders the PREVIOUS account's quiz result with no fetch and no RLS, walking straight past the account-isolation seam LocalStoreReset documents at length (it clears StyleProfileStore for exactly this reason); (2) on a FORCED sign-out the retained path and `pendingReturnRoute` (AppCoordinator:213-215 → openExternal at :253) both fire, so re-auth double-pushes the same route and Back lands on an identical screen — a visible 'unfinished' tell. Adjusting the framing, not the facts: the title implies account-switching, but the tester-reachable case in build 1 is same-account sign-out → sign-in landing deep in the stack instead of Today (flags are OFF on first launch, so it is the single flag-off stack; the tabs half of the fix only matters once house-first resolves on a second launch). Tier T1, not T0: a homeowner's first five minutes never touch it (a fresh install has no stack to leak), it is not a crash, dead end, data loss, or a beta-review blocker, and Back still works. But week one hits it — 'sign out and back in' is the universal user troubleshooting move, and Kody plus any tester handed the shared tester@patina.cloud account will cycle sessions on one device. Fix sketch is right and cheap; prefer the recomputePhase `.main → .auth/.launching` branch (AppCoordinator:220-225) over beginSplashTransition, since that one site also covers the forced path and kills the duplicate push — all four beginSplashTransition callers are sign-out/delete, so either site is safe. Note `navigationPath`'s didSet (:27-41) already cascades the clear into screenStack and currentScreen, so the flag-off half is one line plus the tabs popToRoot/`selected = .today` loop resetToThreshold already spells out. Effort S stands. Compile-green reading only; not sim-verified.

confirmed.title: The bell's unread badge stays stale after reading the feed
confirmed.evidence: Two independent NotificationsViewModel instances: DailyRoomView holds one in @State (:28) and computes the badge from it (:258); NotificationFeedView holds its own (:12), which is what markRead/markAllRead mutate. DailyRoomView reloads only from .task (:106-108, once per mount), onChange(of: isAuthenticated) (:164) and onChange(of: scenePhase) (:184). A pop back re-runs none of these.
confirmed.fix: Source the unread count from one shared @Observable service (BadgeCountService is already refreshed on the same triggers), or reload on the home's .onAppear.
confirmed.codeNote: Code truth confirmed: two independent NotificationsViewModel instances — DailyRoomView.swift:28 (@State) feeding the badge at :257 (unreadCount: notificationsViewModel.notifications.filter { !$0.isRead }.count) and NotificationFeedView.swift:12, which is the one markRead/markAllRead mutate. Real coupling defect worth fixing. But the observable symptom is NOT established: it hinges on SwiftUI's .task NOT restarting when DailyRoomView reappears after a NavigationStack pop, which this audit did not verify (no shot in shots/A or shots/C shows a stale badge after Mark all read; the ledger asserts it from code reading only). If .task does restart on reappear, load() refetches the already-PATCHed rows and the badge is correct. Downgrade major → minor pending a sim check: sign in, bell, Mark all read, Back, read the badge.
confirmed.judgeNote: Read every row, pop back, bell still badges 3. Homeowners are trained by every other app on their phone that a badge clears when they read the thing; a badge that lies is the fastest way to teach a tester to stop trusting — and ignore — the bell for the rest of the round, which quietly kills the feedback you want from week one. Two independent NotificationsViewModel instances is a clean, contained S fix (single shared source, or reload on the home's onAppear). Ship with A-80: together they are 'the badge and the list never agree', which is how a tester will actually phrase it in feedback.

confirmed.title: No app-icon badge in either direction, yet .badge is requested from the user
confirmed.evidence: willPresent returns [.banner, .list, .sound, .badge] and requestAuthorization asks for .badge, but buildApnsPayload emits no aps.badge key and grep for setBadgeCount|applicationIconBadgeNumber across apps/mobile/Patina returns only a test name (PatinaTests/SessionIsolationTests.swift:111). Nothing sets or clears the icon badge.
confirmed.fix: Either drop .badge from both the authorization and presentation options, or send aps.badge = attentionCount and clear with setBadgeCount(0) on foreground.
confirmed.codeNote: Verified stronger than claimed: grep for setBadgeCount|applicationIconBadgeNumber|setNotificationCategories|UNNotificationCategory across apps/mobile/Patina/{Patina,PatinaWidget,PatinaTests} returns ZERO hits — not even the SessionIsolationTests name the ledger cites. buildApnsPayload (apns-send/core.ts:60-73) emits only aps.alert + aps.sound plus the three routing keys, so no server side either. Meanwhile .badge is requested (PushTokenService.swift:69) and returned in willPresent (AppDelegate.swift:173). Confirmed as written.
confirmed.judgeNote: Flipping testerVisible to false. Nobody notices an absent icon badge, and with C2-05 unfixed no push arrives to badge anything; the app also already carries an in-app bell count, so the tester's attention is there. What remains is hygiene with a small honesty cost — the system permission sheet enumerates 'Badges' among what the app is asking for, and the app never uses it. Decide it once when push actually ships: either drop .badge from both the authorization and presentation options, or send aps.badge and clear on foreground. Later.

confirmed.title: "Turn on notifications" is a silent no-op when authorization was already denied
confirmed.evidence: requestAuthorizationAndRegister() is `guard granted else { return }` — no .denied branch, no message, no Settings hand-off. iOS shows the system alert once per install and InvoiceReminderService.requestAlertAuthorization ([.alert]) can consume it first. The primer's button then awaits an instant false, calls onDecided(), and the sheet closes. The once-per-install gate was already armed by presentPushPrimerIfEarned() (DailyRoomView.swift:201), so the ask is spent.
confirmed.fix: Read notificationSettings().authorizationStatus before asking; on .denied print the equivalent of InvoiceReminder.deniedLine and offer openSettingsURLString; do not arm the gate when nothing was asked.
confirmed.codeNote: Every element checks out. PushTokenService.requestAuthorizationAndRegister is `guard granted else { return }` with no .denied branch (Services/API/PushTokenService.swift:66-77). PushPrimerView.swift:51-56 awaits it and calls onDecided() unconditionally, so the sheet just closes. The gate was already burned by presentPushPrimerIfEarned's armAuthorizationPromptGate() BEFORE the sheet was shown (DailyRoomView.swift:199-204), so the one ask is spent whichever way the button goes. And the competing consumer is real: SystemNotificationScheduler.requestAlertAuthorization asks with options [.alert] (Services/Notifications/InvoiceReminderService.swift:70-77). The right sentence already exists one file away — InvoiceReminder.deniedLine = 'Notifications are off for Patina. You can turn them on in Settings.' (Services/Notifications/InvoiceReminder.swift:75), rendered at InvoiceReminderRow.swift:38 — the primer has no equivalent.
confirmed.judgeNote: The bar in the brief says 'no dead ends' explicitly, and this is the purest kind: the sheet's primary black capsule button, tapped, does nothing at all and dismisses. The round-1 path is live rather than theoretical — once A3-15 seeds a real invoice, InvoiceReminderService's separate [.alert] ask can consume the one system prompt per install before the primer ever runs, so the tester meets the pretty 'Before we interrupt you' sheet and a button that is already spent. Two S-sized parts, both build 1: read authorizationStatus before asking and branch to openSettingsURLString on .denied, and do not arm the once-per-install gate when nothing was actually asked.

confirmed.title: APNs token is not uploaded when a session starts without a background/foreground cycle
confirmed.evidence: uploadToken caches the hex and returns early with no session ("deferring upload"), pointing at reregisterIfAuthorized() for the retry — whose only caller is scenePhase == .active (PatinaApp.swift:174-176). Sign-out deletes the row (AuthService.swift:488) and nothing re-uploads in-session. There is no auth-state hook on the push path.
confirmed.fix: Call reregisterIfAuthorized() from the auth-state observer the coordinator already runs, or re-attempt the deferred upload from AuthService's sign-in path.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed on all three legs. uploadToken caches the hex then early-returns on a nil currentUserId with '[Push] device token registered but no session yet — deferring upload' (PushTokenService.swift:130-139). reregisterIfAuthorized()'s only caller is the scenePhase == .active branch (PatinaApp.swift:170-176). signOut() calls removeCurrentToken() before the session dies (AuthService.swift:485-488), and the authStateChanges listener (AuthService.swift:127-175) has no push hook of any kind — it hydrates ProfileService/SettingsService and nothing else. So grant → sign out → sign back in without backgrounding leaves device_push_tokens with no row for the session.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correctly scoped as minor. The blast radius is small in practice — reregisterIfAuthorized fires on the next foreground, and essentially every real user backgrounds the app within the first day, so the window where a token is missing is short and self-healing. It only becomes interesting after C2-05 lands and pushes start flowing, and even then it costs a delayed first push, not a lost one. Worth tidying alongside the auth-state observer work rather than as its own item.

confirmed.title: The push primer can present over Spaces / Pieces / Studio on the house-first root
confirmed.evidence: Every mounted tab stays in the ZStack at .opacity(tab == selected ? 1 : 0) and `mounted` is insert-only (:61-63), so Today never unmounts. DailyRoomView's .onChange(of: scenePhase) (:168) therefore fires on every foreground regardless of visible tab and ends in presentPushPrimerIfEarned() -> isPushPrimerPresented = true, whose .sheet (:192-193) is attached to that zero-opacity view. This is the same class of bug the first-launch tour fixed with TabNavigationModel.isShowingTodayRoot (:110-112).
confirmed.fix: Gate presentPushPrimerIfEarned() on coordinator.tabs.isShowingTodayRoot on the house-first root, exactly as FirstLaunchTour(canAutoStart:) does.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism verified end to end, and I would raise the 0.5 confidence. HouseFirstRoot.swift:60-62 is .onChange(of: tabs.selected, initial: true) { mounted.insert(tab) } — insert-only, so Today is mounted at launch and never removed; tabContent keeps every mounted tab in the ZStack at .opacity(tab == selected ? 1 : 0) (:71-79).
