Note the app already has the right helper, Design/Accessibility/AccessibleHitTarget.swift, whose header says "call sites adopt it in later waves" — it has zero call sites.
confirmed.fix: Apply the existing 36-visual/44-thumb pattern from QRScannerView.swift:67-73 (or accessibleHitTarget) to each site, starting with BackChevronButton.
confirmed.codeNote: Canonical for the tap-target root; absorbs A-04, B-33, C-21, C2-19 and C3-22. Verified: PatinaTransitions.swift:34-41 BackChevronButton is 36×36 and is the back affordance on all 26 title-less `.patinaScreen` destinations; RecommendationsView.swift:510/528 are 30×30 and 6pt apart on every browse card; DailyGreetingHeader.swift:98/119 are 36×36 in an `HStack(spacing: 4)`; RoomProjectView.swift:371-376 is 36×36. The key structural observation is correct and independently verified: `Design/Accessibility/AccessibleHitTarget.swift` defines exactly the right 44pt modifier and has ZERO production call sites — its only two uses are inside its own `#Preview`. Highest-priority instances: the back chevron (every pushed screen) and A-04's 14.7pt legal links on the first screen.
confirmed.judgeNote: Canonical for tap targets; absorbs A-04, B-33, C-21, C3-22, C2-19. BackChevronButton at 36x36 across 28 pushed screens is the highest-traffic instance and the one to lead with. Design/Accessibility/AccessibleHitTarget.swift already exists with zero call sites — this is an adoption task, not an authoring one, which is why a 21-site sweep is still M and not L.

confirmed.title: Colour-only selection state — .isSelected is used at 6 sites and missing everywhere else
confirmed.where: Missing at Features/Collections/Views/CollectionsView.swift:89-107 (Saved/Boards tabs), Rooms/Views/CrossRoomView.swift:94-107 (All Items / By Category / By Maker), Rooms/Components/RoomTypePillRow.swift:27-44, Home/Views/AddToRoomSheet.swift:61-93, RoomScan/Views/HeroPickerSheet.swift:33-57, Rooms/Views/MoveOrCopyItemSheet.swift:103
confirmed.evidence: .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected) appears at only 6 sites app-wide (PatinaTabBar:110, StyleSwatchCell:52, StylePillButton:44, VisualResonanceView:93, PriorityView:79, ScanPickerView:238). On the tab strips above, selection is conveyed by colour plus a clay underline that is itself only 2.18:1 (C6-13), so VoiceOver announces selected and unselected identically.
confirmed.fix: Add .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? [.isSelected] : []) at each site.
confirmed.codeNote: Canonical for colour-only selection; absorbs B-37 (StyleQuizView) and C-52 (FilterChip), both of which should be added to the site list. Verified: `.accessibilityAddTraits(… .isSelected …)` appears at exactly the 6 named sites (PatinaTabBar:110, StyleSwatchCell:52, StylePillButton:44, VisualResonanceView:93, PriorityView:79, ScanPickerView:238) and nowhere else. The compounding link to C6-13 is real. The AX half is VoiceOver-only — correct testerVisible to false; the colour-only-cue half is C6-13's.
confirmed.judgeNote: Split the finding. The sighted half — selection conveyed only by a 2.18:1 clay underline on Collections Saved/Boards, CrossRoom's three segments and the room-type pills — is T1 and is the same edit as C6-13. The .isSelected trait sweep across the six sites is T2 and becomes a one-liner on lines you are already touching.

confirmed.title: Settings rows announce their decorative icon and their chevron
confirmed.evidence: Every row draws Image(systemName: icon) at :363 and Image(systemName: "chevron.right") at :374 with no .accessibilityHidden(true) and no .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) on the row, so each row reads as three elements ending in "right chevron".
confirmed.fix: Hide both images and combine the row into one element.
confirmed.codeNote: The code fact is right, the consequence is not. CONFIRMED: settingsRow draws Image(systemName: icon) at :363 and Image(systemName: "chevron.right") at :374 with no .accessibilityHidden(true), and no row carries .accessibilityElement(children: .combine). REFUTED: 'Each Settings row reads as three elements ending in right chevron.' Every chevron row is the label of a Button or NavigationLink (settingsButtonRow :331-336, the Account link :62-70), and SwiftUI combines a Button's children into ONE accessibility element — so these read as a single button whose derived label picks up the symbol descriptions, not as three elements. The three-elements claim only holds for the rows that are NOT buttons: appearanceRow (:289-322) and contextMemoryToggle (:241-285), which are bare HStacks whose icon Image is its own element. Compare ProfileView.swift:293-295, which does hide its chevron. Restate accordingly; minor is right. Not sim-verified — I did not run describe_screen (no clone assigned to this lane), so the exact spoken string is unconfirmed either way.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed against the helpers: settingsRow draws Image(systemName: icon) and chevron.right with no .accessibilityHidden(true) and no children:.combine on the row, so every row reads as three elements ending in 'right chevron'. Real, and the fix is trivial — but no first-round tester is a VoiceOver user unless Kody invites one, and the rows are still navigable and announce their label. T2: batch it with C6-30 into one accessibility pass on these two files once the visual work has settled, so the combining doesn't have to be redone.

confirmed.title: ProductCard's tile variant announces only a price
confirmed.evidence: tileLayout is a PatinaAsyncImage (which correctly sets .accessibilityHidden(true) on success — PatinaAsyncImage.swift:71) plus a price overlay and nothing else, so in board previews VoiceOver says "$4,850, button" with no product name. The list variant has no .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) and a trailing unhidden chevron.right at :139.
confirmed.fix: Give both variants an explicit combined label of maker + name + price.
confirmed.codeNote: Tile half CONFIRMED, list half REFUTED, and the whole thing is unreachable today. CONFIRMED: tileLayout (ProductCard.swift:148-166) is thumbnail + a price overlay and nothing else, inside `Button(action: onTap)` at :89-98, so VoiceOver announces the price and the button trait with no product name. REFUTED: the list-variant complaint — because the card IS a Button, SwiftUI already merges the label's contents into a single element, so the absent `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` is not a defect and the trailing chevron.right (:139) is inside that merged label, not a separate stop. Also the cite 'PatinaAsyncImage.swift:71 sets .accessibilityHidden(true) on success' is wrong — :71 is inside loadingPlaceholder; the success branch (:44-50) sets no accessibility modifier at all (the unlabelled Image is decorative by default, which happens to give the same outcome). REACHABILITY: `.tile` has exactly one call site — CollectionsView.swift:350, the board preview grid — and a board can never exist because BoardModel is not in the SwiftData schema (C7-02). Fix C7-02 first; this becomes tester-visible only after.
confirmed.judgeNote: Kept at major as an accessibility defect — a product tile announcing only '$4,850, button' is unusable, and correct VoiceOver is explicitly in the bar — but marked not tester-visible: a first round of homeowner testers invited by Kody will almost certainly contain no VoiceOver user, and nothing about it is perceptible to a sighted tester. Build 2, with the list variant's combine + unhidden chevron in the same edit.

confirmed.title: RoomGalleryCard — the Your Spaces card — has no accessibility treatment
confirmed.evidence: Zero accessibility modifiers in the file. The stats row emits up to six separate Text nodes ("4", "ITEMS", "$12K", "BUDGET", "87%", "MATCH") with no pairing and no children: .combine, so the card reads as eight disconnected fragments.
confirmed.fix: Combine the card into one element labelled "<room>, <n> items, budget <x>, match <y>%".
confirmed.codeNote: Verified exactly. `grep -n accessibility Features/Rooms/Components/RoomGalleryCard.swift` returns nothing across all 179 lines. The stats row (:90-101 with statCells at :113-123) emits up to three Stat cells, each drawn by `stat(value:label:)` as two separate Text nodes, on top of the hero's room-name and galleryMetaLine Texts — so a fully-populated card is eight unpaired fragments inside one Button with no .accessibilityElement(children: .combine). Fix sketch is right.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified — RoomGalleryCard.swift has zero accessibility modifiers, and the stats row emits up to six unpaired Text nodes with no children: .combine, so the Your Spaces card reads as eight disconnected fragments ('4', 'ITEMS', '$12K', 'BUDGET', '87%', 'MATCH'). The brief's bar names correct VoiceOver outright, and this is the gallery's primary card. S effort, high leverage. T1: a VoiceOver user is possible but not certain in a hand-picked round-1 cohort, so it sits behind the defects every tester sees — but it must not slip past build 2.

confirmed.title: AddToRoomSheet has no accessibility treatment at all
confirmed.evidence: The row Button at :63-92 ends in an unhidden Text("+") at :82; selection is Interactive.active fill vs Background.secondary at :89 with no .isSelected; the "Add to Room" heading at :25 has no .isHeader; a hand-drawn grab handle at :18-22 stands in for .presentationDragIndicator.
confirmed.fix: Label and combine each room row, add .isSelected, tag the heading, and use presentationDragIndicator.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed; line numbers off by one, nothing else. Zero accessibility modifiers in all 103 lines of AddToRoomSheet.swift. The row Button is :62-91 ending in an unhidden `Text("+")` at :81; selection is Interactive.active vs Background.secondary fill at :85-88 with no .isSelected; the 'Add to Room' heading at :25 has no .isHeader; the hand-drawn RoundedRectangle grabber is :17-22. One addition: the sheet does declare `.presentationDetents([.medium])` at :57 but no .presentationDragIndicator, so the hand-drawn handle is a straight substitution for the system one.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified — 103 lines, 0 accessibility modifiers: unhidden Text("+") at :82, selection carried by fill colour alone at :89 with no .isSelected, an unmarked heading at :25, and a hand-drawn grab handle at :18-22 instead of .presentationDragIndicator. Same class as C6-28 and same S effort; the hand-rolled grabber is also a visual-system miss independent of VoiceOver, since it will not match any other sheet in the app. Fix in the same pass as C6-28.

confirmed.title: AccountView — label/value rows unpaired, headings untagged, zero labels
confirmed.evidence: sectionHeader is Text.muted with no .isHeader; infoRow is Text(label) + Spacer() + Text(value) with no children: .combine and no accessibilityLabeledPair (which appears 0 times app-wide), so "Email" and the address read as two unrelated strings on opposite sides of the row; the QR row is icon + text + chevron with no label.
confirmed.fix: Combine each infoRow, tag section headers .isHeader, label the QR row.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed, with one wording caveat. AccountView.swift:221-227 sectionHeader is a plain uppercased Text with no .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) — confirmed. :229-240 infoRow is HStack { Text(label); Spacer(); Text(value) } with no combine — confirmed, and because it is NOT inside a Button this genuinely does expose two separate elements, so the 'Email' / address split the lane describes is real (unlike C6-26's button rows). I re-ran the grep: `accessibilityLabeledPair` appears 0 times across apps/mobile/Patina — confirmed. Caveat on the QR row (:161-180): 'no label' is accurate about the source (no .accessibilityLabel modifier) but it is a Button, so it does get a derived label from its Text('Sign in on the web') — the defect there is the unhidden chevron and icon riding along, not silence.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed — AccountView's infoRow is Text(label) + Spacer() + Text(value) with no pairing, so 'Email' and the address read as two unrelated strings, and sectionHeader carries no .isHeader. The accessibilityLabeledPair-count-zero observation is a good catch and applies app-wide, not just here. Same T2 accessibility pass as C6-26; note that if C1-14 rewrites the guest Account state, these rows change shape anyway — so sequence this AFTER C1-14 rather than before.

confirmed.title: Onboarding hides real copy along with the illustration
confirmed.evidence: pageIllustration(...).accessibilityHidden(true) at :136 hides a subtree that contains meaningful text: "Five quick questions" at :285 and "Saved on this iPhone first" at :313 — the latter is the app's privacy reassurance for the camera page, so a VoiceOver tester never hears it.
confirmed.fix: Move the two captions out of the hidden illustration, or expose them via the page's accessibility label.
confirmed.codeNote: Mechanism confirmed, impact overstated. OnboardingFlowView.swift:136 does apply .accessibilityHidden(true) to the whole pageIllustration subtree, which contains 'Five quick questions' (:285) and 'Saved on this iPhone first' (:313). But on the shipped quiz-first path the hidden caption is 'Five quick questions', which is repeated verbatim as the first words of the page body at :57 — a VoiceOver tester loses nothing (see P-12, which files that duplication as a copy defect). 'Saved on this iPhone first' lives in cameraIllustration, which renders only on the walk-first variant behind the onboarding_walk_first PostHog flag — OFF for a first-launch TestFlight build — so no first-round tester reaches it in either modality. Real, but it does not bite the audited path.
confirmed.judgeNote: Minor overall, but sharper than it reads: the copy hidden inside the accessibilityHidden illustration includes 'Saved on this iPhone first', which is the app's only privacy reassurance at the camera-permission moment. A VoiceOver tester is asked for camera access having never heard the sentence that justifies it. S fix.

confirmed.title: PatinaButton loses its title while loading
confirmed.evidence: In the isLoading branch the label is only ProgressView(); there is no .accessibilityLabel(title) and no value. The button is .disabled(!isInteractive) at :82, so VoiceOver announces "dimmed button" with no name — on every submit button in the app, exactly while the tester is waiting on it.
confirmed.fix: Keep .accessibilityLabel(title) on the Button and add .accessibilityValue("Loading") while isLoading.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed and stronger than stated: PatinaButton.swift contains NO accessibility modifiers at all (grep for 'accessibility' in the file returns nothing). In the isLoading branch (:57-61) the label is only ProgressView(), and :82 applies .disabled(!isInteractive), so VoiceOver announces a dimmed, nameless button on every submit in the app at exactly the moment the user is waiting. 41 call sites. Clean S fix.
confirmed.judgeNote: For a VoiceOver tester this is not minor — it is a nameless dimmed button on every submit in the app, occurring precisely during the wait when they most need to know what is happening. Two lines (.accessibilityLabel(title) plus .accessibilityValue). The bar names VoiceOver explicitly; this and C6-34 are the cheapest accessibility wins in the audit.

confirmed.title: Canonical loading and error states are unlabelled and unannounced
confirmed.evidence: PatinaErrorState's Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle") at :21 is not hidden, there is no children: .combine, and no announcement fires when the state appears; PatinaLoadingState has the same gaps plus no .updatesFrequently. Both are the app's shared states, so the defect reproduces on every screen that uses them.
confirmed.fix: Hide the icon, combine the block, and announce the message on appear.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed in full: PatinaErrorState.swift:21 renders Image(systemName:"exclamationmark.triangle") with no .accessibilityHidden, the VStack has no children:.combine and nothing announces on appear; PatinaLoadingState.swift:14-24 has the same gaps plus no .updatesFrequently on the ProgressView. Both are the app's shared states — PatinaErrorState is even the component R-20 wants Today's error row routed through — so the defect reproduces everywhere at once. S fix, good value.
confirmed.judgeNote: Same family as C6-33 and equally cheap: hide the decorative icon, combine the children, announce on appear, add .updatesFrequently. Because these are the app's shared loading and error states, the fix reproduces on every screen that uses them — very high leverage for S effort.

confirmed.title: Companion action rows read a stray chevron and are not combined
confirmed.evidence: The row Button carries only .accessibilityIdentifier("companion.action.\(icon)") at :832 — no accessibilityLabel and no children: .combine. Its label contains an unhidden Image(systemName: icon) at :804, the uppercase hint at :814-818, and Text("\u{203A}") at :823. Everything else in the Companion meets the OPTION_B_ACCEPTANCE clause ("Every state has a VoiceOver label, value, hint, logical reading order, and a minimum 44×44 point interactive target") — CompanionPresentation.swift:139-158 supplies label/value per state and CompanionHearthView.swift:146-150/223-226/448-450 wires them; the action rows are the one gap.
confirmed.fix: Combine the row and label it "<label>. <hint>"; hide the icon and the chevron.
confirmed.codeNote: Line citations are exact (CompanionOverlay.swift:796, 804, 818, 823, 832 all verified) but TWO OF THE THREE CLAIMS ARE WRONG, and the lane's own AX dump refutes them. research/C.md ('Companion — AX tree') records the measured label as `"Message your designer, Chat with your designer, ›"`. That single concatenated string proves (a) the rows ARE combined — SwiftUI implicitly merges a Button's label into one element, so the absence of `children: .combine` is not a defect and 'not combined' is a mis-read; and (b) the SF Symbol does NOT leak — no symbol description appears in the measured label, so 'hide the icon' is unnecessary work. What survives is exactly one thing: the decorative `Text("\u{203A}")` at :823 is spoken on all six rows. Fix collapses to `.accessibilityHidden(true)` on that Text. Two further notes: the finding's supporting claim that 'everything else in the Companion meets the OPTION_B_ACCEPTANCE clause' is contradicted by its own lane — the same AX dump reports `companion.bubble` as `role = AXGenericElement` with no button trait, and C6-36 is a second gap. Separately the AX dump shows the row identifiers are raw SF Symbol names (`companion.action.bubble.left.and.bubble.right`), which is a real smell the finding only glances at via :832.
confirmed.judgeNote: Severity minor→major, conditional on the tester. Verified at CompanionOverlay.swift:796-834: the row Button carries only .accessibilityIdentifier — no label, no children: .combine — so the unhidden SF Symbol, the uppercased mono hint and Text("\u{203A}") each surface as separate elements. These rows are the Companion's ONLY controls, so a VoiceOver tester does not meet a rough menu, they meet an unusable one; a sighted tester sees nothing at all. Everything else in the Companion already meets the acceptance clause, so this is a single missed spot, S to close. T1 — build 2, unless Kody has a VoiceOver user in round 1, in which case promote.

confirmed.title: The Companion first-launch coach mark buries its "Got it"
confirmed.evidence: .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) at :731 plus an .accessibilityLabel of the body copy at :732, applied over a VStack whose second child is the "Got it" Button at :712-723 — the same demotion-to-custom-action mechanism as C6-08. The comment at :700-704 shows the team already fixed the harder version of this (they removed .isModal because it hid companion.close), so the pattern is understood; this instance was missed.
confirmed.fix: Drop children: .combine so "Got it" stays focusable.
confirmed.codeNote: Code-confirmed verbatim. CompanionOverlay.swift:706-733: a VStack whose second child is the 'Got it' Button (:712-723) carries `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` at :731 plus `.accessibilityLabel(<body copy>)` at :732. `.combine` merges descendants and demotes contained controls to custom actions on the merged element, so 'Got it' stops being focusable by swipe. The finding's read of the :700-704 comment is fair — the team removed `.isModal` for a related reason and left this one. Real exposure: same first-open gate as A-50 (CompanionOverlay.swift:887 + CompanionCoachingModel.swift:436-438), so a VoiceOver tester meets it on their first Companion open. Related to A-50 but NOT a duplicate — that is a layout occlusion, this is an accessibility-tree demotion, and each fix leaves the other standing.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified at CompanionOverlay.swift:731-732: children: .combine plus a body-copy accessibilityLabel over a VStack whose second child is the 'Got it' button — demoting the only dismissal on a first-run card to a rotor custom action. Same coach mark as A-50, so fix both in one pass; the comment at :700-704 shows the team already understands this exact failure mode from the .isModal fix, this instance was just missed. S. T1.

confirmed.title: Reduce Transparency is not handled anywhere, and one site actively defeats it
confirmed.where: accessibilityReduceTransparency: 0 occurrences app-wide. 11 files use glassEffect/.ultraThinMaterial; the concrete offenders are Features/Companion/Views/CompanionOverlay.swift:450 and Features/Recommendations/Views/RecommendationsView.swift:507 and :527
confirmed.evidence: CompanionOverlay:450 writes Color.black.opacity(0.3).background(.ultraThinMaterial.opacity(0.5)) — the explicit .opacity(0.5) on a material overrides the system's Reduce-Transparency opacity increase. RecommendationsView puts Circle().fill(.ultraThinMaterial) behind 14pt symbols over live photography. Most other Material/glassEffect sites self-adapt, which is why this is the lowest-confidence finding in the lane.
confirmed.fix: Drop the .opacity(0.5) on the material and, on the two browse-card buttons, branch to an opaque fill when accessibilityReduceTransparency is on. Confirm on the simulator before changing the rest.
confirmed.codeNote: Both halves confirmed. `accessibilityReduceTransparency` returns zero occurrences app-wide, and CompanionOverlay.swift:449-450 is verbatim `Color.black.opacity(0.3).background(.ultraThinMaterial.opacity(0.5))` — the explicit `.opacity(0.5)` does override the system's Reduce-Transparency handling. RecommendationsView.swift:507 and :527 are `Circle().fill(.ultraThinMaterial)` behind 14pt symbols. The finding's own 0.65 confidence is well calibrated: the code is certain, the perceived visual impact still wants a simulator pass with the toggle on, which this audit did not do.
confirmed.judgeNote: Down from minor, consistent with the lane's own 0.65 confidence. Only CompanionOverlay.swift:450 (.opacity(0.5) applied to a material, which defeats the system's own reduce-transparency handling) is a concrete bug; the rest self-adapts. Fix that one line, leave the survey.

confirmed.title: accessibilityIdentifier coverage is thin and inconsistently named
confirmed.where: 182 unique identifiers against 525 control occurrences. Zero in RoomScan (5,675 LOC / 41 controls), Messaging, Shared, ARPlacement, StyleConversation, Conversation, Walk, Splash and Documents; thin in Rooms (9/50), Collections (2/12), Settings (6/24), Account (2/8)
confirmed.evidence: Two competing conventions: lowerCamel screen keys (auth.* ×23, companion.* ×15, invoiceDetail.* ×11) and PascalCase view names (DailyRoomView.* ×19, SettingsView.* ×6, ProductDetailView.* ×5). PatinaUITests references only 14 distinct strings, so UI tests can reach a fraction of the app and a new test author cannot guess the convention.
confirmed.fix: Pick one convention, write it down, and add identifiers to the zero-coverage features that a walk must drive (RoomScan first).
confirmed.codeNote: Reproduced against main. 182 unique accessibilityIdentifier strings across 191 occurrences in apps/mobile/Patina/Patina — 182 matches exactly. Prefix histogram matches to the unit: auth 23, DailyRoomView 19, companion 15, invoiceDetail 11, SettingsView 6, ProductDetailView 5 — so both naming conventions and their volumes are real. Zero-coverage features verified by directory: RoomScan 0 ids / 5,675 LOC (LOC matches exactly), Messaging 0, Shared 0, ARPlacement 0, StyleConversation 0, Conversation 0, Walk 0, Splash 0, Documents 0. Thin ones verified exactly: Rooms 9, Collections 2, Settings 6, Account 2. PatinaUITests references 13 identifier-shaped strings out of 18 bracketed literals (the rest are copy assertions), consistent with the stated 14. One number I could not reproduce and would treat as approximate: the '525 control occurrences' denominator (a plain Button/NavigationLink/TextField/Toggle/Picker/Menu grep over Features/ gives ~180); the per-feature id counts, which carry the finding, are all exact.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed: 182 identifiers against 525 control occurrences, two competing conventions (lowerCamel screen keys vs PascalCase view names), zero coverage in RoomScan / Messaging / ARPlacement / StyleConversation / Conversation / Walk / Splash / Documents, PatinaUITests reaching only 14 distinct strings. No tester path whatsoever, so T2 — this audit's own walks drove the app fine on scan_ui frames without identifiers, which is the practical proof that it is not blocking. It becomes worth doing when someone commits to automated walks (RoomScan first, at 5,675 LOC and 41 controls it is both the hardest surface to drive by coordinates and the one where a regression is most expensive). Pair it with G-03's rewrite half if that path is taken — one convention written down, then identifiers added to whatever the rewritten suite must drive. Absorbs B-55.

confirmed.title: The hand-rolled tab bar gives no positional context and no per-item identifiers
confirmed.evidence: The bar is otherwise well built — .accessibilityAddTraits(.isTabBar) at :73, .isSelected per item at :110, canonical VoiceOver names via tab.canonicalName at :109, and a deliberate .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility2) cap on the drawn word only at :100. What TabView would still have given is an .accessibilityValue/position announcement ("Tab 1 of 4") and per-item accessibilityIdentifiers, of which there are none on the bar.
confirmed.fix: Add .accessibilityValue("Tab \(index + 1) of \(PatinaTab.allCases.count)") and an identifier per item.
confirmed.codeNote: Code-true: `grep -n 'accessibilityIdentifier|accessibilityValue' Features/Navigation/PatinaTabBar.swift` returns nothing at all, and the praise is accurate too (.isTabBar at :72-73, .isSelected at :110, tab.canonicalName at :108, the deliberate AX2 cap on the drawn word only at :100). But PatinaTabBar draws only under HouseFirstRoot (ContentView.swift:149-153), which is flag-gated OFF on a first-launch Release build — a round-one tester never sees this bar. testerVisible should be false.
confirmed.judgeNote: Correctly self-limited — the finding grants the bar is well built and names only what TabView would have added. Flipping testerVisible to false for this round: PatinaTabBar is instantiated only from HouseFirstRoot.swift:124, and house-first is off on a first TestFlight launch, so no round-one tester sees this bar at all. Worth doing before house-first ships (the per-item identifiers also pay for themselves in PatinaUITests), not before build 1. T2.

confirmed.title: The accessible-gesture work from PT-2-4 guards dead code
confirmed.evidence: grep for all five modifiers across Features returns zero call sites. The VoiceOver alternatives inside them (VoiceOverTapModifier, accessibilityAction(named:)) are real and correct — they simply protect nothing, which makes it easy to read this directory and conclude custom gestures are handled.
confirmed.fix: Delete or explicitly park the unused gesture modifiers so the directory stops implying coverage.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed exactly: all five modifiers — `holdable`, `lingerable`, `companionSwipeDownGesture`, `companionTapGesture`, `companionLongPressGesture` — return zero call sites anywhere outside `Design/Gestures/` itself. The framing is the valuable part: reading that directory would leave a builder believing custom gestures have VoiceOver alternatives when nothing ships them.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not a tester-facing defect at all, and valuable precisely for that reason: five unused gesture modifiers make the Design/Gestures directory read as covered when nothing calls it. Delete or park with an explicit comment so the next audit is not misled.

confirmed.title: HomeStoryRetryRow puts the 44pt minimum on the row, not the button
confirmed.evidence: .frame(minHeight: 44) at :38 is applied to the enclosing HStack; the Button's own contentShape(Rectangle()) at :34 wraps only the roughly 18pt text, so the retry affordance on the Today home is well under the minimum.
confirmed.fix: Move the minHeight inside the Button label, before contentShape.
confirmed.codeNote: Line-exact. HomeStoryRetryRow.swift: `.frame(minHeight: 44)` is at :38 on the enclosing HStack; the Button's `.contentShape(Rectangle())` at :34 is applied to the Text inside the label, so with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` the hit region is the ~20 pt text bounds vertically centred in the 44 pt row. And unlike C6-44 this one is live on the round-one path: shots R/18-cold-today-bottom.png and R/19b show 'Today's story couldn't load' / 'Let's try that again' actually drawn on Today whenever the story fetch fails.
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from polish. This is not an accessibility nicety — a retry control with roughly 18pt of hittable height affects every tester with ordinary thumbs, and R-02 proves the story-failure state it lives in is reachable in normal use. The failure mode is nasty in combination: the story fails to load, the tester taps Retry, nothing happens because they missed it, and with no pull-to-refresh (R-03) they conclude the app is dead. Moving the minHeight inside the Button label is S. T1, or free-ride it onto the R-03 fix.

confirmed.title: MoveOrCopyItemSheet and ManualRoomEntryView speak arrows and multiplication signs
confirmed.evidence: The destination-room Button has no accessibilityLabel and ends in Text("→") at :141; the current room is .disabled(isCurrent) at :154 but otherwise signalled by .opacity(0.5) alone. ManualRoomEntryView places Text("×") at :42 between the Length and Width fields, which VoiceOver reads as "multiplication sign".
confirmed.fix: Hide both glyphs and label the destination rows "Move to <room>".
confirmed.codeNote: Two of the three claims are exact, one is wrong. Confirmed: MoveOrCopyItemSheet.swift:141 is a bare `Text("→")` with no accessibilityLabel on the destination Button (:123-153), and ManualRoomEntryView.swift:42 is `Text("×")` between the Length and Width fields, which VoiceOver speaks as 'multiplication sign'. Refuted: 'the current room is .disabled(isCurrent) but otherwise signalled by .opacity(0.5) alone' — MoveOrCopyItemSheet.swift:134-140 substitutes a visible `Text("Current")` mono label for the arrow on that row, so the disabled state is explicitly labelled in both the visual and the AX tree. Keep the two glyph fixes, drop the opacity claim.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified as described. 'Move to Guest Bedroom, right arrow' and a Length field followed by 'multiplication sign' are exactly the details that separate good from world-class, and both are one .accessibilityHidden(true) plus a label. But MoveOrCopyItemSheet is deep in the item-management flow that a first-round homeowner with two rooms and zero saved pieces will not reach, and ManualRoomEntryView's × is a single stray token. Correct call at polish; T2. The isCurrent row signalled by .opacity(0.5) alone is the more substantive half — a disabled control with no non-visual cue.

confirmed.title: HelpTooltip triggers are tap gestures wearing a button trait
confirmed.where: Features/Help/Views/HelpTooltip.swift:108-111, with the trait supplied by the caller at Features/Help/Views/HelpInfoIcon.swift:100
confirmed.evidence: The trigger uses .onTapGesture rather than a Button, with .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton) added by hand. VoiceOver activation does forward a tap so it works in practice, but there is no accessibilityAction and no pressed state. The good part: HelpInfoIcon.swift:96 does apply .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).
confirmed.fix: Wrap the trigger in a real Button, keeping the existing label, hint and 44pt frame.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED, line-exact. HelpTooltip.swift:108 is `.onTapGesture { handleTriggerTap() }` on the caller-supplied trigger; HelpInfoIcon.swift:100 supplies `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` by hand; the 44pt frame is at HelpInfoIcon.swift:96 as stated. No accessibilityAction and no pressed state, confirmed by reading the whole trigger chain. Confidence 0.6 is honest — VoiceOver double-tap does forward a synthetic tap, so this is a craft/consistency defect rather than a functional one. Worth one extra note for the fix: HelpTooltip.handleTriggerTap (:150-158) returns silently when there is no content, so wrapping it in a real Button must preserve that silent-absence path or the app will start presenting empty popovers.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed exactly as written and correctly rated polish. Verified HelpTooltip.swift's trigger really is `trigger().onTapGesture { handleTriggerTap() }` with the .isButton trait hand-applied by the caller at HelpInfoIcon.swift:100, and the good part the finder credits is real too — HelpInfoIcon:96 does apply .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44) with .contentShape(Rectangle()), so the tap target meets HIG. With no observed user-facing failure (VoiceOver activation forwards the tap; the trait is present) this is idiom debt: no pressed state, no accessibilityAction. T2. One scheduling note: B-07's T0 fix reworks this exact view's presentation, so if the implementer is comfortable, wrapping the trigger in a real Button while they are already in HelpTooltip.swift is nearly free — but it should not be allowed to expand the T0 change.

confirmed.title: ModelContainer failure is fatalError — no fallback, no MigrationPlan; a build-2 schema change crash-loops every installed app
confirmed.evidence: `do { container = try ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: [configuration]) } catch { fatalError("Failed to create ModelContainer: \(error)") }`. The container is built from a bare `Schema([...])` — no VersionedSchema, no SchemaMigrationPlan anywhere in the app (grep-verified). It is constructed synchronously from PatinaApp.swift:88, before the first frame.
confirmed.fix: Add a SchemaMigrationPlan; on catch, move the old store aside and open a fresh one (or in-memory) behind a designed 'we had to start your data over' screen. Never fatalError in a shipping build.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED verbatim. PersistenceController.swift:41-45 is exactly `do { container = try ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: [configuration]) } catch { fatalError("Failed to create ModelContainer: \(error)") }`, built from a bare `Schema([...])` of 8 models (:26-35). `grep -rn 'SchemaMigrationPlan|VersionedSchema'` across the app returns ZERO hits. Constructed synchronously from PatinaApp.swift:88 before the first frame. Timing nuance worth stating in the plan: this cannot bite build 1 on a fresh install — it is a build-2-onward crash loop, which is exactly the shape of a multi-build TestFlight round, so T0 stands.
confirmed.judgeNote: Dormant on a fresh install, which argues for T1 — I am overriding that. The consequence of getting build 2's schema change wrong is every installed tester bricked in a launch crash loop with no recovery path and no way to tell you why, and doing the work in build 1 costs the same M. Stamp the V1 VersionedSchema before any tester data exists in an unversioned store, and never fatalError in a shipping build: move the old store aside behind a designed 'we had to start your data over' screen.

confirmed.title: BoardModel is fetched and inserted against a container whose Schema does not contain it (Saved / Collections)
confirmed.evidence: Schema is exactly TableItemModel, RoomModel, SavedItem, StylePreferenceModel, SyncQueueItem, RoomScanPackage, DesignRequestDraft, SubmittedDesignRequest. BoardModel is a @Model, is not in that list, and is not reachable by relationship from anything in it. CollectionsViewModel does `FetchDescriptor<BoardModel>` on appear and `context.insert(BoardModel(...))` from the New Board alert. LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData() (:27-34) omits it too. CollectionsView is live on both roots (ContentView.swift:273,310; HouseFirstRoot.swift:214,240).
confirmed.fix: Add BoardModel.self to the schema (and to LocalStoreReset), or remove the boards feature from CollectionsView before shipping.
confirmed.codeNote: Every code claim CONFIRMED verbatim: PersistenceController.swift:26-35 Schema is exactly the eight models listed; BoardModel (Core/Models/BoardModel.swift:12-13) is a @Model, absent from it, and unreachable by relationship; CollectionsViewModel fetches FetchDescriptor<BoardModel> at :49 and :202 and does `context.insert(BoardModel(...))` at :146-148; LocalStoreReset.wipeUserScopedData (:26-35) omits it; CollectionsView is live on both roots. ONE correction that changes where the risk sits: the fetch-on-appear half is PROVEN NON-FATAL — shots/B/79-saved.png shows Saved rendering with the Boards / All items tabs and the '+' control, so `try? context.fetch(...)` swallows the error and Boards is permanently, silently empty rather than crashing. The blocker claim therefore rests entirely on the untested `context.insert(BoardModel(...))` reached from '+' → the New Board alert (CollectionsView.swift:135-141): worst case a SwiftData fatalError ('failed to find a currently active container'), best case a board that vanishes on the next load. Either way the '+' is a visible dead control on a screen every tester can open. Confidence 0.7 is honest — a single sim tap on '+' settles blocker vs major and is worth doing before the fix program scopes it.
confirmed.judgeNote: Schema verified at PersistenceController.swift:26-35 — eight models, no BoardModel. Tier holds on either reading: if the out-of-schema fetch/insert raises (SwiftData's insert of an unknown @Model is the harder path; `try? context.fetch` at CollectionsViewModel.swift:49-51 swallows only a thrown error, not an entity-description exception) it is a crash on the Saved screen; if it degrades quietly, build 1 ships a Boards tab whose Create button does nothing. Cheapest T0 is to hide the Boards tab for build 1 rather than widen the schema under time pressure. Second-order: LocalStoreReset omitting BoardModel means any board that did persist survives sign-out — a cross-account leak on a shared device.

confirmed.title: ARSession didUpdate retains the ARFrame in an escaping Task and runs the whole capture pipeline on the main actor at 60 Hz
confirmed.evidence: `nonisolated public func session(_:didUpdate frame: ARFrame) { Task { @MainActor in ... await self.frameCaptureService.captureFrame(from: frame); self.posedPhotoService?.consume(frame: frame); recorder.consume(frame: frame, ...); self.frameSinks.broadcast { $0.capture(frame: frame, ...) } } }`. The frame escapes the delegate (ARKit documents that retaining ARFrames exhausts the camera buffer pool and stalls the session) and one Task per frame puts hero-frame capture, posed photos, depth recording and every instrument sink on the main thread.
confirmed.fix: Extract pose/timestamp synchronously inside the delegate, hand Sendable values to a dedicated actor, never let the ARFrame escape.
confirmed.codeNote: Read the delegate in full at RoomCaptureService.swift:868-901 and it is exactly as quoted: `nonisolated public func session(_:didUpdate frame:)` opens `Task { @MainActor in ... }` on every AR frame, letting the ARFrame escape the delegate, and inside that Task runs `await frameCaptureService.captureFrame(from: frame)`, `posedPhotoService?.consume(frame:)`, `depthRecorder.consume(frame:...)` (plus a posed-photo timestamp correlation) and `frameSinks.broadcast { $0.capture(frame:timestampSeconds:) }`. The code's own comment at :896-898 concedes the sinks 'run inside the AR frame pump'. Tier T2 rather than T1 only because it is L-effort, LiDAR-only, and this audit produced no measurement of an actual session stall — the ARKit buffer-pool hazard is a documented risk, not an observed one.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified at RoomCaptureService.swift:867-901 and worse than written: the `guard self.isScanning` sits INSIDE the Task, so a Task is spawned per ARFrame (~60/s) whenever the delegate is attached, scanning or not — and each closure captures the ARFrame, which ARKit documents as exhausting the camera buffer pool. Hero capture, posed photos, depth recording and every instrument sink all run on the main actor inside that pump. If this bites, the headline feature stutters or the session stalls on the target tester's own iPhone 17 Pro, which is a build-1 blocker. But it is L effort, code-read only, and NOTHING in this audit is device-verified. So: T1 for the refactor, and the real T0 item this finding implies is a program action — a device scan pass on a physical LiDAR iPhone before build 1 ships. If that pass shows dropped frames or a stalled session, promote this to T0/blocker immediately. Take C7-05 and C7-35 first; they cut the same main-thread load for S/M.

confirmed.title: A fresh CIContext() is constructed per captured hero frame, on the main actor, mid-scan
confirmed.evidence: `let context = CIContext()` sits inside the per-frame compression path (captureInterval 2.0 s, :41) and is then used to render + HEIC/JPEG-encode the frame. CIContext construction compiles kernels and allocates GPU state. PosedPhotoService does this correctly — one shared context built at init (PosedPhotoService.swift:72-73).
confirmed.fix: Hoist to one lazily-created CIContext and move the encode off the main actor.
confirmed.codeNote: Code facts all confirmed: FrameCaptureService is @MainActor (:17), `let context = CIContext()` sits at :247 inside the per-captured-frame compress path, and PosedPhotoService.swift:73 builds one shared context at init (KeyframeBundleWriter.swift:110 does the same), so the correct pattern is already established in the same folder. Severity adjusted major -> minor because the finding's own evidence bounds the cost: captureInterval is 2.0s (:41), so this is one context construction every two seconds during a scan, not per frame — a main-thread hitch, not a sustained stall. S-effort and unambiguous, so still worth doing; T1.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: FrameCaptureService.swift is @MainActor (:17) and `let context = CIContext()` sits at :247 inside the per-capture compression path (captureInterval 2.0s, :41), then renders and HEIC-encodes. Kernel compilation and GPU state allocation on the main actor, every two seconds, while the tester is walking their living room holding a live AR session. PosedPhotoService already does it right (one shared context at init, :72-73), so this is an oversight with a known-good pattern sitting next to it. S effort, same hot path as C7-04 — take it in build 1 even if the bigger refactor waits.

confirmed.title: Launch housekeeping does recursive disk enumeration and multi-hundred-MB directory deletes on the main actor
confirmed.evidence: `.task(priority: .utility)` sets the task priority, but ScanHoldMigrator, ScanDiskBudget and ScanRecoveryService are all `@MainActor`, so the work hops back to the main thread. evictIfNeeded fetches every RoomScanPackage, calls FileManager.removeItem on whole bundle directories (budget 3 GB / 20 bundles) and saves; scanForRecoverableSessions calls bundleByteCount(at:) which enumerates every file in every non-resting bundle reading .fileSizeKey per entry, plus contentsOfDirectory in countPhotos.
confirmed.fix: Make the file passes nonisolated/actor-isolated, return plain values, and touch the ModelContext on the main actor only for mutations.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. PatinaApp.swift:106 `.task(priority: .utility)` sets priority only; the closure is MainActor-isolated by SwiftUI and all three collaborators are `@MainActor` at their type declarations — ScanHoldMigrator.swift:36, ScanDiskBudget.swift:19, ScanRecoveryService.swift:41 — so every byte of this runs on the main thread. evictIfNeeded (ScanDiskBudget.swift:110-183) fetches all synced RoomScanPackages, FileManager.removeItem's whole bundle directories and saves the context; scanForRecoverableSessions (ScanRecoveryService.swift:119-161) fans out to bundleByteCount (:412-438), which walks a FileManager.enumerator reading .fileSizeKey per entry, plus contentsOfDirectory in countPhotos (:387-394). Only quibble on the description: the work never 'hops back' to main — it is main-isolated from the first line.
confirmed.judgeNote: Framing overstates round-1 exposure: on a fresh TestFlight install there are zero scan bundles, so the enumeration walks an empty set and costs nothing on the launch every tester makes first. It bites only once a tester has captured several rooms — plausible in week one for an engaged tester, at which point it is a main-thread hang at launch. Confirmed real (PatinaApp.swift:106-123 even comments 'Both run silently on the main actor's SwiftData context'), but T1 — and pair it with C7-07 as one work package.

confirmed.title: The scan-recovery disk pass runs twice on every cold launch (app root and Today), with no coalescing
confirmed.evidence: Both call `ScanRecoveryService.shared.scanForRecoverableSessions(in: context)`. There is no in-flight guard (contrast RecordForeground.coalesce, which exists for exactly this), so the full main-actor enumeration of C7-06 happens twice on a launch landing on Today, and both passes can context.delete / quarantine / save the same rows concurrently.
confirmed.fix: One owner (the root); publish the count on ScanEventChannel, which already carries pendingRecoveryCandidateCount, and let Today read it.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. Two unconditional callers of ScanRecoveryService.shared.scanForRecoverableSessions(in:): PatinaApp.swift:123 and DailyRoomView.swift:133-136 (cited 130-134). I read scanForRecoverableSessions end to end (ScanRecoveryService.swift:119-161) — it opens straight into the FetchDescriptor with no in-flight guard, no debounce and no memo, and both passes run apply()/commit() over the same rows, which can context.delete or quarantine concurrently. The contrast the finding draws is real: RecordForeground carries a coalesce for precisely this shape. On a launch landing on Today the C7-06 main-actor disk walk therefore happens twice.
confirmed.judgeNote: testerVisible corrected false→true: two uncoordinated passes that context.delete/quarantine the same rows can lose or hide a room scan the tester spent minutes capturing, and a vanished scan is the most visible failure this app has. Same fresh-install caveat as C7-06 (nothing to race over on day one), so T1 — but the in-flight guard is S and RecordForeground.coalesce is already the in-repo pattern, so it should ride with the C7-06 fix.

confirmed.title: Every PostgREST client silently downgrades to anon when the token is missing; RLS then returns [] and the screen says 'you have nothing'
confirmed.where: RoomsAPIClient.swift:211-220 and 204-209; NotificationsAPIClient.swift:43-54; DecisionsAPIClient.swift:235-246; ProductAPIClient.swift:26-34; same shape in Messaging/Projects/Fulfillment/Roster/EditorialStories/Invoices/Proposals/Documents clients
confirmed.evidence: `request.setValue(APIConfiguration.anonKey, forHTTPHeaderField: "apikey"); if let token = await authToken() { request.setValue("Bearer \(token)", ...) }` where authToken() is `try? await ...auth.session.accessToken`. A failed refresh, expired refresh token or keychain failure yields nil, the request goes out as anon, owner-scoped RLS matches nothing, and PostgREST answers HTTP 200 with []. Nothing downstream distinguishes that from a genuinely empty account.
confirmed.fix: Make the token non-optional for owner-scoped reads: throw .notAuthenticated when absent so the UI can say 'we couldn't reach your account' instead of rendering an empty state.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED — the pattern is identical across the clients I spot-checked. ProductAPIClient.swift:21-34: `authToken()` is `try? await …auth.session.accessToken` and applyHeaders sets `apikey` unconditionally, `Authorization` only `if let token`. RoomsAPIClient.swift:211-222 and NotificationsAPIClient.swift:42-56 are the same shape verbatim (both also carry the optional `prefer:` param). A nil token therefore sends an anon request, owner-scoped RLS matches nothing, and PostgREST answers 200 with [] — indistinguishable downstream from an empty account. Compounded by A2-25 (no Release SDK diagnostics) and A2-16 (no error reporting), so this failure is silent AND undiagnosable.
confirmed.judgeNote: This is the exact shape that turns an auth hiccup into 'you have nothing' — an HTTP 200 with an empty array that no layer distinguishes from a genuinely empty account. It is also indistinguishable from A3-01's real emptiness, which is why guesswork must not be the diagnosis path. T1 rather than T0 only because it needs a token failure to fire; land A2-25 alongside it so that when it does fire you can see it. The fix is the right one: throw .notAuthenticated for owner-scoped reads rather than degrading to anon.

confirmed.title: Non-LiDAR iPhone: 'Scan with camera' is offered unconditionally and silently becomes a typing form; the unsupported-device screen is dead code
confirmed.evidence: NewRoomSheet has no RoomCaptureService.isSupported check; its first tile reads 'Scan with camera — Walk your room with the camera — best picks, AR placement, and a floor plan.' On any non-Pro iPhone that tap routes to .scanFlow and bootstrap() quietly sets `step = .fallback` (ScanFallbackEntryView, a width/length/windows/doors form). RoomPlanUnsupportedView, which says the right thing, has no call site outside a #Preview (grep: only :101).
confirmed.fix: Gate the tile on RoomCaptureService.isSupported, or relabel it and explain the device limit when false.
confirmed.codeNote: All three claims verified. NewRoomSheet.swift:14-52 contains no RoomCaptureService.isSupported check and offers 'Scan with camera — Walk your room with the camera — best picks, AR placement, and a floor plan.' unconditionally, routing to .scanFlow(reason: .fresh). QuietConversationFlowHost.bootstrap (:149-159) then silently sets `step = .fallback` on non-LiDAR hardware, landing the tester in ScanFallbackEntryView's typed form with no explanation. And RoomPlanUnsupportedView is dead: it is declared at RoomCaptureViewRepresentable.swift:57 and referenced exactly once more, at :100 inside `#Preview("Unsupported Device")`. This is the tester-visible defect behind A1-15 and the scan half of C9-06.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: NewRoomSheet.swift:28-37 has no isSupported check and its tile promises 'Walk your room with the camera — best picks, AR placement, and a floor plan'; QuietConversationFlowHost.bootstrap() then quietly sets step = .fallback; and RoomPlanUnsupportedView, which says the honest thing, has exactly two references — its own declaration and a #Preview. A non-LiDAR tester taps the app's headline promise and lands in a typing form with no explanation. That is a bait-and-switch on first contact, and shots/B/77-scan-fallback.png shows the form it lands in is in a different design language entirely (emoji cards, italic serif, 'Continue to Style Discovery'). T1 rather than T0 only because the brief names iPhone 17 Pro as the round-1 device — which makes this a Kody decision as much as a code fix: either gate/relabel the tile (S) or tell round 1 to invite Pro owners. Primary of the device-capability cluster with C9-06 and A1-15.

confirmed.title: iPad ships as a device family with no iPad design and zero size-class handling in 435 files
confirmed.evidence: grep for horizontalSizeClass, UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom and `.pad` across the whole app returns nothing. TestFlight will install a portrait-only phone layout on iPad, where iPadOS 26's resizable windowing has no declared answer; UIRequiresFullScreen is not set either.
confirmed.fix: Set TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1 for round 1. iPad support is a design program, not a build setting.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed by grep and pbxproj: TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2" on all eight configurations (project.pbxproj:511,543,712,760,781,803,823,843); a repo-wide search for horizontalSizeClass, verticalSizeClass, userInterfaceIdiom and UIUserInterfaceIdiom returns ZERO matches; INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations = UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait at :692,740; and UIRequiresFullScreen is absent. T0 because the fix is one build setting and the failure mode — TestFlight installing a portrait phone layout as a native iPad app — is unrecoverable in review. iPad support itself is a later program.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified: TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2" at 8 sites. Some fraction of an invited homeowner cohort owns an iPad and will install there first — and a portrait-locked phone layout with zero size-class handling in 435 files is the worst possible first impression, delivered before they ever see the app on a phone. The fix is one build setting; iPad is a design program for later. Do not ship build 1 with family 2.

confirmed.title: Everything expensive at launch is synchronous inside PatinaApp.init(), before the first frame — 18 TTFs, PostHog setup, flags, ModelContainer open
confirmed.evidence: In order, all synchronous: PatinaFonts.registerAll() → CTFontManagerRegisterFontURLs over 18 TTFs totalling 2,967,384 bytes; PostHogService.initialize() → PostHogSDK.setup(config) (disk read of queue+flag payload, first network kick) on the calling thread; FeatureFlags.resolveAtLaunch() plus an App Group UserDefaults write; PersistenceController.shared.container.mainContext (opens/migrates the SQLite store, and can fatalError per C7-01); RoomScanSyncService.configure (starts NWPathMonitor). The splash then holds a further 1.5 s minimum plus a 0.5 s cross-fade.
confirmed.fix: Move font registration and PostHog off the launch path (background task with a main-actor handoff); build the container lazily so the splash can paint first.
confirmed.codeNote: Substance CONFIRMED, one sub-claim overstated. PatinaApp.init (:58-90) does, in order and before any frame: PatinaFonts.registerAll() (:64), PostHogService.shared.initialize() (:76), FeatureFlags.shared.resolveAtLaunch() (:83), `PersistenceController.shared.container.mainContext` (:88 — forces the ModelContainer open/migrate), RoomScanSyncService.configure (:89). The font figures are exact: 18 TTFs in PatinaDesignKit totalling 2,967,384 bytes. CORRECTION: 'all synchronous' does not hold for the font step — PatinaFonts.swift:24 calls CTFontManagerRegisterFontURLs with a NON-nil registrationHandler, which per the CoreText header (CTFontManager.h:296) 'may be called multiple times during the registration process' with a `done` flag, i.e. it reports progress asynchronously rather than blocking on 3 MB of TTF. PostHog setup and the ModelContainer open are the genuinely blocking items and are where the fix should aim; pulling font registration off the launch path risks a first-frame fallback-font flash for a cost that may not exist. Re-measure the init span with a signpost before moving the fonts.
confirmed.judgeNote: This is the real cost behind the blank first frame, and 2.97MB of font registration plus a synchronous PostHog setup before any frame is exactly the kind of launch cost Apple-grade apps do not pay. Held at T1 rather than T0 on risk grounds: reordering launch (PostHog init, ModelContainer availability, flag resolution) is where a build-1 regression would strand testers, and C-29 plus C1-18 already make the same interval feel branded rather than broken. Do the measurable version in build 2.

confirmed.title: Telemetry queue re-queues failed batches without bound and rewrites the whole file every 30 s
confirmed.evidence: `if !ok { pending.insert(contentsOf: batch, at: 0); await persistToDisk() }`. maxBatchSize (100) only triggers a flush, it never caps `pending`. The destination is client.patina.cloud/api/interactions/batch — a client-portal route whose deploy is still on the program's OWED list. If it 404s (or the tester is offline a while) pending grows forever and the 30 s timer JSON-encodes and atomically rewrites the entire array to Application Support/daily_room_queue.json every tick.
confirmed.fix: Cap pending (drop oldest), add backoff on repeated failure, stop persisting on every failed tick.
confirmed.codeNote: Code mechanism CONFIRMED: DailyRoomBatchQueue.swift:77 `pending.insert(contentsOf: batch, at: 0)` inside `if !ok`, with maxBatchSize (:20) gating only the flush trigger (:62) and never capping `pending`; the 30 s timer (:82-91) calls flush(), which re-encodes and atomically rewrites the whole array (:96-101) on every non-empty tick. Backoff and a cap are worth having. But the PREMISE that inflates it is refuted: the endpoint is not undeployed. `apps/client-portal/src/app/api/interactions/batch` exists in the repo and a GET to https://client.patina.cloud/api/interactions/batch returns 405 (Method Not Allowed), i.e. the route is live on production and answering. With no 404 path, unbounded growth needs a genuinely long offline stretch, and nothing about it is visible to a tester — drop to minor / not tester-visible.
confirmed.judgeNote: Framing understates it — verified at DailyRoomBatchQueue.swift:68-101: the queue also persists across launches (loadFromDisk) and writes the whole file TWICE per failed tick (once after removeAll, once after re-insert). With client.patina.cloud/api/interactions/batch still on the program's OWED deploy list, the failure condition is TRUE today, so every tester's queue grows monotonically for the entire beta week with a growing atomic rewrite every 30s. 'The beta build eats my battery' poisons a whole round; the cap-and-backoff is S. T0, independent of whether the endpoint ships.

confirmed.title: Launch resume fans out up to 10 unstructured upload tasks (20 concurrent artifact uploads); the in-flight guard its own comment relies on does not exist
confirmed.evidence: The doc comment says 'duplicate launches for the same scanId are bounced by the task-in-flight guard'. `grep -rn "inFlight|activeUploads|uploadTasks" Services/Sync/` returns nothing — no such guard exists. resumePendingUploads launches one detached Task per package (fetchLimit 10), each running an artifact group with maxInFlight 2. Three independent triggers call it: PatinaApp.swift:148, and ScanSyncQueue.onBecameOnline / onBecameUnmetered (RoomScanSyncService.swift:58-68).
confirmed.fix: Add the Set<UUID> in-flight guard the comment promises and serialise the resume loop.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed including the strongest claim. `grep -rn 'inFlight|activeUploads|uploadTasks|activeScanIds' Services/Sync/` returns nothing — the guard the doc comment at :335-341 relies on genuinely does not exist. resumePendingUploads (:343-403) fetches with fetchLimit 10 and launches one unstructured `Task { [weak self] in ... }` per package (:392-402), each running an artifact group with maxInFlight 2 (:466), so 20 concurrent artifact uploads is right. Three triggers confirmed, with one location correction: PatinaApp.swift:148, plus RoomScanSyncService.swift:79 and :85 — the finding cites :58-68, but the onBecameOnline / onBecameUnmetered closures actually sit at :77-86.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified — `grep -rn 'inFlight|activeUploads|uploadTasks' Services/Sync/` returns nothing, so the guard the doc comment at :334-340 relies on genuinely does not exist (the `inflight[task]` map in BackgroundScanUploader is the URLSession task table, not a scanId guard). Adjusting the framing, not the severity: the ten-bundle stampede needs ten pending packages, which a first-round tester will never have. The realistic bite with ONE pending scan is that PatinaApp.swift:148 and ScanSyncQueue.onBecameOnline can both resume the same bundle, so the tester's scan uploads twice — duplicated cellular data and doubled token churn feeding C7-15. S effort (add the Set<UUID> the comment promises, serialise the loop). T1.

confirmed.title: A forced GoTrue token refresh runs before every single artifact upload
confirmed.evidence: `try? await SupabaseClientManager.shared.client.auth.refreshSession()` runs per artifact, and a bundle has many (manifest, USDZ, world map, meshes, depth, photos). GoTrue rotates refresh tokens and rate-limits /token; combined with C7-14's parallel bundles this is a credible route to a 429 or a rotated-token mismatch and a mid-upload sign-out. The build log also flags the line: `warning: result of 'try?' is unused` (:154).
confirmed.fix: Read auth.session (which refreshes only when expired) once per bundle rather than calling refreshSession() per artifact.
confirmed.codeNote: The code fact is confirmed: BackgroundScanUploader.upload(_:) calls `try? await SupabaseClientManager.shared.client.auth.refreshSession()` before building every single artifact request (the refresh is at :154, inside the per-artifact entry point at :147-162), and a bundle carries many artifacts. The consequence is not. The finding's own confidence is 0.6 and nothing in this audit demonstrates a 429 or a rotated-token mismatch; the call is `try?` with a documented, working fallback (the comment at :148-153 explains that a signed-out user falls through to buildRequest throwing .missingSession, which is recorded as the artifact's lastError rather than swallowed). Downgrading major -> minor and testerVisible -> false: this is an efficiency/robustness cleanup with a one-line fix, not a demonstrated sign-out. Keep the fix (read auth.session once per bundle); drop the mid-upload sign-out narrative.
confirmed.judgeNote: Verified at BackgroundScanUploader.swift:146-156 — `try? await ...auth.refreshSession()` runs per artifact, and a bundle carries manifest + USDZ + world map + meshes + depth + photos. GoTrue rotates refresh tokens and rate-limits /token; stacked with C7-14's parallel resume this is a credible route to a 429 or a rotated-token mismatch, and the failure mode is the worst one available: the tester gets signed out in the middle of uploading the room they just spent 90 seconds walking. Confidence is only 0.6 that it fires, but the fix is one line (read auth.session once per bundle, which refreshes only when expired) and the compiler is already flagging the line ('result of try? is unused'). Cheap insurance on the highest-stakes path — T0 on cost/benefit, not on likelihood.

confirmed.title: 236 unique compiler warnings in the app target, 112 of them 'error in the Swift 6 language mode'
confirmed.evidence: 236 unique file:line:col warnings, all in the app target (the log builds no test target); 112 carry 'this is an error in the Swift 6 language mode'; 28 are deprecations. Top emitters: 73 main-actor member from nonisolated context, 49 main-actor-isolated conformance used nonisolated (BuyabilityGate.Refusal, ScanManifest.Session/PoseGraphSummary, Product: Decodable), 28 'async but not marked with await', 26 'usdzData is deprecated', 21 supabase 'database is deprecated'. Individually real: RecommendationsView.swift:160 non-Sendable ModelContext exiting the main actor; captured-var-in-concurrent-code at QRApprovalViewModel:83, KeyframeTelemetryRecorder:132, RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle:577; AppCoordinator:14 'conformance crosses into main actor-isolated code and can cause data races'; PushTokenService:207 losing MainActor. Dead code the compiler caught: ARPlacementView:58,166 unused captureScreenshot(); AuthService:669 unused currentSession; MessagingViewModel:193 and ThreadDetailView:256 'no calls to throwing functions occur within try'. Build hygiene: '.swiftlint.yml couldn't be opened … falling back to default configuration' and the SwiftLint phase runs every build.
confirmed.fix: Triage the 112 Swift-6 errors before the language-mode bump; fix the five real concurrency ones now; restore .swiftlint.yml readability so the project's own rules apply.
confirmed.codeNote: Reproduced from .build/xcodebuild.log by deduping on file:line:col: 236 unique warnings, of which exactly 112 carry 'this is an error in the Swift 6 language mode' — both headline numbers exact. All ten named individual warnings exist verbatim in the log: RecommendationsView.swift:160:70 non-Sendable ModelContext exiting main actor; AppCoordinator.swift:14:36 'conformance of AppCoordinator to Coordinator crosses into main actor-isolated code and can cause data races'; PushTokenService.swift:207:62 losing global actor MainActor; captured-var-in-concurrent-code at QRApprovalViewModel:83, KeyframeTelemetryRecorder:132, RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle:577 ('done'); ARPlacementView:58/166 unused captureScreenshot(); AuthService:669 unused currentSession; MessagingViewModel:193 and ThreadDetailView:256 try-without-throwing. The '.swiftlint.yml couldn't be opened … Falling back to default configuration' warning is real (xcodebuild.log:12581) and I found its root cause, which strengthens the entry: ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES (pbxproj:585,649) plus a script phase declaring no inputPaths means the in-build lint cannot read the config at all, so the project's own severity:error custom rules are never loaded, not merely un-enforced. Two nits, neither material: deprecations dedupe to 32, not 28; and the bucket counts (73/49/28/26/21) are raw log occurrences, not deduped, so they sit on a different denominator from the 236 headline. The five named concurrency hazards deserve T1 treatment even if the 112-warning triage is T2.
confirmed.judgeNote: The warning-wall half is the same condition as G-09, measured differently (236 unique file:line:col in the app target alone vs 1604 warning lines / 169 distinct texts across app+test build) — fold that half into G-09 at T2. Severity adjusted major->minor for the wall: 1523 tests and every sim walk in this audit passed, so nothing here is a manifest defect. But C7-16 carries a payload G-09 does not, and it should be carved out as its own T1 item rather than dropped in the merge: six named concrete concurrency sites — RecommendationsView.swift:160 (non-Sendable ModelContext exiting the main actor; SwiftData off-main is the one on this list most likely to corrupt or crash), QRApprovalViewModel:83, KeyframeTelemetryRecorder:132 and RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle:577 (captured var in concurrent code), AppCoordinator:14 ('conformance crosses into main actor-isolated code and can cause data races'), PushTokenService:207 (losing MainActor). Those are latent, but if one fires on a tester's phone it is a crash — i.e. that subset IS tester-visible even though the finding as filed is not. Six sites, hand-fixable, worth doing in the first week rather than waiting for a language-mode migration. The dead code it caught (ARPlacementView:58,166 unused captureScreenshot(); AuthService:669; two try-without-throwing at MessagingViewModel:193 / ThreadDetailView:256) rides along free. The '.swiftlint.yml couldn't be opened' observation belongs to G-04, where I have folded it.

confirmed.title: The U39 all-or-nothing decode still stands on the saved-pieces and single-piece reads
confirmed.evidence: decodeProducts (:100-112) is the U39 fix (`[FailableDecodable<Product>]`) but has exactly one caller, fetchRecommendations. The Record's saved-pieces read does `try JSONDecoder().decode([RawProductWithVendor].self, from: data).map { $0.toProduct() }` — one malformed products row throws and takes every saved piece with it. fetchProduct(id:) has the same shape. Product.init(from:) is properly lenient; RawProductWithVendor is not.
confirmed.fix: Wrap both in FailableDecodable exactly as decodeProducts already does.
confirmed.codeNote: no V1 verdict
confirmed.judgeNote: Raised from minor on failure mode, not on likelihood: one malformed products row makes the ENTIRE saved list throw, and the tester reads that as their saved pieces being gone — the same catastrophic-looking failure as A1-04, arrived at from the other side. Decisive context: Kody will be seeding and editing the production catalogue during the beta week (see A3-21/A3-22), so a bad row mid-week is a live risk, not a theoretical one. The fix already exists eight lines above the defect (FailableDecodable, decodeProducts:100-112). First candidate to slide to T1 if the T0 list has to shrink.

confirmed.title: The .launching phase has no watchdog — if the auth stream never emits, the splash plays forever
confirmed.evidence: derivePhase returns .launching while !isAuthStateReady, and isAuthStateReady is set only from inside the `for await` over supabase.auth.authStateChanges. scheduleSplashDeadlineRecompute fires exactly once, at the 1.5 s deadline. A cancelled listener task, an SDK throw before the first emission, or a keychain failure leaves the app on the splash with no timeout, no error and no retry. emitLocalSessionAsInitialSession makes this unlikely, not impossible.
confirmed.fix: After N seconds without readiness, fall through to .auth with a 'couldn't reach your account' affordance.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed by full call-graph check. AuthService.isAuthStateReady (:49) is `private(set)` and written in exactly one place, markAuthStateReady() (:116-125), which is called from exactly one place — inside the `for await (event, session) in supabase.auth.authStateChanges` loop in startAuthStateListener (:127-135). waitForAuthReady (:217-223) only parks continuations; it cannot set the flag. derivePhase (AppCoordinator.swift:255-258) returns .launching whenever !isAuthStateReady, with no elapsed-time escape, and scheduleSplashDeadlineRecompute (:152-165) merely wakes the observer — it never forces a phase. So a cancelled listener task, an SDK throw before the first emission, or a keychain failure does leave the app on the splash forever with no timeout, no error and no retry. Likelihood is genuinely low (emitLocalSessionAsInitialSession normally guarantees an emission), which is why minor + confidence 0.5 is the honest rating; the consequence is unbounded, and a watchdog is an S fix.
confirmed.judgeNote: Keeping severity at minor rather than raising it, because the probability is genuinely low (emitLocalSessionAsInitialSession covers the ordinary paths) and the finding is code-read at 0.5 confidence with no reproduction — but flagging it as the worst tail in first-run: if it ever fires, the tester's entire experience of Patina is a splash screen that never ends, and the bug report Kody gets is 'it doesn't open', which is unactionable. That asymmetry, plus first-round testers being on real cellular against production, is why it earns T1 rather than T2 despite the low odds. Caution for the fix: a naive timeout that falls through to .auth while a valid session is still loading would flash a sign-in screen at already-signed-in testers — a worse, more frequent defect than the one being fixed. Gate the fallthrough on a genuinely long deadline and keep a retry affordance. T1.

confirmed.title: Cold-launch request fan-out: roughly a dozen PostgREST round trips before Today settles
confirmed.evidence: Today's appearance fires in parallel: viewModel.load() (story + feed), notificationsViewModel.load(), badges.refresh() ('six PostgREST reads' per its own doc), requestStatus.refresh(), refreshProjectRooms(), refreshRecord(), mirrorLastSeenIfNeeded(), refreshNewThisWeek(), RoomSyncCoordinator.reconcile(), plus the scan-recovery disk pass. The root's scenePhase hook adds RecordForeground.onForeground(), processQueueIfOnline() and PushTokenService.reregisterIfAuthorized(). The coalescing is good, so this is not a correctness bug — on a weak connection it is a dozen spinners resolving at a dozen moments.
confirmed.fix: Sequence the non-urgent reads behind the record paint; consider one composed read for the badge counts.
confirmed.codeNote: The inventory is code-true — six `.task` blocks at DailyRoomView.swift:101-135 (load, notifications, the badges→requests→rooms→record→mirrorLastSeen chain, newThisWeek, RoomSyncCoordinator.reconcile, ScanRecoveryService), badges.refresh is six concurrent PostgREST reads (BadgeCountService.swift:194-203), and PatinaApp.swift:150-176 adds RecordForeground.onForeground / processQueueIfOnline / reregisterIfAuthorized on .active. But the tester-facing claim is contradicted by this audit's own measurement: R.md step 2 records 'Today is fully drawn by ~1.5–3 s and stable from 3 s on. Cold launch is fast even with every request hanging' — with the backend fully paused. No lane observed a spinner storm or a slow settle. This is an architecture note, not a round-one defect; testerVisible false.
confirmed.judgeNote: Down from minor. The finding's own evidence concedes the coalescing is correct and this is not a correctness bug, and no cold-launch timing was measured — so the tester-visible symptom is staggered paint on a weak connection, not a slow app. That matters to the brief's 'fast cold launch' bar, but it is a tuning exercise with real regression risk across six .task blocks and a scenePhase handler, which is precisely the wrong shape of change to make in a hurry before build 1. Measure first on build 1 telemetry, then decide. T2.

confirmed.title: Remote images decode at full resolution with no downsampling and no configured URLCache
confirmed.where: apps/mobile/PatinaDesignKit/Sources/PatinaDesignKit/Components/PatinaAsyncImage.swift:28-56; used by 13 files incl. RecommendationsView.swift:369 and ProductCard.swift:176
confirmed.evidence: AsyncImage(url:) decodes at source resolution and leans entirely on the default URLCache.shared — grep for URLCache, NSCache or ImageCache across the app returns nothing. A grid of full-size catalogue photos on a 402 pt screen holds far more decoded bitmap than it needs, and evicted images re-download on scroll-back.
confirmed.fix: Configure a shared URLCache at launch and downsample with ImageIO (kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize) to the card size.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED. PatinaAsyncImage.swift:28-56 is a bare `AsyncImage(url:)` with a phase switch — no downsampling, no ImageIO thumbnail path, source-resolution decode. And `grep -rn 'URLCache|NSCache|ImageCache'` across apps/mobile/Patina and apps/mobile/PatinaDesignKit returns ZERO hits, so there is no configured cache of any kind and the component leans entirely on the process default URLCache.shared. Both halves of the claim hold as written.
confirmed.judgeNote: Right severity: on an iPhone 17 Pro the memory headroom hides the decode cost, so what a tester actually notices is re-downloading catalogue photos on scroll-back over cellular. Worth splitting the fix — configuring a shared URLCache at launch is nearly free and could ride with build 1; the ImageIO downsampling across 13 call sites is the M half and belongs in build 2.

confirmed.title: The app's only two print( call sites, in the scan instrument path
confirmed.evidence: `print(line)` and `print(instrumentLine)`, both inside #if DEBUG with a comment explaining that devicectl --console captures only stdout. They never ship; recorded because they are the only two print( sites in the app and a reader will trip over them.
confirmed.fix: None required. Leave as-is or route through a DEBUG-only logger helper.
confirmed.codeNote: Accurate and self-cancelling. RoomCaptureService+Instrument.swift:116 and :123 are the two print( sites, both inside a `#if DEBUG` block that also logs the same strings through PatinaLog.scan.info, with a comment explaining that devicectl --console only captures stdout. They cannot ship in a Release TestFlight build. The finding's own fix says 'None required'. Recording the verdict so the fix program can drop the row rather than re-derive it.
confirmed.judgeNote: Not a defect. Both print( calls are inside #if DEBUG with a comment explaining why (devicectl --console captures stdout only), so they cannot ship in the TestFlight Release build, and the finder says 'None required'. Recording it was right — a reader will trip over the only two print sites in a 435-file app — but it should carry no work in the fix program. Cut, and keep the ledger entry as documentation.

confirmed.title: DateFormatter constructed per list row and per body evaluation
confirmed.evidence: SavedRowMeta.formatter(_:) builds a fresh DateFormatter inside line(savedAt:roomName:), which is called once per saved row; DailyRoomViewModel.greetingDate is a computed property read from body that allocates one every render. ISO8601DateFormatter() is also allocated per PostHog event (PostHogService.swift:116) and per call in NotificationsAPIClient:88,110,131 and MessagingAPIClient:290.
confirmed.fix: static let cached formatters — the codebase already does this correctly elsewhere.
confirmed.codeNote: CONFIRMED at all three primary sites. SavedRowMeta.swift:20-26 builds a fresh DateFormatter inside `formatter(_:)`, which line(savedAt:roomName:) calls at :35 — once per saved row. DateDisplay.swift:25-31 allocates a parser DateFormatter per fromDateString call. DailyRoomViewModel.swift:114-118 `var greetingDate: String` is a computed property that allocates a DateFormatter on every read from body. DateFormatter allocation is the expensive part of DateFormatter, and the codebase already caches correctly elsewhere, so the `static let` fix is right-sized.
confirmed.judgeNote: Genuine and mechanical, but invisible at round-1 data volumes — a handful of saved rows and one greeting per render will not drop a frame. Do it when a list gets long enough to hitch; zero risk, zero urgency.

confirmed.title: isSyncing is cleared by the first of up to ten concurrent bundle uploads
confirmed.evidence: `isSyncing = true; lastError = nil; defer { isSyncing = false }` on a @MainActor @Observable singleton, with up to ten concurrent callers per C7-14. The first bundle to finish tells the UI syncing is done while nine are still uploading.
confirmed.fix: Use a counter, or derive the flag from the RoomScanPackage rows.
confirmed.codeNote: Confirmed with a small location fix and a bounded blast radius. The pattern is at RoomScanSyncService+AdvancedBundle.swift:78-80 (finding says :77-79): `isSyncing = true; lastError = nil; defer { isSyncing = false }` on the @MainActor @Observable singleton, and C7-14 establishes up to ten concurrent callers, so the first bundle to finish does clear the flag for all of them. Bounding the harm: the only consumer is YourSpacesView.swift:242's 'Uploading…' pill, so the visible symptom is that pill disappearing early — real, small, and the counter fix is trivial. Minor is right.
confirmed.judgeNote: Confirmed as written but downstream of C7-14: `defer { isSyncing = false }` on a @MainActor @Observable singleton only misreports while several bundles run concurrently, which is precisely what the missing in-flight guard allows. Serialising the resume loop makes this mostly moot; the counter is still the correct shape. Keep it on the list so the C7-14 fixer takes both, but it does not earn its own slot in build 1 or 2.

confirmed.title: Force-unwrapped string-interpolated URL with an interpolated piece id, plus a request built and never sent
