The AASA half the finding already closed stands. The only residue is that the App Group's group identifier membership is not listable through the ASC API — no evidence of a problem, and the A2-07 archive would surface it. This RESUME OWED row should be struck, not scheduled.

refuted.title: Product images contradict their titles
refuted.note: Prod does not carry these rows — the check the finding itself asked for comes back negative. Read-only on Strata, public.products is 15 rows / 8 published and is entirely a DWR + Herman Miller scrape ('Corbel Storage Bed', 'Otto Dining Table', 'F24 Storage Bench', 'PH5 Pendant Lamp', 'Line Credenza, Large' ×2 …) with vendor-CDN imagery from images.hermanmiller.group. 'Live-Edge Coffee Table', 'Terracotta Planter Set', 'Brass Arc Floor Lamp' and 'Velvet Club Chair' exist only in supabase/seed/products.sql, where the images are hand-picked Unsplash ids (live-edge-coffee-table → photo-1506439773649, which is the chair on grass). The mismatch is real in that fixture and the shot is honest, but it is a local dev-seed fault that no TestFlight tester against Strata will see. Worth a cheap seed-file fix so future local walks stop manufacturing this, but not a release item.

refuted.title: The share sheet carries no piece metadata; its preview read "Piece not found"
refuted.note: The premise about how the preview is produced is wrong, and the shot proves it. ShareLink given a URL item lets iOS fetch LPLinkMetadata FROM the destination — which is exactly why the sheet read 'Piece not found / client.patina.cloud': apps/client-portal/src/app/piece/[id]/page.tsx:53-61 returns literally `{ title: "Piece not found" }` when the id does not load, and the shared id was a local-seed uuid absent from Strata. For a real piece the same route returns pieceMetadata (piece-content.ts:119-137) with openGraph title '<name> by <maker>', a description and images:[imageUrl] — so a valid link DOES preview the piece, contradicting 'even a valid link will never preview the piece'. The app could not have produced the string 'Piece not found' itself; its presence is proof the remote-metadata fetch works. Residual and genuine but polish-grade: with no locally supplied UIActivityItemSource/LPLinkMetadata the preview needs a network round-trip and shows the generic compass until it lands, and stays generic offline.

refuted.title: The product hero scrolls under the status bar with no scrim; the clock becomes unreadable
refuted.note: The cited shot disproves the claim. I read shots/A/19-product-detail-scrolled.png and a 2× crop of its top 190 px: '9:41' renders in WHITE over the dark wardrobe — high contrast, fully legible — and the cellular/wifi glyphs render dark over the LIGHT wall and framed artwork on the right, not over the wardrobe. Nothing in that status bar is unreadable, so 'renders in dark ink directly over the near-black wardrobe' and 'the clock becomes unreadable' are both mis-reads. The structural half is true — at rest the hero is inset below the status bar (shots/A/18, shots/B/67) and on scroll it passes under it with no scrim — so an un-scrimmed hero stays a latent risk on a differently-lit photograph, but that is a hypothesis this evidence does not support.

refuted.title: Machine-composed strings use " - " where the rest of the app uses an em dash
refuted.note: Not app copy. The app's formatter is HouseRecord.swift:413 — `\(item.designerIsPerson ? firstName(of: name) : name) asked about \(item.title).` — and the punctuation lives entirely in `item.title`, a designer-authored decision row. Proof the strings are seed data, not app strings: 'Dining chairs - Shaker Oak vs Windsor Elm', 'Rug color - Natural vs Sand' and the em-dashed 'Design Development sign-off — drawing set B' all appear verbatim as decision titles in an unrelated designer-portal probe dump (artifacts/document-wayfinding-directions-2026-08-25/probe/text-dump-w1280.json) — the same seed set, some rows typed with a hyphen and some with an em dash. The sketched fix (compose with an em dash in the formatter) would have the iOS app rewrite designer-authored text, and a real tester sees whatever their own designer typed. At most this is a seed-data tidy for the demo project.

refuted.title: All-caps letterspaced MONOSPACE is the app's chrome typeface
refuted.note: REFUTED as a defect. The finding's own evidence is that all-caps letterspaced DM Mono is applied CONSISTENTLY across 12+ screens for one job — eyebrows, metadata, state labels — which is the visual system working, not failing. Source confirms one owner: PatinaTypography.monoLabel/monoSmall (DMMono-Regular, relativeTo:.caption2) and the MonoLabel component with 73 call sites, the second-most-adopted component in the kit. No inconsistency is demonstrated. The finding's own fix begins 'Decide deliberately' — that is a direction ruling for Kody, not a polish item, and Kody has already ruled once against typography churn (feedback_desk_studio_block_typography_locked). Route as a question, not a backlog row.

refuted.title: No Sign Out anywhere in Settings; it is buried in Account directly above 'Delete account'
refuted.note: Refuted by code and by the audit's own shots. SettingsView.swift:77-94 puts BOTH a 'Sign Out' row (accessibilityIdentifier SettingsView.SignOutButton) and a 'Delete account' row inside `if authService.isAuthenticated`, in the Account group. shots/A/54-settings.png (signed in) shows Account / Sign in on the web / Sign Out / Delete account. The lane's evidence, shots/B/58-settings-signedin-bottom.png, is the SCROLLED-TO-BOTTOM sheet (Haptic → Terms) — the Sign Out row is off-screen above it; the lane compared that to shots/B/21-guest-settings.png, which is the TOP of the guest sheet (correctly showing only Account + Sign in on the web, per the :77 guard). The headline and the fix ('Add a Sign Out row to Settings') are both already done on main; git blame: 6f9039e2a 'feat(ios): SP-20 — Sign Out in Settings and an account-deletion path'. Salvageable residue only: on AccountView (:184-195) 'Delete account' does sit directly under the Sign Out pill with no separating footer section — that is a distinct, minor Account-screen point, and the Settings-side version of it is C-24.

refuted.title: The direct-orders Buy path is unreachable — the designer pre-emption fires on a merely 'matched' designer
refuted.note: The premise is wrong and the proposed fix would break a documented ruling. `supabase/seed/leads_room_scans.sql:147-152` seeds james.okafor (h4) with an **accepted** lead ('accepted', and :172 sets `accepted_at`). `DesignerRelationship.isLive` (Core/State/DesignerRelationship.swift:30-35) is true for `.lead` and `.project`, false for `.none`/`.roster`; `PieceActResolver.act` (Features/Purchase/PieceAct.swift:156-158) pre-empts on `relationship.isLive` before the flag or the gate. So 'Ask Leah to source this' for james.okafor is the specified behaviour, not a bug — the account is NOT 'matched with no live designer'. The suggested fix ('gate on an ACTIVE roster relationship, not a match/lead ceremony') is the exact hazard PieceAct.swift:9-16 and DesignerRelationship.swift:70-77 were written to prevent (`.roster` is deliberately not live; resolving `.none` too early already shipped a wrong Buy once). What survives is a COVERAGE GAP, not a defect: neither seeded local account can reach Path A, so the audit could not exercise it — worth a seeded no-designer account for future walks. On production the path is closed anyway (A3-13/A3-20).

refuted.title: 'Member since' shows today's date for every account
refuted.note: Environment artifact, not an app defect. AccountView.swift:242-247 reads `authService.currentUser?.createdAt` — that IS auth.users.created_at, so the fix sketch ('read the account's created_at rather than the profile row's touched timestamp') describes code that already exists. The date is Sep 1 because supabase/seed/dev-accounts.sql:20 declares `ts TIMESTAMPTZ := NOW()` and inserts it into auth.users.created_at (:29,:55) — every seeded account's creation date is the local `supabase db reset` time, which was the walk day. The Aug-28 activity the lane cites is separately-seeded content with backdated timestamps. On a TestFlight build against Strata a tester sees their real signup date. Not reproducible off the local seed.

refuted.title: The Send button is correctly disabled but renders as a fully enabled solid control
refuted.note: The claim "no dimming — indistinguishable from its active state" is false on both code and pixels. ThreadDetailView.swift:280 already does exactly the proposed fix: `.foregroundStyle(canSend ? PatinaColors.Text.interactive : PatinaColors.Text.muted.opacity(0.6))`. I sampled the fill in shots/C/26-dark-messages.png at (1075,2400)/(1100,2440): #7A6E5C — the exact composite of DarkPalette.textMuted #B5A487 at 0.6 over background #211E1B. The enabled state is clay #C4A57B (DarkPalette.textInteractive), a clearly brighter, higher-chroma tan. The walker only ever saw the disabled state (no typed-text comparison shot exists in shots/C/), so "indistinguishable from active" was inferred, not observed. Nothing to fix.

refuted.title: The money-moment push is written to notification_log and never sent — the primer's promise is never kept
refuted.note: Mis-read of the migration: the finder cited 00534:190-192 (the push-row INSERT) and stopped before the dispatch. notify_client_attention dispatches apns-send ITSELF, immediately after that insert — supabase/migrations/00534_client_attention_notifications.sql:195-213: 'BEGIN PERFORM public.invoke_edge_function(''apns-send'', jsonb_build_object(''user_id'', p_user_id, ''title'', p_title, … ''notification_log_id'', v_push)); EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RAISE WARNING …'. apns-send then stamps the same row 'delivered' or 'failed' (supabase/functions/apns-send/index.ts:216-238). So the callers correctly do NOT invoke apns-send — by design, the RPC is the one dispatcher, which is also why client-attention.ts only mentions it in comments and why no cron drainer exists. (Unrelated and still open per research/A3-prod.md:203-206: APNS_AUTH_KEY/KEY_ID/TEAM_ID/TOPIC presence on Strata is UNVERIFIED — that is a config question, not this finding.)

refuted.title: Sign Out offline appears to work and doesn't
refuted.note: The mechanism it hinges on does not hold in supabase-swift 2.40. Read the pinned checkout (DerivedData/Patina-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/supabase-swift, Sources/Auth/AuthClient.swift:964-990): for the default `.global` scope, signOut does `await sessionManager.remove()` and `eventEmitter.emit(.signedOut, session: nil)` at :971-972 — BEFORE the POST to /logout at :976. So a transport throw (offline) happens with the local session already gone and .signedOut already emitted. AuthService subscribes to that stream (AuthService.swift:129 `for await (event, session) in supabase.auth.authStateChanges` → :135 applySession(session)), so AuthService.session is cleared even though the skipped applySession(nil) at :492 never runs, and derivePhase (AppCoordinator.swift:258-270) returns .auth. The tester is signed out. The lane's own 0.55 confidence and PLAUSIBLE label were right to hedge. Residue worth one line elsewhere, not here: the catch sets errorMessage to a raw SDK/URLError string (:494) which the auth screen then renders — a raw-error-string copy finding, not a sign-out-correctness one.

refuted.title: Tapping a designer thread that resolves to nil is a dead tap
refuted.note: Mis-read, and the scenario is unreachable. `DesignerThreadOpener.openThread` (DesignerThreadOpener.swift:60-68) returns nil for exactly one reason — the relationship is `.none` or `.roster` — never from the RPC. Both cited call sites resolve the relationship, guard `relationship.isLive` (false only for .none/.roster, DesignerRelationship.swift:30-35), and then pass THAT SAME value into openThread: ThreadListView.swift:211-215 and NotificationFeedView.swift:151-156. So the nil branch is unreachable defensive code, not a dead tap. The claimed "RPC succeeds and returns no id — a plausible RLS outcome" cannot happen either: MessagingAPIClient.swift:269-272 does `guard let threadId = try? decoder.decode(String.self …), !threadId.isEmpty else { throw RoomsAPIError.emptyResponse }`, so a null/empty result lands in the catch, which already sets `openThreadFailed`. Nothing to fix.

refuted.title: Settings toggles ship with an empty VoiceOver name
refuted.note: Mis-read: the lane stopped reading three lines short. SettingsView.swift:410-415 is `Toggle("", isOn: isOn).tint(...).labelsHidden()` FOLLOWED BY `.accessibilityLabel(label)` at :415, with the comment at :413-414 spelling out the exact defect the finding claims: 'R21: without this VoiceOver announces just "switch, on" — give the control the visible row label as its subject.' All three call sites (:109 Notifications, :118 Haptic Feedback, :127 Upload scans on cellular) pass `label`, so each toggle is named. Already fixed on main; no work here.

refuted.title: Tier pill on product cards is 10pt uppercase at 2.18:1
refuted.note: REFUTED as tester-visible: TierPill has ZERO production call sites. `grep -rn 'TierPill'` across the whole app returns only Design/Components/TierPill.swift itself — the struct at :10 and three references inside its own #Preview at :34-36. Nothing renders it, so no product card carries this pill and no tester ever sees 2.18:1. The colour math (offWhite on clay@0.85 at 10pt tracked uppercase) is correct as written, so if the component is ever adopted the defect is real — but for this audit it is dead code. Note this also corrects C3-11, which counts TierPill as having 3 call sites.

refuted.title: Splash wordmark is likely spelled out letter by letter
refuted.note: Refuted as a finding: nothing in the cited evidence supports it. No VoiceOver pass was run anywhere in this audit — the stated evidence is an assumption ("VoiceOver commonly spells short all-caps strings") plus a true-but-irrelevant fact (`.tracking(8)`, which affects glyph spacing and has no bearing on speech output). iOS speaks pronounceable all-caps words as words and reserves letter-by-letter reading for strings it classifies as acronyms; "PATINA" is a six-letter pronounceable word, so the predicted failure is unlikely, and the finding is self-hedged ("likely", confidence 0.6). The only verified part — SplashView.swift:25-30 sets no .accessibilityLabel — is not itself a defect, since the Text already exposes the correct string. This belongs on the coverage-gap list (one VoiceOver pass over the splash and one .textCase(.uppercase) MonoLabel, ~10 minutes) rather than the fix backlog; promote it only if that pass shows spelling.

refuted.title: Browse-card swipe-to-save/skip has no VoiceOver equivalent action
refuted.note: Already fixed on main; the reviewer read the gesture definition, not the card. The browse card DOES carry VoiceOver equivalents: RecommendationsView.swift:326-328 `.accessibilityAction(named: viewModel.isSaved(product) ? "Unsave" : "Save") { toggleSaved(product) }` and :329-331 `.accessibilityAction(named: "Skip") { viewModel.skipProduct(product) }`, carrying the comment 'PT-2-4: expose the swipe-to-save / swipe-to-skip gestures as VoiceOver actions, since the swipe itself is inaccessible.' The cited range :424-441 is `productCardSwipeGesture`, the DragGesture definition, roughly 100 lines below where the actions are attached in `productCard(_:)`. The note's parenthetical about DailyStoryDetailView and ScanWalkView is accurate and can be kept as a GOOD.

refuted.title: AddedToRoomToast — the save confirmation — is silent and reads its checkmark
refuted.note: AddedToRoomToast is dead code. `grep -rn 'AddedToRoomToast' --include='*.swift'` across all of apps/mobile returns matches ONLY inside Features/Home/Views/AddedToRoomToast.swift itself — the struct declaration at :8 and its own #Preview at :51-52. Zero production call sites in Patina, PatinaWidget, PatinaDesignKit or anywhere else. The accessibility observations about the source are individually accurate (no announcement on appear; Image(systemName:"checkmark") at :20 unhidden; no children:.combine), and one is slightly off — the View button DOES get an implicit label from its Text("View") child at :29 — but none of it can reach a tester because nothing renders it. Not a TestFlight-polish finding; at most a dead-code cleanup.

refuted.title: Order-line DTO requires four non-optional fields while every other money DTO is all-optional
refuted.note: The failure scenario cannot occur. `00350_fulfillment_core.sql:92-111` declares all four columns NOT NULL — `item_name text NOT NULL`, `qty integer NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0)`, `unit_price_cents integer NOT NULL`, `line_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'intake'` — so 'one null column blanks the whole order list' has no path. The non-optional Swift declarations are a CORRECT model of the schema; if anything the all-optional DTOs elsewhere are the anomaly, not this one. Compounding: the surface is unreachable on production anyway (no client SELECT policy — A3-14) and behind `direct-orders` in the app. At most a style note, not a defect.

refuted.title: Depth PNG encode plus file append at 1 Hz on the main actor during a scan
refuted.note: Mis-read: the finding read writeFrame but not its caller. DepthFrameRecorder.consume(frame:associatedPhotoId:) at :80-107 hops onto `ioQueue` — a DispatchQueue(label: "com.patina.depth-recorder.io", qos: .userInitiated) declared at :56 — via `ioQueue.async { ... self.writeFrame(...) }` at :95. So writeDepthPNG16, writeConfidencePNG8, the JSONEncoder pass and the FileHandle append all run OFF the main actor; only the sceneDepth guard, the sampleInterval throttle and a few property reads run inline in the AR frame Task. The central claim ('on the main actor') is the whole finding, so it does not survive. Worth handing to the fix program as a different, real defect: the comment at :88 says 'Clone pixel buffers (they're recycled by ARKit; retain content before dispatch)' but :89-90 only copies references to depth.depthMap / confidenceMap, so the io queue can read buffers ARKit has already recycled.

refuted.title: Unit gate costs 610 s of wall clock for 4.7 s of tests (600 s simctl diagnose timeout)
refuted.note: Environment fault, and not reproducible in the cited evidence — the brief's explicit refute class. The stall itself is real (G-unit.log:26896-26898: '1523 tests … passed after 4.733 seconds', then 'Failure collecting diagnostics from simulator: Timed out after 600.0 seconds', then '610.538 elapsed'). But the very next tier ran `xcodebuild test` against the SAME simulator clone (BD8D6AC8-BA6C-484B-B819-6E671FA72D8D) with the same -derivedDataPath four minutes later and finished in 146.631 s with no diagnostics timeout at all (G-ui.log:2 and :2238). One tier paid the tax, the next did not, on the same device in the same session — so this is a transient CoreSimulator diagnostics hang, not a property of ios-gate.sh, the test plan, or the project. The finder's own confidence is 0.55 and their fix begins 'Reproduce on a freshly erased clone first'. Nothing for the fix program to change; if it recurs it is a simulator-hygiene note, not a finding.

refuted.title: Patina/Generated/GitCommit.swift is tracked and rewritten by every Debug build
refuted.note: Already fixed on main — the recommended fix IS the current state. apps/mobile/Patina/Patina/Generated/GitCommit.swift is not tracked: `git ls-files apps/mobile/Patina/Patina/Generated/` returns nothing, `git log --all -- <that path>` returns no commits (it was never tracked), and `git check-ignore -v` resolves it to .gitignore:57, added by da9d8b79a 'chore(ios/build): stamp short git SHA into Debug builds'. The 'the file is dirty because the file is dirty' reasoning is also wrong: the Stamp Git SHA phase runs `git -C "$SRCROOT" diff --quiet`, which tests the whole worktree rather than this one file, and this worktree genuinely has ~10 other modified files — so the `+` in `d7287c3f+` reflects real repo dirt, not self-inflicted churn. The phase additionally short-circuits with `exit 0` when the generated content is unchanged, so it does not rewrite on every build. Nothing here for the fix program.

refuted.title: Cold launch shows a returning signed-in user the guest home plus the first-run coach tour
refuted.note: REFUTED on the exact mechanism the finding proposes. AppCoordinator.swift:258-266 derivePhase(): 'if !AuthService.shared.isAuthStateReady || splashStillPlaying { return .launching }' — the app holds the splash until the auth state resolves, so DailyRoomView cannot render 'while the session is still restoring'. AuthService.swift:49/118-119 shows isAuthStateReady is a one-way latch set only after restore completes. The guest composition is a settled state, not a race: TodayExperience.swift:295 appends .signInLine on !isSignedIn, which is reached only in .main, which requires either a session or guestModeOptIn. What shot 12 actually shows is the state the walker's OWN environment fault 3 predicts — 'xcrun simctl openurl <https universal link> cold-restarts the app WITHOUT -DeploymentTarget local, so the app comes up against Strata production, where client@patina.dev has no session'. That is a genuinely signed-out app on prod, correctly rendering the guest home, correctly offering a first-run tour for that context. The reporter's own 0.6 confidence and the 'process churn' caveat point the same way. Recommend cutting the finding; shot 12's real value is GAP1-14 (which stands).

refuted.title: DocumentListView's designed empty state is unreachable on the flags-off path
refuted.note: REFUTED — there is a third entry point the lane missed, and it is ungated. Companion/Services/CompanionAreaBuilders.swift:255-263: for screen == .projectDetail, projectItems always returns item("folder", "Documents", "Files for this project", route: .documentList, id: "documents") with no hasDocuments condition; it is reached via CompanionContextProvider.screenItems (:141-148) → studioItems (:237-238). So any tester who taps the Companion orb on a project detail — the orb is present in shots 44/45 — lands on DocumentListView with zero documents and sees exactly the PatinaEmptyState the finding says can never be displayed. The two gated entry points cited (StudioQueueBuilder.documentRecordRow:536-538 guard !documents.isEmpty, ProjectDetailView.swift:37 if viewModel.hasDocuments) are real but not exhaustive. Note the inversion: the actual finding here is that a Companion row promises 'Files for this project' and delivers an empty screen with a 'Get design help' CTA — but that is not what was claimed, so this entry should be cut and re-filed by whoever owns the Companion menu.

refuted.title: presentationDetents are ignored on iPad: sheets become fixed-height form sheets and phone-tuned content is clipped mid-glyph
refuted.note: PREMISE REFUTED BY GREP. There are exactly 20 .presentationDetents call sites in the app and NONE of them is on this sheet: the Sign In sheet is ContentView.swift:68-70 .sheet(isPresented:$showingPasswordSignIn){ AuthenticationView(initialMode:.signIn) } with no presentation modifiers at all. Detents are not 'ignored on iPad' — none were ever declared, so iOS presents the platform default, which on iPad is a form sheet. That is correct system behaviour, not a bug, and 'this is the probe's detent question answered' answers it backwards. The residual is thin: AuthenticationView.swift:22 already wraps the content in a ScrollView, so the clipped rows are ordinary scroll-view clipping at the card edge and iOS scroll indicators are transient by design. Nothing here for a fix lane; A2-03 moots the form-sheet geometry anyway.

refuted.title: A product card shows a flat grey rectangle where the image should be — no placeholder, no spinner, no failure state
refuted.note: REFUTED AS WRITTEN — the three-state treatment the fix asks for already exists, and what was photographed is the designed state. PatinaAsyncImage.swift ships a loading placeholder (Background.secondary + StrataMarkView at 0.35, :64-70) and a failure placeholder (StrataMark + 'Tap to retry', tap-to-retry wired, :72-88); RecommendationsView.swift:366-372 routes a nil imageURL to product.placeholderGradient, with the comment 'category gradient remains the deliberate no-URL fallback'. I read shots/GAP5/15b-runner-card.png: the 'flat grey' is a top-leading→bottom-trailing pale warm-grey ramp — that is PatinaGradients.linen (#D4CFC7→#E5E2DD, PatinaGradients.swift:39-42), the .decor fallback, rendering as intended. So 'no placeholder, no spinner, no failure state' is false. Residual (polish only): linen is too low-contrast to read as a deliberate placeholder. Also already reported by lane B (B.md:176, shot 34).

refuted.title: The Saved footer wraps into nonsense at accessibility sizes
refuted.note: No evidence exists for this. The AXXL pass captured shots 44-54 (Today, Companion, Your Spaces, room, budget ×2, browse, card menu, add-to-room, item menu ×2) — there is NO Saved-list capture at accessibility-extra-large, and shots/GAP6/ledger.md confirms it. The specific break quoted ('Saved Sep 1 / · Audit Room / B') is unverified in any artifact. Structurally it is plausible — CollectionsView.swift:234-257 is an `HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline)` with a wrapping Text and a `.frame(minHeight: 44)` button, which would strand 'Add a note' on the first baseline — but plausible is not observed. Refuted as written; re-capture the Saved list at AXXL to settle it.

critic.summary:
COMPLETENESS CRITIQUE (K) — Patina iOS TestFlight-polish audit, 435 findings across 19 lanes.

## 1. Screens with NO screenshot and NO finding

The A1 inventory holds 100 screens. Cross-referencing every ledger table in shots/{A,B,C,P,R}/ledger.md against every finding lane in research/*.md:

**45 of 100 screens were photographed.** 55 were never seen by anyone.

**7 screens are strictly zero-touch — no shot, and no lane's ledger even names the file:**
- #35 Add-to-Calendar (EventKit editor) — Features/DesignServices/AddToCalendarButton.swift
- #40 Decision consent + e-sign — DecisionDetailView.swift:368 (DecisionConsentSheet, private)
- #41 Defer a decision — Features/Decisions/Views/DecisionDeferSheet.swift
- #49 Invoice reminder primer — Features/Invoices/Views/InvoiceReminderPrimerView.swift
- #53 Document preview — Features/Documents/DocumentQuickLook.swift
- #92 Soft landing — Features/RoomScan/Views/SoftLandingView.swift
- #94 Style conversation (5 questions) — Features/StyleConversation/Views/StyleConversationContainerView.swift

Three more are effectively zero-touch: #34 Designer portfolio, #50 Stripe Checkout (invoice), #78 Stripe Checkout (direct order) — all three are Features/Invoices/Views/SafariView.swift, cited only by C9 (layout) and by P's finding about *system* Safari; the in-app SFSafariViewController cover itself was never opened or read.

**48 more screens have ≥1 static finding but zero pixels.** Grouped:
- Design services (8): #31 consultation (A1-14's hard-coded "Matched Designer" card has never been seen), #32 status, #33 match intro, #61 request flow, #62 scan picker, #63 sign-in wall, plus #34/#35.
- Decisions + projects + money detail (12): #36–#41, #51 Budget, #52 Documents, #53, #54 Ordered, #55 Order, #49.
- Purchase (4): #75 Ask your designer, #77 Order sheet, #78, #79 Order placed.
- Piece/room sheets (6): #18 All Items, #65 Move/copy, #74 Add to room, #81 Note on a saved piece, #82 Item actions, #83 Room budget.
- Browse/saved routes (2): #20 roomSavedItems, #22 roomEmergence.
- Onboarding branch (4): #94–#97 (conversation, contemplative pause, reveal, floor plan) + #6/#7 camera primer/privacy sheet.
- Scan/AR (10): #28 AR placement + #84–#92 LiDAR.
- Other (4): #42 thread list, #59 QR approval, #67 Story detail, #98–#100 widgets.

## 2. Modalities never run

Nothing in this audit is device-verified — the brief says so, but the consequence is under-stated in the lane notes. Specifically **not exercised in any mode**:
1. **LiDAR/RoomPlan capture** (#84–92) and **ARKit AR placement** (#28) — Simulator has no LiDAR; A1-15 documents it, nobody could close it.
2. **Real camera** — the QR viewfinder was photographed (B: 24-guest-signin-web) but never scanned a code; the walk-first camera primer (#6/#7) is behind PostHog flag `onboarding_walk_first` and was never forced on.
3. **Face ID / LocalAuthentication** — #59 QR approval; C4-10 is code-only.
4. **Push round trip** — no APNs token registered on a real device, no push delivered, no cold-launch-from-push, no badge. A3 could not read APNS_* edge env; aps-environment is `development` (A2-24/G-12/C9-20). All 14 notifications findings from C2 are code-read.
5. **Apple Pay / Stripe Checkout** — never opened in either direction. The local key is a placeholder and production is off-limits, so the app's entire money conversion path terminates at a failure banner in every walk.
6. **Widget on a Home Screen or Lock Screen** — lane B read the App-Group JSON only. No gallery, no rendered small widget, no accessory families, no timeline refresh, no widget tap.
7. **Universal links against real AASA association** — `simctl openurl` of an https URL does not exercise the association; only that path and `patina://` (A-105: does nothing) were tried.
8. **The Release binary at all** — G-01: Release does not compile, so every "in TestFlight this behaves differently" claim (A2-15 analytics kill-switch, A2-25 Debug-only diagnostics, C5-22/C5-28/C2-18 dead code shipping) is inference from `#if DEBUG` source shape. No archive exists; A2-01/02/03/19 and G-05/06/12 are unproven against a real IPA.
9. **A signed-in production session** — the advertised tester credential fails in-app (A3-16), Sign in with Apple is unusable on a Simulator, and account creation on prod is forbidden. Lane P got no further than the guest quiz gate.
10. **iPad** — TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY is 1,2, six iPad simulators with the iOS 26.5 runtime are installed, and the app was never launched on one. A2-03 is a *blocker* and C7-11 a major, both static.
11. **Offline** — R's "outage" was a Kong pause with full device network (R's own note). NWPathMonitor/reachability behaviour (C4-02) is untested.
12. **VoiceOver actually running** — lane C read the AX tree through blitz; no rotor, no focus order, no announcement was ever heard. Haptics, ProMotion scroll, thermals and memory are not observable in a Simulator.

## 3. Claims resting on a single unverified lane

- **All A3 production claims** (A3-01 zero recommendations, A3-17 hero-less stories, A3-21/22 category vocabulary and NULL published_at) are SQL/REST reads by one lane; nobody has seen a single production screen past the guest quiz. Meanwhile every signed-in visual finding (A-34 match scores, A-36/B-18/C-27 missing images, C5-16 UNKNOWN MAKER, A-81 four counts, C-11 three match scores, R-01 Studio composition) is measured on the **local seed**. The audit's picture of "what a tester sees" and its picture of "what production holds" have never been reconciled on one screen.
- **A2's TestFlight blockers** — one lane reading pbxproj + the ASC API. No archive, no `altool` validation.
- **C7's performance claims** (60 Hz ARFrame retention, per-frame CIContext, launch-time cost, unbounded telemetry queue) — one static lane, zero measurements. No Instruments, no signposts, no measured launch on an optimised build.
- **C2's push/widget/deep-link layer** — one static lane; corroborated only by B's read of the App-Group file.
- **C3's contrast maths** — computed from hex literals in one lane; partially corroborated by C's rendered measurements (C-20, C-01) and contradicted nowhere, but the 89-site `pearl` claim (C3-01) rests on grep alone.
- **A1's dead-code claims** (A1-05/07/08/09/10) — one lane, call-site greps only.
- **C1/C6 accessibility** — the VoiceOver phrasing claims (rotor actions, combined children, announcements) are inferred from modifiers; only lane C's tree dump partially corroborates.

## 4. Thin dimensions relative to app surface

- **Decisions** — 4 screens (list/detail/consent-e-sign/defer), 2 static findings, 0 shots, and 2 of the 4 files unmentioned anywhere. This is the client's core "act" surface: the "5 things need your eye" badge counts these.
- **Design services** — 8 screens on the app's only conversion funnel for a discovering tester, 8 findings total, 0 shots, and the one confirmed placeholder (A1-14) never seen.
- **Orders / purchase** — 5 screens, no ids of their own (only copy/token mentions in C3/C5/C6). Lane B was pre-empted for both seeded accounts by "Ask Leah to source this", so the direct-orders path has never been entered.
- **Messaging** — 6 findings, 2 screens; the thread list was never opened and a message was never sent, so C4-04 ("a failed send is completely silent") and C4-15 are unobserved.
- **Widget/deep-links** — 10 findings, zero rendered pixels, and an internal contradiction: B says the snapshot bridge works, A-105/C2-02/C2-21 say links do nothing.
- **Help/tour** — 8 findings, but the *fallback* path (the one a tester gets when Sanity is empty, per C5-02) was never walked with Sanity unreachable; only R-10 touched the failure surface.
- **Performance-resilience** — 17 findings, zero measurements.
- **Sheets/detents generally** — C9 predicts a keyboard trap (RoomBudgetSheet: `.numberPad`, `.medium`-only detent, no ScrollView, and C9-08 says the app has no keyboard-dismiss affordance anywhere). Confirmed in source at RoomProjectView.swift:132-137. If real, that is a blocker-class dead end and no one has tapped it.

## 5. What the audit does well (calibration)

First-run, auth, onboarding, Today, visual system, copy and accessibility are saturated — five lanes each, sim-verified and cross-corroborated. The gap is not breadth of *inspection*; it is that the audit walked the front half of the app on local seed data and read the back half.
unverifiedClaims: Nothing in the audit is device-verified. Every claim is compile-green or sim-verified at best, and the brief's own bar (an iPhone 17 Pro on iOS 26.5 against production) has never been met by any lane.

No production signed-in session exists anywhere in the audit. The advertised tester credential (tester@patina.cloud / 000000) fails in-app with HTTP 403 (A3-16, P step 3), Sign in with Apple is unusable on a Simulator, and account creation on production is forbidden — so every signed-in finding rests on local seed data while A3 proved production content is essentially empty.

The Release binary was never produced or run: G-01 shows `xcodebuild archive` fails with exit 65 on four `#Preview` blocks referencing DEBUG-gated fixtures, and `.build/Patina.xcarchive` was never created. All Release-only behaviour claims (A2-15 analytics kill-switch, A2-25 Debug-only Supabase diagnostics, C5-22/C5-28/C2-18 dead code shipping, flags-OFF-in-Release) are source inference.

No archive means no IPA-level proof for A2-01 (CFBundleVersion), A2-02/G-05 (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy / ITMS-91053), A2-03 (iPad multitasking validation), A2-19 (invalid profile), G-06 (encryption compliance) or G-12 (whether aps-environment flips to production on export). All six are pbxproj/ASC-API reads by a single lane.

Push has never round-tripped: no APNs token was registered from a signed build on a device, no notification was delivered, no cold-launch-from-push occurred, and A3 could not read APNS_AUTH_KEY / APNS_KEY_ID / APNS_TEAM_ID / APNS_TOPIC from edge-function env. All 26 C2 findings are code-read.

Stripe Checkout was never opened in either direction (invoice #50, direct order #78). The local key is a 32-char placeholder and production is off-limits, so the app's entire money conversion path terminates at a failure banner in every walk — and the direct-orders path was additionally pre-empted in lane B by 'Ask Leah to source this' for both seeded accounts.

The widget was never rendered. Lane B read the App-Group JSON (widget-snapshot.json / house-record.json) only; the Home Screen widget, the two Lock Screen accessory families, the gallery preview, timeline refresh and widget-tap deep links (#98-#100) are all unrendered.

Universal links were never exercised against real AASA association — only `xcrun simctl openurl`, which bypasses the association check. The custom scheme `patina://` was tried and A-105 reports it does nothing; the two claims have not been reconciled.
LiDAR/RoomPlan (#84-#92) and ARKit AR placement (#28) are unreachable on any Simulator, so C7-04, C7-05, C7-14, C7-15, C7-28, C4-08 and C4-11 have no runtime evidence at all.

The camera was never used: the QR viewfinder was photographed but never decoded a code, Face ID / LocalAuthentication (#59 QR approval) was never invoked, and the walk-first camera primer (#6/#7) behind PostHog flag `onboarding_walk_first` was never forced on.

Lane R's 'outage' was a Kong pause with full device network. True offline behaviour — whether the app has any reachability awareness at all (C4-02: one NWPathMonitor in the scan lane) — is unverified; no airplane-mode or Network Link Conditioner pass was run.

VoiceOver was never actually running. Lane C read the accessibility tree through blitz; no rotor navigation, focus order or spoken announcement was heard, so the phrasing claims in C6 (rotor custom actions, `.combine` output, announcements) and C1 remain inferred from modifiers.

No performance was measured. C7's 17 resilience/performance findings (per-frame CIContext, 60 Hz ARFrame retention in an escaping Task, synchronous launch work in PatinaApp.init, unbounded telemetry re-queue, full-resolution image decode) are code-shape claims — no Instruments trace, no signposts, no memory or thermal observation, and cold-launch timing is wall-clock on a Debug simulator build only.
iPad was never launched, despite TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1,2 and six iPad simulators being installed on the iOS 26.5 runtime. A2-03 (blocker) and C7-11 (major) are static.

C3's contrast figures are computed from declared hex literals, not measured on a render, except where lane C independently measured (C-01, C-20, C-27, C-41). The 89-site `pearl` claim (C3-01) rests on grep alone.
A1's dead-code and duplication claims (A1-05, A1-07, A1-08, A1-09, A1-10, A1-16) are single-lane call-site greps with no runtime confirmation.

Messaging was never used: the thread list (#42) was never opened, no message was sent, and no send failure was induced — so C4-04 ('a failed message send is completely silent'), C4-15 and C9-05 (composer under the Companion dock) are unobserved.

The predicted keyboard dead end has never been tapped: RoomProjectView.swift:132-137 presents RoomBudgetSheet at `.presentationDetents([.medium])` only, RoomBudgetSheet.swift:61 uses `.keyboardType(.numberPad)` with no ScrollView, and C9-08 claims the app has no keyboard-dismiss affordance anywhere. If those compose, it is a blocker; as reported it is two separate minors.
